items.abstract: <jats:p>Background and Objectives: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears may be associated with persistent deficits in lower limb neuromuscular control and alterations in gait stability that are not fully captured by linear walking assessments. Turning is a complex locomotor task that requires dynamic balance and coordination. This study aimed to investigate preoperative spatiotemporal gait characteristics during an 180° turning task using a wearable inertial measurement unit (IMU). Methods: Forty-nine adults (20 with ACL rupture and 29 healthy controls) performed the TURN test, which included forward, turning, and return gait phases. Spatiotemporal parameters were recorded using a wireless IMU (G-Walk, BTS Bioengineering). Results: Individuals with ACL rupture demonstrated significantly lower gait speed during forward walking and turning, reduced cadence during forward and return walking, and prolonged gait cycle duration across all three phases, with the largest between-group effect size observed for turning speed (p < 0.001, d = 1.48). No significant differences were observed in absolute or normalized stride length. Conclusions: The findings suggest that IMU-based assessment during a turning task may offer complementary insights into functional gait alterations in individuals with ACL rupture. Further research is required to establish its clinical utility.</jats:p>
title: Preoperative Turning Gait Alterations in Individuals with Anterior Cruciate Ligament Rupture: Insights from Inertial Measurement Unit Analysis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Tungsten is regarded as a primary candidate for plasma-face material for internals of ITER and, possibly, other thermonuclear installations. This article presents the investigation results of the effect of low-energy proton irradiation temperature on the degradation of the structure and properties of ITER-grade tungsten. High-purity tungsten (99.94 wt.%) was irradiated with 350 keV protons to a fluence of 5 × 1017 cm−2 at room temperature and at 773 K (UKP-2-1 accelerator, Institute of Nuclear Physics, Almaty), followed by isochronal annealing at 873–1273 K. Structure and properties were examined through X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and microhardness measurements. Irradiation at room temperature produced unruptured blisters, predominantly 10–20 μm in size; annealing at 873–1073 K reduced their total number while increasing the fraction of larger blisters (20–25 μm and above); and annealing at 1273 K fully dissolved the blisters without surface exfoliation, recovering microhardness to its initial level. Irradiation at 773 K caused blister appearance and burst during irradiation process; predominant blister size was 3–5 μm; subsequent annealing produced second-generation blisters at the sites of the primary ones. After annealing at 1273 K, only erosion spots and second-generation blisters were left on the surface; microhardness recovered also.</jats:p>
title: Effect of Proton Irradiation Temperature on the Surface Degradation of High-Purity Tungsten

items.abstract: <jats:p>Recently, multi-view clustering methods based on deep matrix factorization have exhibited significant promise in learning hierarchical semantic representations. However, three critical limitations remain in existing approaches. First, due to the independent intra-view hierarchical decomposition, these methods rely on pairwise view correlations, thereby failing to capture high-order consistency. Second, the complementary information embedded in intermediate layers remains under-utilized. Third, they are susceptible to sensor noise and feature redundancy, which degrades the quality of learned representations. To address these limitations, this paper presents a novel approach named Noise-Aware Hierarchical Tensor Fusion (NAHTF). The proposed NAHTF integrates tensor dictionary learning with deep semi-nonnegative tensor decomposition, leveraging the tensor t-product to facilitate cross-view and cross-layer information fusion of multi-view data. Specifically, a noise-aware tensor dictionary learning module is designed to construct a robust tensor representation by combining Schatten p-norm-based low-rank tensor recovery for capturing high-order correlations and l2,1-norm-based sparse noise modeling for suppressing adverse components. A deep semi-nonnegative tensor factorization module is then employed to hierarchically decompose the refined tensor representation using the tensor t-product, which facilitates the propagation of complementary information across all decomposition layers and thereby fully exploits both inter-view consistency and intra-view diversity. Moreover, a joint optimization framework is developed to simultaneously learn the tensor representation and perform deep tensor factorization, avoiding suboptimal representations caused by decoupled processes. Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets, including text, face, and image data, demonstrate that NAHTF outperforms fourteen state-of-the-art multi-view clustering methods.</jats:p>
title: Noise-Aware Hierarchical Tensor Fusion for Multi-View Clustering

items.abstract: <jats:p>Conventional industrial safety helmets primarily provide passive protection and lack the ability to continuously identify environmental and motion-related hazards. Halm is a multimodal edge-AI smart helmet prototype integrating vision, fall detection, location reporting, local warnings, and dashboard monitoring. Smart Vision uses YOLOv8 Small on a Raspberry Pi 5 to detect ground-level sharp tools, potholes or surface depressions, and safely handheld tools. The 6409-image dataset (11,697 annotated objects) was split by source image into training, validation, and test subsets (70/20/10), keeping augmented variants together. Across three runs (638–643 test images), precision was 91.5±1.7%, recall 87.7±3.5%, mAP@50 92.2±2.1%, and mAP@50–95 70.7±2.1% (mean ± SD). Source-disjoint pothole AP@50 was 33.9%, indicating limited cross-source generalization. Prototype tests showed detections and LED warnings; PyTorch inference averaged 1.446 s/frame. Smart Sense applies deterministic thresholds to total acceleration from the BNO085 inertial measurement unit (IMU). In 24 controlled trials using self-testing and human-shaped dummy fall simulations, sensitivity and specificity were both 91.67%. Across 15 communication trials, estimated post-detection edge-to-dashboard latency was 1.091±0.059 s, excluding visual inference. These results demonstrate controlled feasibility; independent construction site testing, larger participant studies, and ergonomic and embedded-performance evaluations remain necessary before deployment.</jats:p>
title: Halm: An Edge-Computing Smart Helmet for Ground Hazard Detection and Fall Alerting Using YOLOv8 and Inertial Sensing

These results underscore the need for policy coordination among countries to achieve EU decarbonization targets.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Case overview/synopsis</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Banas Dairy was Asia’s largest dairy cooperative. It transported liquid milk from its Palanpur plant, Gujarat to Faridabad plant, Delhi National Capital Region. For this transportation, Banas dairy used railway milk tankers (RMTs) and road transport. These modes inherently had some concerns. For example, in RMTs there were frequent delays, repetitive milk transfers and increased costs due to demurrage charged by Indian Railways (IR). Along with that, another grave issue was maintaining the quality of milk. In trucking mode, truck drivers had to undergo risks of pilferage, road accidents and police harassment. In 2021, the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) offered the ToT service on its Western Dedicated Corridor of India (The Economic Times, 2025a). Part A of this case was positioned around six months before the Banas Dairy actually adopted the ToT. That time, conundrum was whether Banas Dairy would change its transportation mode to the ToT. The conundrum faced by Banas Dairy would have to be resolved under the able guidance of Mr Sangram R. Chaudhary, managing director of Banas Dairy. The change was to be implemented in the immediate future to overcome the cons posed by the RMTs and road transport. Part B of this case, which was based on 2023–2026 and covered the period after the shift to ToT mode, showed another dilemma – how to optimize the return journey of the ToT. This case study detailed the operations of the DFCCIL and the salient features of the ToT. It highlighted logistics improvements, savings in fuel costs and the positive environmental effects of innovative logistics, especially in rail transport, in a developing economy such as India. This is a teaching note supplementing the “Neither truck nor train, rather truck on train: innovative freight fusion or patchwork?” case study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                    <jats:title>Complexity academic level</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This case study is designed for undergraduate or graduate-level programs in supply chain and logistics or strategy management, and senior management professionals in executive education programs undertaking courses in logistics management, supply chain operations and related cargo logistics.</jats:p>

<jats:p>
                    Exocytic and endocytic membrane fusion needs R, Qa, Qb, and Qc family SNARE proteins. SNARE domains have 16 layers, each with an apolar amino acid except for an arginine (R) or glutamine (Q) at the central 0-layer. In solution, SNAREs may spontaneously assemble into RQaQbQc complex, engaging all four SNAREs from their SNARE domain N-terminal -7 layers to C-terminal +8 layers, a process termed “zippering.” We confirm that SNARE assembly in detergent is interdependent among the four SNAREs and does not require the Qb-SNARE C-terminal layers, suggesting N to C 4-SNARE synchronous zippering. However,
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">in vivo</jats:italic>
                    SNARE assembly and fusion is catalyzed and regulated by proteins such as HOPS. HOPS tethers membranes, then catalyzes the assembly of their SNAREs in
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">trans</jats:italic>
                    for fusion. HOPS does not bind the N-terminus of all four SNAREs, but rather binds the R and Qa SNARE domains in a parallel orientation with their central 0-layer arginyl and glutaminyl residues directly apposed. Little is known of the subsequent order of engagement of Qb and Qc SNAREs and how their SNARE domains engage with HOPS-bound R and Qa. Using assays of reconstituted proteoliposome fusion and an
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">in situ</jats:italic>
                    assay of
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">trans</jats:italic>
                    association of SNAREs, we now report that the Qc SNARE engages reversibly with R and Qa, and Qb assembles last. Even after HOPS has assembled
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">trans</jats:italic>
                    -complexes with Qc and a mutant Qb lacking its C-terminal layers, the subsequent addition of Qb with a full SNARE domain reverses the block and restores fusion. Stable SNARE assembly requires the C-terminal layers of the Qb SNARE engaging the other SNAREs, completing the pre-fusion
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">trans</jats:italic>
                    -complex.
                  </jats:p>
title: SNAREs engage sequentially and reversibly for membrane fusion

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Plasma cathodes often exhibit a bi-modal current–voltage behavior whose physical origin remains unclear, where a low voltage, low current regime transitions to a higher current, high voltage regime at some transition point. Here, two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations using EDIPIC-2D are used to study an argon electron-cyclotron-resonance plasma cathode with an extracting anode, with the goal of identifying the kinetic mechanism connecting this transition point to the formation of a confined orifice plasma. The simulations reveal two self-consistent regimes: a low-current, diffusion dominated state in which the supply of electrons to the orifice is limited, and a high-current state characterized by a dense orifice plasma separated from the prescribed discharge plasma by a weak electrostatic double layer. In the latter regime, the double layer sustains intense localized ionization by accelerating source electrons while regulating particle exchange across the interface. Ion-acoustic wave activity is observed, and a low-Mach-number ion-acoustic shock forms within the double-layer region that produces a pronounced reversal in axial ion current density immediately below this interface. Time-resolved diagnostics reveal the formation mechanism for this orifice plasma that culminates in the coupling of the source, orifice, and plume regions. These results reveal a kinetic, time-dependent mechanism for the bi-modal transition in plasma cathodes and identify electron supply, plume-ionization seeding, and double-layer-shock dynamics as key elements governing access to the high-current regime.</jats:p>
title: A kinetic simulation of orifice plasma formation in plasma cathodes

items.abstract: <jats:p>After allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, there is profound, prolonged hypogammaglobulinemia due to slow B cell immune reconstitution, often requiring 1-2 years for full numeric and functional recovery. During this time, patients, particularly those with graft-versus-host disease, respond poorly to vaccinations and are at serious risk from opportunistic infections. Plasma cells can produce copious amounts of immunoglobulin (Ig), essential for long-lasting immunity and robust vaccine responses. Herein, we report the development of human B cells and their terminally differentiated progeny, plasma cells, from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) with the potential to restore provide protective, medically relevant antibody. We show that human iPSCs engineered to express a single-chain VJ-VDJ differentiated into immature IgM+ B cells, in contrast to non-engineered iPSCs that failed to produce immature B cells. Furthermore, these immature B cells could be matured toward transitional B cell subsets by adding BAFF and IL-4 to the iPSC culture. Matured B cells accompanied increased B cell proliferation following stimulation, and IgG class switching compared to non-matured subsets. This study benchmarks the capacity of human iPSCs to differentiate into B cells and plasma cells and offer a path toward off-the-shelf cell-based therapeutics.</jats:p>
title: Engineered iPSC derived B- and plasma cells provide insights into B cell development and a novel therapeutic platform

items.abstract: <jats:p>The dual need to secure vanadium as a strategically valuable resource and minimize the environmental impact of vanadium-contaminated effluents has encouraged the exploration of advanced and effective separation approaches for recovering it from secondary and industrial wastes sources. In the current work, a sustainable sol-gel methodology was employed to fabricate nano silica functionalized with Alamine 336 sorbent (NSi-Al336) and evaluated for its potential in vanadium uptake. Comprehensive assessment of the prepared material was conducted to elucidate its structural features, surface properties and textural characteristics. The dependence of vanadium uptake on solution acidity, initial concentration, shaking time, and temperature was assessed to elucidate the adsorption performance. Surface modification with amine functionalities resulted in a remarkable improvement in adsorption capacity. Efficient and rapid vanadium sorption was achieved using the functionalized sorbent at pH 4.0. Dubinin-Radushkevich and Langmuir models provided a good description of the equilibrium results, yielding loading capacity of 97.09 mg/g. Whereas, satisfactory consistency was observed between kinetic data and pseudo-second-order model. Thermodynamic evaluation revealed favorable spontaneous sorption accompanied by endothermic interaction. These results supported the feasibility of employing the developed material for vanadium separation from fly ash leach liquor.</jats:p>
title: Tailoring and Characterization of Alamine 336-Functionalized Silica Nanomaterial for Effective Vanadium Sorption: Equilibrium, Kinetic, and Thermodynamic Insights

<jats:sec id="st1">
                    <jats:title>Introduction:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Androgenic/Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) typically involves a receding hairline, hair loss on the crown, or both. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is an effective autologous blood product with a large concentration of platelets used for treatment of AGA. Microneedling, a minimally invasive procedure with fine needles, stimulates stem cells and growth factors. We aim to study the efficacy and safety of PRP with microneedling vs PRP in the treatment of AGA</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="st2">
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      54 AGA patients separated into 2 groups of 27 each were enrolled. After ethical clearance, Group 1 underwent three sessions of PRP therapy, while Group 2 underwent PRP in combination with 1-mm dermaroller microneedling. The patient’s hair growth and density were assessed using a seven-point scale, and physicians evaluated hair growth from baseline photos using the same scale. Statistical analysis was performed using descriptive and inferential methods, with the Chi-square test applied, and a
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      value <0.05 considered statistically significant.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="st3">
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Both groups showed statistically significant improvement on both subjective and objective assessments. On subjective assessment, mild-to-moderate improvement was observed in 74.1% of the PRP group and 77.8% of the PRP+MN group (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      =0.0001 for both). On objective assessment, mild-to-moderate improvement was seen in 88.9% of the PRP group and 77.8% of the PRP+MN group (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      = 0.0001 for both), with minimal non-responders or worsening in either group. Small sample size, Attrition to follow-up, lack of long-term (>6months) follow-up, lack of trichoscopic evaluation were the limitations of the study.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="st4">
                    <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The addition of microneedling to PRP did not result in a statistically significant difference (Subjective
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      =0.98, Objective
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      =0.37), although patients with PRP+MN experienced better results.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Comparison of microneedling with platelet rich plasma therapy versus platelet rich plasma therapy in patients of androgenic alopecia: A prospective study

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Oxygen transport in zirconium dioxide controls the growth kinetics of the oxide layer that protects zirconium alloy cladding, yet how the charge state of an oxygen vacancy modulates this transport at the electronic level remains poorly quantified for the monoclinic phase. Here we combine first-principles calculations with kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations to link the electronic structure of oxygen vacancies to macroscopic diffusion in monoclinic ZrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    (m-ZrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ). We first build the complete network of elementary vacancy hops, with migration barriers spanning 1.42-2.60 eV, and find that diffusion is intrinsically anisotropic, being fastest along [001]. A single direct hop along [001] dominates the transport, contributing more than 90% of the total diffusion coefficient over 400-1400 K, while the [100] and [010] directions are fed by the higher-barrier hops; the total diffusion coefficient follows an Arrhenius law with an effective activation energy of 1.748 eV and a pre-exponential factor of 2.70 × 10
                    <jats:sup>-2</jats:sup>
                    cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    s
                    <jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>
                    . The doubly positively charged (+2q) vacancy is the thermodynamically stable species over most of the Fermi-level range and is also far more mobile: the barrier of the dominant hop falls to 0.76 eV, the effective activation energy of the total diffusion coefficient to 0.758 eV, and the diffusion coefficient rises by up to eleven orders of magnitude at 400 K, the lowest temperature considered. Charge density difference, electron localization function and Bader charge analyses trace this behavior to the removal of the vacancy-trapped electrons, which eliminates their repulsive interaction with the electron cloud of the migrating oxygen ion and weakens the Zr-O bonds along the migration path, as evidenced by elongated bond lengths and reduced charge transfer. Oxygen diffusion in m-ZrO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    is therefore governed by a charge-state-driven interplay between the local electronic distribution and the Zr-O bonding, with the +2q vacancy ensuring both thermodynamic stability and rapid kinetics under reactor operating conditions and thus providing a microscopic basis for modeling oxide growth and the corrosion lifetime of zirconium alloy cladding.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Oxygen Vacancy-Mediated Diffusion in Monoclinic ZrO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    : A Combined First-Principles and Kinetic Monte Carlo Study

items.abstract: <jats:p>Digital engineering initiatives and the increased complexity of today’s systems necessitate using model-based systems engineering in defense acquisitions. While model-based systems engineering research grows, performing system safety analysis in a digital environment is limited in the knowledge space. This paper presents research investigating how to create and present model-based safety reviews that meet MIL-STD-882E system safety process requirements. A coordination-rich and civil engineering small Unmanned Aerial System development project served as the case study using a model-based systems engineering framework comprised (1) System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA) extended for coordination as the safety analysis method, (2) Systems Modeling Language with extension Risk Analysis and Assessment Modeling Language, and (3) modeling tool CATIA Magic Systems of Systems Architect. Results provide the model-based STPA artifacts for a system safety review that meets MIL-STD-882E Element 1 through 4 requirements and the qualitative survey responses from presenting a model-based safety review to a focus group. Significant contributions of this research include an STPA to MIL-STD-882E mapping, a Risk Analysis and Assessment Modeling Language model–based safety review framework using STPA extended for coordination, and curated insights and recommendations to promote successful model-based safety reviews.</jats:p>
title: Toward model-based safety reviews: MIL-STD-882E system safety compliance using STPA extended for coordination

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Efficient pneumatic conveying of fine agricultural grains requires reliable prediction of pressure loss under varying conveying and particle conditions. This study presents a computational fluid dynamics discrete phase model (CFD-DPM) sensitivity analysis of pressure drop in dilute-phase pneumatic conveying of teff grain, considering superficial air velocity, pipe diameter, particle sphericity, particle density, and representative particle diameter. A balanced factorial design comprising 324 CFD-DPM simulations was evaluated using four pipe diameters (46, 71, 102, and 125 mm), three air velocities (16, 20, and 24 m s
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ), and three levels of each particle property. The numerical model was quantitatively assessed against previously measured horizontal conveying data, achieving an R² of 0.989. Mesh-independence testing showed a pressure-drop difference of 0.8% between the selected 4.60-mm mesh and the finest tested mesh. Across the investigated design space, the predicted pressure drop ranged from 43.67 to 480.03 Pa, with an overall mean of 158.58 Pa. Increasing air velocity from 16 to 24 m s
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    increased the marginal mean pressure drop from 108.04 to 209.26 Pa, corresponding to a 93.7% increase. Increasing pipe diameter from 46 to 125 mm reduced the marginal mean pressure drop from 227.37 to 84.43 Pa, corresponding to a 62.8% reduction at a constant solids feed rate of 0.030 kg s
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    . Increasing particle sphericity from 0.67 to 0.70 reduced the marginal mean pressure drop by 50.3%, whereas increasing particle density from 1120 to 1381 kg m
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    and particle diameter from 0.68 to 0.72 mm increased it by 17.9% and 16.6%, respectively. Range-normalized sensitivity coefficients were + 2.14, − 1.54, − 0.33, + 0.19, and − 0.07 for air velocity, pipe diameter, sphericity, density, and particle diameter, respectively. These results identify air velocity and pipe diameter as the most sensitive variables within the investigated design space, while particle sphericity has a greater normalized influence than particle diameter.
                  </jats:p>
title: CFD-DPM sensitivity analysis of particle and conveying parameters on pressure drop in dilute-phase pneumatic conveying of teff grain

items.abstract: <jats:p>Advancing Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF), particularly Fast Ignition and Shock Ignition, requires a deeper understanding of laser–plasma interactions in extreme regimes that remain difficult to access at large-scale ICF facilities. Long-wave infrared (LWIR) lasers provide a powerful approach, leveraging favorable wavelength scaling to access relativistic plasma physics, enable efficient laser beam channeling, and enhance the generation of hot electrons and energetic ions at significantly reduced laser intensity and plasma density. This capability allows laboratory-scale experiments to reproduce ICF-relevant conditions with improved diagnostic access and greater physical transparency. The Brookhaven National Laboratory Accelerator Test Facility offers a unique platform for such studies, combining a multi-terawatt LWIR laser with synchronized optical diagnostics and accelerator-based probes. This capability enables systematic investigation and optimization of key plasma processes governing ICF performance, thereby supporting the development of practical fusion energy systems.</jats:p>
title: Long wave infrared laser platform for plasma studies relevant to inertial fusion

items.abstract: <jats:p>Monod and Haldane parameters are frequently reported for field bioremediation trials, yet whether they can be identified from typical field sampling designs has rarely been examined. The aim of this study was to determine which kinetic parameters can be estimated from a field trial of realistic design and which design features are needed to identify more complex models. Six kinetic models were fitted to total petroleum hydrocarbon (TPH) series from a non-replicated field trial in the Kyzylorda region, Kazakhstan (five oil-amended treatments, seven sampling dates over 83 days, initial TPHs 18,188–19,800 mg kg−1). Identifiability was assessed with standard errors and profile likelihood, model support with the small-sample Akaike criterion, and design requirements with Monte Carlo simulations. The Monod half-saturation constant was not identifiable: its estimates collapsed to the zero- or first-order limit and ranged from the lower bound of the search interval to 7.8 × 105 mg kg−1 between treatments. The Haldane inhibition-constant profile was flat, and the nitrogen half-saturation constant was at best weakly identifiable. Zero- and first-order models fitted comparably but predicted cleanup times differing by a factor of 2.2–2.6. Simulations showed that identifying the Monod constant required at least 95% degradation, the Haldane constant at least three contaminant loading levels, and a defensible choice between zero and first order at least 70% degradation. Parameters of complex kinetic models should therefore be reported only together with an identifiability assessment.</jats:p>
title: The Limits of Validity of Kinetic Models in Field Trials of Bioremediation of Oil-Contaminated Soils

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The continuous advancement of magnetic shielding technology has posed greater challenges for underwater magnetic target detection. Given that installation position errors are inevitable during the installation of underwater fluxgate sensor, and that significant errors can cause the detection system to fail, a localization method based on event-triggered particle swarm optimization (ET-PSO) is proposed for underwater fluxgate sensors. An energized solenoid coil is used as the magnetic source, and ET-PSO estimates the sensor positions from the recorded magnetic-field measurements. The known range of sensor installation errors is used to guide the initialization of the particle swarm, enabling the algorithm to attain its final global-best solution in fewer iterations. To accommodate inaccurate prior installation information, an event-triggered mechanism dynamically adjusts the search center and radius. Extensive comparative simulations and experiments have demonstrated the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method. The proposed method achieves satisfactory localization accuracy with a relatively short iteration-stage runtime. In the water-tank experiment, it maintained a mean localization error of 0.0464 m even when the sensor position lay outside the initial search region, demonstrating centimeter-scale localization performance under inaccurate prior information.</jats:p>
title: Event-triggered particle swarm optimization-based localization method for underwater fluxgate sensor

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Universal donor cell therapies aim to combine the scalability and standardization of allogeneic manufacturing with reduced immune rejection across genetically diverse recipients. Current strategies primarily disrupt polymorphic human leukocyte antigen molecules and add constitutive protective modules against T cells, natural killer cells, antibodies, complement and phagocytes. However, immune compatibility cannot be inferred from the intended genotype alone. Reprogramming, genome engineering, clonal selection, expansion and differentiation can alter cellular identity, genomic integrity, proteostasis, inflammatory signaling and immune-ligand expression. In parallel, indirect antigen presentation, minor and non-HLA antigens, humoral memory, myeloid recognition and interindividual diversity in natural killer-cell repertoires may sustain rejection despite extensive immune editing. Here, we integrate these product-intrinsic, adaptive and innate barriers and examine the limitations of progressively accumulating permanent immune-evasion mechanisms. We argue that broader constitutive cloaking may increase manufacturing burden, compromise tissue-specific function and antiviral or antitumor surveillance, and protect cells that have become dysfunctional or unsafe. To address these trade-offs, we use the term Synthetic Immune Privilege to describe an integrative design framework for a programmable, localized and revocable protective state. This framework combines tissue-appropriate constitutive protection against predictable early threats with sensors of immune attack and cellular integrity, context-dependent decision circuits, temporally matched protective outputs and independent safety mechanisms. Rather than rendering grafts permanently invisible, Synthetic Immune Privilege seeks to deploy proportionate protection only when needed and withdraw it when the threat resolves or graft integrity is lost. Although its individual components have precedents in stem-cell and synthetic-cell engineering, their integration into universal donor grafts remains to be demonstrated and will require validation of circuit kinetics, stability, lineage compatibility and failure modes. We present this framework as a set of design principles for developing more controllable and adaptable universal donor cell therapies.</jats:p>
title: From Immune Evasion to Synthetic Immune Privilege: Residual Immune Barriers in Universal Donor Cell Therapies

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Although antiretroviral therapy (ART) has significantly improved the life expectancy of people living with HIV (PLWH), a survival gap compared with HIV-negative individuals persists. This premature aging is increasingly attributed to HIV-associated immunosenescence, with T cell senescence as a core pathological feature. However, the mechanisms that drive this process remain unclear, especially the contribution of specific cosignaling molecules. In contrast to the conventional view that immunosenescence is characterized by the loss of costimulatory signals, we found that the expression of the costimulatory receptor CD226 was significantly upregulated on CD4
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    T cells from PLWH and positively associated with immunosenescence. Elevated CD226 expression correlated with advanced HIV-1 disease progression and served as a potential prognostic biomarker for incomplete immune reconstitution after ART. We further demonstrated that CD226
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    CD4
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    T cells exhibited a distinct senescent phenotype, marked by increases in senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) activity, cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors, and DNA damage marker expression, and the secretion of proinflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotypes (SASPs). Multiomics and functional studies revealed that CD226 selectively activates the AKT–mTOR–SREBP1 pathway to induce lipid metabolic reprogramming, thereby potentiating pro-ferroptotic signaling and accelerating CD4
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    T cell senescence in PLWH. Importantly, in vitro treatment via CD226 blockade, classical ferroptosis inhibitors, or the non-canonical ferroptosis suppressor vitamin K3 effectively delayed CD4
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    T cell senescence in PLWH. Collectively, our findings reveal a CD226–ferroptosis–senescence regulatory cascade, identifying CD226 and its downstream metabolic-ferroptotic pathways as promising immunotherapeutic targets to mitigate immunosenescence and guide personalized immune reconstitution strategies in PLWH.
                  </jats:p>
title: CD226-induced ferroptosis contributes to CD4+ T cell immunosenescence in people living with HIV

items.abstract: <jats:p>Magnetic flux ropes are ubiquitous magnetic structures found in plasmas ranging from astrophysical to laboratory. We employ a newly developed parallel-kinetic–perpendicular-moment model to simulate the 3D interaction and evolution of two line-tied flux ropes at realistic laboratory plasma parameters, while retaining essential parallel kinetic physics in the system. We find that ropes undergo a current-dependent transition from a diamagnetic to paramagnetic regime, which we quantify with a simple analytic model. Although the macroscopic structural evolution qualitatively differs significantly between these regimes, analyzing the reconnection in proper field-aligned coordinates reveals that the underlying kinetic dynamics remain similar. Using the squashing factor and quasi-potential as diagnostics of 3D magnetic reconnection, we identify the formation of a quasi-separatrix layer and show that these quantities provide consistent metrics for reconnection rate and structure.</jats:p>
title: Line-tied flux rope relaxation and reconnection: A 3D kinetic case study

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Programmed cell death maintains organismal homeostasis and shapes the course of disease. Beyond classical apoptosis, several regulated cell death modalities have been defined, including ferroptosis, cuproptosis and disulfidptosis. Alkaliptosis is a distinct member of this family in which a sustained rise in intracellular pH operates as the proximate lethal signal rather than as a secondary consequence of injury. It differs from lysosome‐dependent cell death, which requires lysosomal membrane permeabilization and cathepsin release, and from general alkaline stress‐induced necrosis, which lacks dedicated molecular regulation. Cell death induced by JTC‐801 proceeds without caspase, RIPK3/MLKL, or GPX4 machinery. Although the core regulatory axes are defined, the downstream execution events connecting intracellular alkalinization to plasma membrane rupture remain unresolved. This review synthesizes current knowledge of alkaliptosis within an explicit evidence framework that separates directly supported findings from bioinformatic associations and review‐level statements. We summarize the two core axes, NF‐κB/IKKβ/CA9 and ATP6V0D1‐STAT3, together with extended regulatory networks that span ubiquitination, metabolic reprogramming, cholesterol metabolism and macropinocytosis. Evidence is strongest in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, where multiple independent studies, including in vivo models, converge, and is moderate in acute myeloid leukemia, gastric cancer, ovarian cancer, and aortic dissection. Involvement in lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, prostate cancer, head and neck cancer, and most non‐neoplastic conditions currently rests on computational association or review‐level mention. A structured comparison places pH homeostasis at the core of alkaliptosis relative to ferroptosis, cuproptosis, disulfidptosis, apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis. All available evidence remains preclinical. No alkaliptosis‐targeting agent has entered clinical trials, and biomarker validation, definition of the therapeutic window and pathway‐specific pharmacodynamics remain unresolved.</jats:p>
title: Alkaliptosis: Mechanisms, Disease Relevance, and Translational Potential of a pH‐Dependent Form of Regulated Cell Death

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Surgical resection with lymph node dissection is standard-of-care for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Resected NSCLC patients may develop distant postoperative recurrence, for which immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based regimens are widely applied. Pre-clinical data suggest that extensive lymph node resection may impair ICI efficacy by disrupting tumor-draining lymph node function, but clinical evidence remains scarce. This study aimed to explore the association between prior lymph node dissection extent and ICI outcomes in patients with postoperative recurrent NSCLC, and to compare ICI efficacy between postoperative-recurrent and de-novo stage-IV metastatic NSCLC.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this single-center retrospective study, 93 driver-gene-negative metastatic NSCLC patients treated with ICI between 2018–2020 were enrolled, including 39 patients with postoperative recurrence and 54 patients with primary metastatic disease. Within the recurrence group, patients were stratified by lymph-node-dissection modality and number of dissected lymph nodes (DLNs, optimal cut-off = 10 defined by X-tile). Survival endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Multivariable Cox regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Postoperative-recurrent patients exhibited shorter median PFS than primary-metastatic patients (7.3 vs. 11.5 months, p = 0.034). Among 39 recurrent patients, those with DLNs&gt;10 had significantly poorer median PFS compared with patients with DLNs ≤10 (5.1 vs. 13.2 months, p &lt; 0.0001). After multivariable adjustment, DLNs ≤10 remained an independent protective factor for PFS (HR = 0.183, 95%CI 0.080–0.421; p &lt; 0.0001). No significant OS difference was observed across subgroups.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A greater extent of prior lymph node dissection is associated with shorter PFS among ICI-treated patients with postoperatively recurrent NSCLC. These real-world findings support the immunological relevance of tumor-draining lymph nodes and generate a hypothesis for individualized lymph node management during NSCLC surgery.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: A retrospective study on the impact of lymph node dissection on the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in postoperative recurrent non-small cell lung cancer patients

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Intestinal stem cell (ISC) dysfunction compromises epithelial repair and contributes to intestinal aging, yet naturally derived metabolites that preserve ISC homeostasis remain incompletely defined. Through metabolomic profiling of a standardized edible mushroom extract, we identified hercynine (HER) as the most abundant detected metabolite and investigated its role in intestinal repair and aging. In
                    <jats:italic>Drosophila</jats:italic>
                    , HER accelerated post‐injury epithelial repair by promoting timely restoration of ISC/progenitor dynamics and epithelial differentiation. During physiological aging, mid‐life HER supplementation preferentially attenuated age‐associated ISC/progenitor dysfunction, accompanied by improved intestinal homeostasis, enhanced organismal fitness, and extended lifespan. Mechanistically, HER shifted aged ISC/progenitor transcriptomes toward a more youth‐associated state, with genetic and pharmacological pathway‐perturbation experiments supporting the functional involvement of insulin signaling in HER‐mediated improvements in aged ISC/progenitor homeostasis. HER was also associated with remodeling of the gut microbiota during injury repair and aging; microbiota perturbation experiments suggested that this remodeling represented an accompanying response to HER treatment rather than the primary driver of ISC protection. In aged human small intestinal organoids, HER improved budding capacity, ISC/progenitor‐associated activity, and epithelial differentiation, while reducing p‐AKT levels, supporting a conserved epithelial response in a mammalian model. Together, these findings identify HER as a mushroom‐derived metabolite that supports ISC‐centered intestinal epithelial repair and mitigates intestinal aging, highlighting dietary metabolites as potential modulators of stem cell‐associated epithelial homeostasis during tissue repair and aging.
                  </jats:p>
title: Dietary Hercynine Protects Intestinal Stem Cell Function During Epithelial Repair and Aging Through Insulin Signaling

items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Secondary neutron fields generated by high-energy proton–target interactions constitute one of the major radiation components that must be considered in the design of shielding systems for accelerator facilities. In this study, the multidirectional transport of secondary neutrons produced by the interaction of 1000 MeV protons with a copper target, together with the associated spatial attenuation characteristics of ambient dose equivalent H*(10), was investigated within a tunnel-type accelerator geometry. The shielding geometry comprised concrete side walls modeled as successive layers, a monolithic concrete base block, and a surrounding soil region, enabling neutron transport to be evaluated in both the horizontal and vertical directions. A dataset consisting of 1158 spatial data points was generated from high-fidelity ambient dose equivalent H*(10) distributions calculated using FLUKA Monte Carlo (MC) simulations and was subsequently employed to develop regression-based machine learning (ML) surrogate models. For the ML analysis, spatial distance along the investigated horizontal and vertical directions was used as the predictor variable, while the corresponding FLUKA-calculated H*(10) value was used as the target variable. The ETR, RF, GBR, HGBR, and KNN algorithms were trained and evaluated using a 10-fold cross-validation procedure. All models reproduced the FLUKA-derived H*(10) distributions with high predictive accuracy (R² &gt; 0.98), with the most stable predictive performance achieved by the tree-based ensemble models.The FLUKA results demonstrated a distance-dependent reduction in ambient dose equivalent H*(10) across the modeled concrete shielding regions and revealed pronounced directional variations in neutron transport within the investigated concrete-soil geometry. Since the adjacent concrete layers were defined with identical elemental composition and density, the calculated attenuation behavior was not interpreted as arising from an additional physical scattering mechanism associated with the boundaries between these layers. Furthermore, because a controlled comparison with a monolithic concrete reference configuration having identical total thickness and material properties was not performed, no inference was made regarding superior shielding performance of the layered geometry relative to monolithic concrete. Accordingly, the present results characterize the multidirectional neutron transport and H*(10) distributions of the investigated concrete-soil shielding geometry under 1000 MeV proton irradiation conditions. The findings demonstrate that integrating MC simulations with ML-based surrogate modeling provides a practical and computationally efficient approach for rapid H*(10) prediction and shielding assessment within the investigated fixed irradiation and shielding configuration.</jats:p>
title: Monte Carlo and Machine Learning Analysis of Multidirectional Neutron Shielding in Layered Concrete Accelerator Tunnels over a Soil-Embedded Concrete Base

items.abstract: <jats:p>O crescimento acelerado do comércio eletrônico exige operações logísticas cada vez mais eficientes, especialmente no setor de Beleza e Saúde, cujos produtos apresentam prazos de validade rigorosos e forte volatilidade de consumo. Este trabalho tem como objetivo desenvolver e avaliar algoritmos preditivos de Machine Learning capazes de estimar a demanda futura dessa categoria, visando mitigar os riscos de ruptura e o excesso de mercadorias no armazém. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como aplicada e quantitativa, utilizando dados reais de transações extraídos do Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset (Olist). O processamento computacional foi realizado na linguagem Python, na qual os registros brutos foram tratados e transformados em uma série temporal diária. Para fins de validação comparativa, o estudo avaliou o desempenho do modelo estatístico tradicional ARIMA contra o algoritmo de aprendizado supervisionado Random Forest, utilizando as métricas matemáticas MAE, RMSE e WAPE. Nos experimentos realizados, o algoritmo Random Forest apresentou melhor desempenho preditivo nas métricas avaliadas, obtendo WAPE de 31,73%, frente a 37,00% do ARIMA, além de maior aderência visual às oscilações sazonais da série. Conclui-se que a adoção de modelos orientados a dados oferece suporte analítico mais consistente ao planejamento de compras, com potencial para auxiliar na mitigação de rupturas e excessos de estoque no setor.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Full‐waveform inversion (FWI) is a powerful technique for recovering high‐resolution subsurface models, but its performance is often limited by insufficient observational constraints, which often lead to cycle skipping and poorly illuminated models. In this study, we propose a diffusion image prior (DIIP) framework for FWI that leverages pretrained diffusion models as geological priors for velocity reconstruction. Unlike conventional Deep Image Prior (DIP) approaches, DIIP represents the velocity model in the latent space of a pretrained diffusion model and performs inversion through latent‐space optimization constrained by seismic data. Deterministic denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM) encoding is used to project the initial model into the diffusion latent space, where a learnable latent perturbation is optimized to minimize the seismic data misfit while the velocity model is reconstructed through the reverse diffusion process. The strength of the diffusion prior is progressively relaxed during inversion through a timestep scheduling strategy, enabling the recovery of stable large‐scale background structures in early iterations, followed by progressive refinement of finer geological details. Numerical experiments on two synthetic examples demonstrate that DIIP improves inversion stability, suppresses inversion artifacts, and produces more geologically consistent velocity reconstructions than both conventional FWI and DIP‐FWI particularly in the absence of low‐frequency information. Field‐data application to the Viking Graben data set further demonstrates the effectiveness of DIIP for realistic seismic inversion. Additional analysis highlights the importance of controlling diffusion‐prior strength during FWI and demonstrates that, in field‐data applications, training diffusion models on geologically similar data sets improves inversion quality by reducing prior mismatch.</jats:p>
title: Diffusion Image Prior for Enhanced Full Waveform Inversion

items.abstract: <jats:p>Pertumbuhan e-commerce fashion wanita menunjukkan peluang besar namun juga tantangan dalam menghadirkan pengalaman belanja yang personal dan relevan. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan sistem rekomendasi personal berbasis machine learning pada platform e-commerce berbasis web untuk fashion wanita. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan Agile Scrum, dengan metode iteratif untuk pengembangan fitur rekomendasi yang dikembangkan dan dievaluasi menggunakan empat algoritma yaitu Logistic Regression, Random Forest, KNN, dan SVM. Evaluasi performa dilakukan menggunakan metrik MAE dan RMSE, serta uji kelayakan sistem melalui System Usability Scale (SUS). Hasil menunjukkan bahwa Logistic Regression memiliki akurasi terbaik dalam skenario data yang digunakan (akurasi 33%), dan pengujian SUS memperoleh skor 67,95 yang termasuk kategori “cukup dapat digunakan”. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi praktis terhadap peningkatan personalisasi dalam platform e-commerce serta pendekatan teknis yang dapat direplikasi pada konteks sistem serupa.</jats:p>
title: Penerapan Machine Learning untuk Fitur Rekomendasi Terpersonalisasi pada Platform E-Commerce Fashion Wanita

items.abstract: <jats:p>This discussion provides an introduction to and survey of machine learning methods in econometrics, covering both predictive and causal applications. We first consider supervised machine learning for predicting or forecasting an outcome of interest, such as wages, credit default, or product demand, including penalized regression, tree-based methods, support vector machines, and boosting, followed by neural network architectures. Next, we discuss unsupervised learning, which aims to detect patterns in data without a predefined outcome variable, covering clustering methods that group observations by similarity and dimensionality reduction techniques that extract compact representations of high-dimensional data. We then turn to causal machine learning for treatment evaluation, such as assessing the impact of job training programs on employment or of price changes on demand, covering average treatment effect estimation via data-adaptive control of confounders using double machine learning, treatment effect heterogeneity analysis based on causal forests, optimal policy learning to target subpopulations for whom treatment is most beneficial, and reinforcement learning for dynamic treatment allocation. We also discuss the implications of artificial intelligence-generated variables for causal analysis. Finally, we provide an introduction to causal discovery, which aims to learn causal structures among multiple variables from observational data in a data-driven manner.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Forecasting with machine learning often goes wrong due to the protocol and not the algorithms for reasons including leakage, model selection on the test sample, no naive benchmark, and no allowance for the number of models tried. 4Cast Lab is a free, open-source, single-file application that makes a benchmark-first protocol the default: time-ordered splits; selection by cross-validation inside the training period; one use of the Test Set; a naive benchmark with Diebold–Mariano and Clark–West tests; and the Holm, Reality Check, SPA and Model Confidence Set procedures. We document the protocol, the leakage controls and the fixed rules of the AutoML verdict, and report three kinds of evidence. A four-stage benchmark against certified values and reference software shows agreement to at least six significant digits and pre-specified equivalence tests for the random learners. A simulation run through the application shows that, for random-walk targets, common reporting rules declare a false success in 21 to 95% of cases and the benchmark-first verdict in 0 to 1%, at a measured cost in power. On 59 M4 monthly series and the US unemployment rate, the application matches MLForecast for like learners and approaches StatsForecast once the target is differenced.</jats:p>
title: 4Cast Lab: Open-Source App for Machine Learning and Statistical Analysis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Non-invasive cancer detection through breath volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis is a promising direction for biomedical screening, yet the comparative value of gradient boosting algorithms and the statistical soundness of explainable pipelines built on them remain under-examined in this domain. This study benchmarks two gradient boosting algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM) against four conventional classifiers (Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron) on a balanced dataset of 1,000 breath-VOC samples comprising seven VOC biomarkers plus age, sex, and smoking status, using stratified 10-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was applied to the best-performing gradient boosting model to quantify biomarker-level feature contributions, and four independent diagnostics — bootstrap confidence intervals, a label-permutation control, learning-curve analysis, and probability calibration — assessed the statistical validity of the resulting model. All six classification models achieved near-perfect discrimination (AUC ≥ 0.9999), with no statistically significant advantage for gradient boosting over simpler models (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p ≥ 0.25); only the Multi-Layer Perceptron showed a materially lower recall (0.91) at its default decision threshold. SHAP identified benzene, formaldehyde, isoprene, and toluene as the dominant contributors to classification decisions, while demographic covariates contributed negligibly. Validity diagnostics confirmed the pipeline was leakage-free but also showed that near-perfect separability saturates with as few as 80 training samples, indicating that the dataset's synthetic label-generating process, rather than genuine biological complexity, drives the observed performance. We conclude that the gradient boosting–SHAP pipeline is methodologically sound as a proof-of-concept explainable-AI framework, but the reported performance cannot be interpreted as evidence of real-world clinical validity without replication on VOC measurements from actual patient cohorts.</jats:p>
title: Gradient Boosting versus Classical Machine Learning for Breath-VOC Cancer Classification

items.abstract: <jats:p>Ecommerce websites can have a lot of reviews, but not all reviews with a specific sentiment lead to a recommendation. This study demonstrates whether review text will predict if a customer would recommend a clothing item and if a transformer can outperform traditional machine learning models when a minority (non-recommended) class is of interest. This Women’s E-Commerce Clothing Reviews dataset has been cleaned to retain 22,641 reviews that have non-empty text and a binary recommendation label. Training, validation and test sets were created using stratification. Using class-specific performance measures, balanced accuracy, ROC-AUC, average precision, confusion matrices and paired bootstrapped confidence intervals, the models were compared: a majority baseline, logistic regression, linear Support Vector Machine (SVM), Naive Bayes, Random Forest, LightGBM and finetuned BERT. The accuracy of BERT on the 4527 unseen test reviews was 91.39%, and the non-recommendation F1 score, recall and precision were 0.780, 0.845 and 0.725, respectively. Compared to logistic regression, BERT achieved an accuracy gain of 0.036 and a non-recommendation F1 gain of 0.064. The 95% paired bootstrapped confidence intervals for both did not contain zero. Both logistic regression and linear SVM were very similar. The most important contribution of this work is the development of a class-aware transformer benchmark for recommendation classification.</jats:p>
title: From Customer Voice to Predictive Intelligence: Machine Learning Analysis of E-Commerce Reviews

                    Accurate disease classification requires holistic reasoning, but unimodal models fail to cross-reference visual patterns from chest X-rays with complementary information from radiology reports. The architecture integrates a Swin Transformer visual encoder and a Bio_ClinicalBERT textual encoder; critically, a Hierarchical Multi-Scale Bidirectional Co-Attention mechanism is introduced to facilitate bidirectional alignment, dynamically weighting radiographic regions of interest based on corresponding clinical entities. Evaluation is conducted on a subset of MIMIC-CXR dataset, involving a systematic comparison of early, intermediate, and late fusion strategies. items.abstract: <jats:p>Hearing impairment is one of the most prevalent sensory disabilities worldwide, affecting an estimated 1.5 billion people and expected to rise to 2.5 billion by 2050. Advances in signal processing, machine learning, and wearable computing have transformed the landscape of assistive technologies designed for individuals with hearing loss. Modern systems go beyond traditional amplification to include adaptive digital hearing aids, cochlear implants with noise-resistant coding strategies, real-time automatic speech recognition (ASR) captioning, sign language recognition and translation, and haptic feedback devices for environmental awareness. This survey provides a structured and technically detailed review of these systems, covering both foundational and emerging approaches. The discussion begins with a taxonomy of hardware-based and software-driven solutions, followed by an in-depth examination of datasets, algorithms, and evaluation protocols. Special emphasis is placed on the integration of deep neural networks into low-latency pipelines, multimodal fusion techniques, and AR-based caption delivery. The paper identifies persistent challenges—such as dataset diversity, real-time processing constraints, and high costs—that limit widespread adoption. Finally, research gaps are translated into actionable future directions, establishing a foundation for a subsequent empirical analysis paper aimed at benchmarking leading hearing-assistive technologies under standardized conditions.</jats:p>
title: ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGIES FOR HEARING IMPAIRMENT PEOPLE USING MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS.

<jats:p>Large-scale portfolio selection requires accurate forecasts of high-dimensional dynamic conditional covariance matrices (CCMs). This task is challenging because the number of covariance elements grows quickly with the number of assets, whereas the available time-series observations are limited and noisy. In this paper, we propose a novel graph-based quantiled (GRAND) CCM estimator in the spirit of “divide and conquer.” By extracting information from the extensive asset features, the GRAND method leverages a new graph-based deep learning network, called the self-grouping autoencoder (SGA), to learn the conditional quantiles of returns. Using those learned conditional quantiles, the GRAND method further learns (co)variances of CCM element-wisely via the quantiled conditional moment (QCM) method, and finally, it makes the resulting assembled CCM estimator positive semidefinite through a projection. Because of the use of the SGA network and the QCM method in an element-wise way, the GRAND method is blessing dimensionality in learning the CCM of a large-scale portfolio, while keeping the computation manageable and maintaining causal semantics. From an extensive empirical analysis of the Chinese stock market, we show that the GRAND method can produce much better tangency portfolios than its competitors, and provide dynamic causal graphs to study variance and quantile connectedness of all stocks for interpreting systemic risk and forecasting the business cycle.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper was accepted by Kay Giesecke, finance.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Funding: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72503203 and 72573142]; the Natural Science Foundation of Fujian Province [Grants 2025J01036 and 2025J08009]; the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities [Grant 20720251053]; and the Research Grants Council, University Grants Committee [Grants 17302424, 17304421, 17304723, and 17312622].</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.08930 .</jats:p>
title: Machine Learning Vast Dynamic Conditional Covariance Matrices: The Spirit of “Divide and Conquer”

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Buoyancy glitches in red giants provide localized information on the interior structure near the base of the convective envelope, but their properties are typically inferred from dedicated seismic modelling rather than global properties, limiting large-sample applications. We investigate whether the buoyancy-glitch amplitude (Ag), location ($W_{\mathrm{g}}^{\star }$), and width (Dg) can be recovered from global stellar properties using gradient-boosted tree regressors (XGBoost and LightGBM). The models were trained on a grid of 12580 synthetic stellar models of low-luminosity red giants, with target parameters derived from fits to the local buoyancy frequency profile. We find that $W_{\mathrm{g}}^{\star }$ and Dg exhibit excellent recoverability, achieving test-set $\mathcal {R}^2$ values of 0.98 and 0.97, respectively. In contrast, Ag shows moderate recoverability overall ($\mathcal {R}^2=0.68$). This reduced recoverability of Ag is concentrated in the large frequency separation range Δν = 4.6–18.9 μHz, where the glitch resides in the evanescent-zone transition between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity, increasing intrinsic scatter. SHAP analysis shows that νmax and Teff dominate the predictions across all targets, indicating that the regressors rely primarily on evolutionary state. While $W_{\mathrm{g}}^{\star }$ and Dg are tightly constrained by global evolutionary trends, the lower recoverability of Ag reflects localized structural complexity associated with red-giant evolution. Overall, for the synthetic grid adopted here, these results indicate that global properties provide a direct estimate of the buoyancy-glitch parameters and a way to prioritise dedicated mixed-mode inversions for large asteroseismic samples such as Kepler and PLATO.</jats:p>
title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning

items.abstract: <jats:p>Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of atmospheric carbon dioxide and its underlying environmental drivers is critical for regional carbon cycle assessment. However, sparse satellite observations often hinder the generation of continuous spatial patterns. In this study, we analyzed the spatiotemporal patterns of a column-averaged dry air mole fraction of carbon dioxide (XCO2) across Mainland China for 2023 by integrating OCO-2 observations with multi-source environmental datasets using a random forest model. The model performance was rigorously evaluated using spatial block cross-validation and validated against ground-based TCCON stations, demonstrating reliable accuracy (R2 = 0.505, RMSE = 2.191 ppm) and effectively correcting the systematic underestimation bias of raw OCO-2 retrievals. Spatially, the predicted XCO2 exhibited pronounced gradients, with high-value areas concentrated in the North China Plain and eastern urban agglomerations, while low values were observed in southwestern forests. Temporally, XCO2 showed a distinct “summer low, winter high” seasonal cycle, primarily influenced by vegetation photosynthesis and meteorological conditions, with potential contributions from seasonal human activities. To unravel the underlying mechanisms, we employed interpretable machine learning techniques, including SHAP values and partial dependence plots (PDPs). The results revealed that temperature (TEMP) and elevation (DEM) are the dominant statistical predictors of XCO2 spatial variability, exhibiting significant nonlinear responses and interaction effects. Notably, the negative impact of Leaf Area Index (LAI) exhibited a saturation threshold effect at approximately 4.0. Furthermore, inter-tree variance analysis indicated that prediction uncertainty was highly heterogeneous, being minimal in flat eastern plains (<1.0 ppm) but elevated in topographically complex regions like the Tibetan Plateau (>1.5 ppm). This study not only provides a high-resolution XCO2 product for China but also offers deep interpretable insights into the nonlinear environmental controls on regional carbon dynamics.</jats:p>
title: Spatiotemporal Patterns of XCO2 in Mainland China: A Machine Learning Approach with Interpretable Environmental Drivers

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Uplift modeling and Heterogeneous Treatment Effect (HTE) estimation aim to predict the causal effect of an action, such as a medical treatment or a marketing campaign on a specific individual. In this paper, we focus on data from Randomized Controlled Experiments which guarantee a causal interpretation of the outcomes. Class imbalance is an important problem in uplift modeling/HTE because it occurs in many domains where it is applied, such as online advertising. Unfortunately classical undersampling or oversampling based approaches are difficult to apply in this context because they distort the predicted effect. Calibration methods have been proposed in the past, however, they do not guarantee correct predictions. In this work, we propose an approach alternative to undersampling, based on flipping the class value of selected records. We show that the proposed approach does not distort the predicted effect and does not require calibration. The method is especially useful for models based on class variable transformation (modified outcome models). We address those models separately, designing a transformation scheme which guarantees correct predictions and simultaneously resolves the problem of spurious correlations with treatment variable which degrade performance of those models. Experiments fully confirm our theoretical results. Additionally, we demonstrate that our method is a viable alternative also for other types of uplift models and for standard imbalanced classification problems.</jats:p>
title: Class Flipping for Uplift Modeling and Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation on Imbalanced RCT Data

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how National Climate Change Policy (NCCP) influences firm-level climate risk disclosure (CRD). The study also investigates whether the policy affects transition- and physical-risk disclosure differently, and how analyst coverage, political connections and CSR intensity shape this relationship.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study uses firm-year data for companies listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange from 2007 to 2022. CRD is measured using a hybrid computational linguistics framework that combines Word2Vec embeddings, semantic expansion and multi-stage expert validation to construct separate disclosure indices for transition and physical risk. The empirical analysis employs an exposure-based difference-in-differences design.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that NCCP affects climate disclosure selectively rather than uniformly. The policy significantly increases physical-risk disclosure, whereas transition-risk disclosure declines in the baseline specification. Dynamic estimates support parallel trends and indicate that the effects emerge gradually. Further analysis shows that policy-relevant political connections are associated with stronger disclosure responses, while higher CSR intensity mitigates the decline in transition-risk disclosure and amplifies the increase in physical-risk disclosure. Analyst coverage provides suggestive evidence of an information-intermediary channel.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings suggest that climate policy alone may not be sufficient to ensure broad-based transparency in a weak-enforcement environment. Stricter mandatory rules, better institutional coordination and external monitoring may improve corporate climate transparency.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study provides evidence from a climate-vulnerable emerging economy and introduces a validated text-based CRD measure that distinguishes transition-risk from physical-risk disclosure and shows that policy effects depend on political access, external monitoring and strategic capacity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Climate change policy and climate risk disclosure: evidence from machine learning and textual analysis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Federated learning (FL) is a distributed learning approach that protects privacy by processing data on the client side without transferring it to a central server. However, the effective implementation of the right to be forgotten, as defined under bullet 17 of the European Union General Data Protection Regulation and bullet 7 of the Turkish Personal Data Protection Law, within FL architectures remains a significant research problem. A significant portion of current approaches require retraining due to the intertwined structure of client contributions within the global model, leading to high computational costs and scalability issues. This study proposes the Federated Forget (FedFORGET) architecture, a new machine forgetting method based on relational classification that does not require retraining for federated learning environments. In the proposed method, each client generates labeled association rules using the Classification Based on Associations algorithm on its own local data. The global model is created by combining these rules on the server side using the Federated Classification Based on Association (FedCBA) algorithm. In the event of a forget request, only the rules belonging to the relevant client are mathematically extracted from the global model; thus, the forget operation is performed without accessing the raw data and without retraining the entire model. The effectiveness of FedFORGET was evaluated on five open datasets with different scales and feature spaces: IBM HR Analytics (1,470 examples, 35 features), Adult Census Income (48,842 examples, 14 features), Mushroom (8,124 examples, 23 features), Car Evaluation (1,728 examples, six features), and Nursery (12,960 examples, eight features). In the experiments, the support and confidence thresholds were set to 0.1; the datasets were split into 80% training and 20% testing. The obtained results demonstrate that FedFORGET significantly reduces the forgetting time compared to retraining-based approaches, while largely preserving model accuracy and classification performance after the unlearning process. Furthermore, the method yields stable performance across both independent and identically distributed (IID) and non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data distributions. Overall, FedFORGET provides a computationally efficient, scalable, verifiable, and explainable solution for enabling the right to be forgotten in federated learning systems.</jats:p>
title: FedFORGET: a relational classification-based method for machine unlearning in federated learning environments

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We propose a generative learner for estimating conditional average treatment effects and characterizing the full distribution of these effects. The learner takes the form of a multi-head feed-forward neural network with three jointly estimated subnetworks: the propensity score, the conditional quantile function of the baseline outcome, and the conditional quantile treatment effect. Each quantile-indexed subnetwork combines a covariate representation with cosine quantile embeddings through element-wise multiplication. We then recover the conditional average treatment effect as an integral over conditional quantile treatment effects. Under the classical causal assumptions within the Neyman–Rubin potential outcomes framework, we find that the proposed generative learner reduces out-of-sample mean squared error relative to the generalized random forest, double machine learning, and generative adversarial networks, with gains ranging from 5.4% to 93.5% on average across experimental designs. In an empirical application, we formalize the Stefan–Boltzmann law within a unidirectional causal model and apply the method to publicly available stellar data. The estimated effects satisfy the restrictions the law implies.</jats:p>
title: Generative Learner for Distributional Causal Effects

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Active flow control (AFC) in supersonic and hypersonic aerodynamics has attracted sustained attention because of its potential to mitigate shockwave boundary layer interactions (SBLI), flow separation, and aerodynamic heating, all of which degrade the performance. Conventional AFC actuators such as synthetic jets and plasma actuators have demonstrated aerodynamic benefits. However, their tuning is largely empirical, computationally expensive and poorly suited to rapidly varying flow conditions. Machine learning (ML) offers a data driven alternative for real time adaptive control. This manuscript summarizes the use of supervised learning, reinforcement learning (RL), transfer learning and physics informed neural networks (PINNs) in AFC for high speed flows, drawing on documented case studies of ML optimized synthetic jet and plasma actuation that report drag reductions of roughly 15–99 % depending on configuration and Reynolds number. The governing compressible flow equations that constrain these ML models are summarized, followed by a comparative assessment of traditional and ML based AFC, a discussion of open challenges data scarcity, computational cost and a set of future directions centered on hybrid physics ML models and onboard real time inference. The results indicate that ML augmented AFC is a promising route toward adaptive, computationally tractable control of supersonic and hypersonic vehicles.</jats:p>
title: Role of machine learning in active flow control for supersonic and hypersonic flows

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Understanding the mechanisms governing complex environmental systems is a central challenge across environmental science and engineering. Where mechanistic understanding is incomplete, machine learning (ML) combined with explainable AI methods─particularly Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)─has been increasingly applied to environmental data sets, with the resulting explanations often interpreted as reflections of underlying process mechanisms. However, the extent to which SHAP explanations reflect true system behavior depends on the conditions under which the model was developed. Here, we systematically investigate how model class, data regime, and hyperparameter configuration as components of the learning environment affect the mechanistic consistency of SHAP-based explanations, using granular activated carbon (GAC) filtration for micropollutant removal from wastewater as a case study. We show that all three components impact explanations and their consistency with proven mechanisms. Model class can affect which feature interactions are captured; the characteristics of the training data─both distribution and lacking coverage of joint feature space regions─shape which relationships can be learned; and hyperparameter sensitivity differs substantially between model classes. These findings demonstrate that SHAP explanations cannot be interpreted independently of the learning environment, but we argue that they can still serve as a valuable tool for hypothesis generation in environmental ML applications.</jats:p>
title:
