items.abstract: <jats:p>Checking automatically that a monitoring stream still comes from the structure it is attributed to is useful for long-lived sensor networks, for drive-by and crowd-sourced sensing, and as a first step towards tracking changes within a structure. This paper studies feature-based fingerprinting of two prestressed highway bridges with similar geometry, built about 20 years apart, from the ambient accelerations recorded during 1705 heavy-vehicle passages over nine days. We propose two frequency-resolved energy measures based on the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) with the Cauchy–Paul wavelet, described by in-band peak and distribution-shape descriptors (24 features), and 12 further wavelet-moment features (excess kurtosis and skewness of the coefficient modulus across time at fixed scale). Together with time-domain, envelope and FFT-based features, they form a 67-feature library. Logistic regression, RBF-SVM and random forest are evaluated by leave-one-day-out validation, so that every test day is unseen. The analyses did not establish a clear performance difference between wavelet and frequency-domain features in this dataset (best balanced accuracy 0.975 for each family, reached by the random forest for wavelet features and by the SVM for frequency features), and their combination is the strongest configuration (0.989). At equal numbers of selected features, frequency features are better for very small subsets and not clearly different at ten, while combining the two families gains about two points. Results hold for night, day and a storm period and 3364 events from a later period (August, Bridge B only, never used for training) are mostly assigned correctly (94–98% across the three classifiers for the combined sets). The moment features alone are weak (balanced accuracy 0.74 to 0.78) and add nothing measurable to the other families. The discriminative information is associated with the location of higher-frequency resonances and the shape of band energy. We do not attribute it to ageing.</jats:p>
title: Wavelet-Augmented Feature-Based Machine Learning: Application to the Fingerprinting of Civil Engineering Structures from Vibration Signatures

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This paper presents a machine learning (ML)-assisted design of a novel asymmetrical open-slotted rectangular antenna for 6G wireless communication systems. The proposed antenna achieves triple-band operation at 10.2–10.6 GHz, 11.3–12.2 GHz, and a wideband range from 15.2–24.2 GHz, all within the 6G candidate upper-mid band (7.125–24.25 GHz). A dataset comprising 108 108 samples was generated through parametric CST simulations by varying key antenna design parameters, with each of the 108 antenna geometries evaluated at 1001 frequency points. To predict and optimize the reflection coefficient of an antenna, various ML models were trained including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, K-Nearest Neighbors and Extreme Gradient Boosting. Among the evaluated ML models, Random Forest demonstrated the best predictive performance, achieving an
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    value of 0.9961 and a root mean square error of 0.2883, with a mean absolute percentage error of only 0.9631%. Experimental validation shows good match between measured and predicted results. The peak gain of the optimized antenna is 7.4 dBi along with a radiation efficiency and total efficiency of 96.1% and 94.5% respectively. The results of this study show that ML-driven approaches can efficiently facilitate antenna design and optimization for high-performance 6G communication systems.
                  </jats:p>

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Traditional technical indicators such as Moving Averages, RSI, MACD, and Bollinger Bands often lag behind rapidly changing markets such as NIFTY 50 and BANK NIFTY, resulting in delayed entries, premature exits, and false signals. This paper proposes the low-latency machine learning indicator (RTMLI), an adaptive trading framework that integrates multidimensional feature engineering with Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM models to generate low-latency Buy, Hold, and Sell signals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The framework incorporates price, trend, momentum, volatility, volume, and price-action features and uses ensemble meta-learning to capture nonlinear market relationships. Experiments used historical and low-latency data from major Indian indices over 2022-2026.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      RTMLI outperforms individual ML models, including RF, XGBoost, LSTM, and GRU, as well as conventional Buy-and-Hold, EMA, RSI, MACD, and SuperTrend strategies. RTMLI achieved higher Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC, cumulative return, CAGR, Sharpe Ratio, Sortino Ratio, Profit Factor, and Win Rate, while maintaining lower Maximum Drawdown and signal latency. Statistical validation using the Paired t-test, Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test, and One-Way ANOVA confirmed the significance of the observed improvements at the 95% confidence level (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.05).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The framework also demonstrated millisecond-level signal generation with efficient computational resource utilization, supporting practical intraday deployment. Overall, RTMLI provides a lightweight, adaptive, and low-latency framework for intelligent algorithmic trading in Indian financial markets.</jats:p>

title: A real-time trading indicator for profitable trade in Indian indexes using machine learning

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Deriving accurate crop variety recommendations from real-world performance trials of small numbers of elite varieties available to farmers is essential for maximizing agricultural productivity. Current methods often rely on simple linear models that do not use genomic data, and genomic prediction methods were developed for large breeding populations. This study first presents a framework integrating 8,805 single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers obtained by genotyping-by-sequencing with Bayesian additive regression trees (BART) for genomic-assisted variety recommendations in winter wheat.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using multi-environment trial data from Ontario, Canada containing 36 elite, genotyped varieties grown at 17 locations between 2004 and 2018, we compared two models based on conventional best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP) and one model based on reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) regression against two BART models with restricted training data to emulate common variety recommendation scenarios. With a panel of only 36 varieties, BART was employed because its regularizing prior constrains each tree’s contribution, which reduces overfitting on small datasets.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>BART with genomic data achieved a higher Pearson correlation, a higher rank correlation, and a lower mean prediction error between predicted and observed grain yields than all other models by 5.0 to 11.2%, 10.2 to 21.7%, and 15.6 to 22.4%, respectively, when predicting individual locations using a single year of training data. This advantage narrowed as the training data increased from 1 to 3 and 5 years. With five years of data and genomic information, the linear models matched or exceeded BART on both correlation measures. Grouping locations into mega-environments increased the Pearson correlation of the BLUP and RKHS models by up to 9.2%, while the BART models changed by less than 2%. BART interpretability analysis revealed top predictive SNPs clustering on chromosomes 1B, 2B, and 3B near or colocalizing within known yield-related quantitative trait loci.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion and Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Genomic information improved both the linear and the tree-based models, and the interpretable regression-tree approach is best suited to location specific recommendations made from few observations, as is the case for newly released varieties.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Integrating genomic data and machine learning to improve winter wheat variety performance predictions in Ontario

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Explainable machine learning is increasingly used in learning analytics, yet the theoretical meaning of the engagement behaviors feeding these models remains underexplored. Drawing on embodied cognition and a four-layer model of embodied engagement, this study reinterprets behavioral engagement indicators and hypothesizes that (a) volitional participation behaviors predict higher achievement, and (b) behavioral withdrawal – indexed by absence – is the single strongest negative predictor.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The hypotheses were tested on two independent public datasets. Study 1 analyzed the xAPI-Edu-Data set (
                      <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                      = 480) using XGBoost with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) attribution. Study 2 replicated the pattern on the Portuguese secondary-school dataset (
                      <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                      = 966) with continuous final grades as the outcome.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In Study 1, the model achieved out-of-fold accuracy of .758 (macro-F1 = .766) against a .440 majority-class baseline. SHAP attribution ranked StudentAbsenceDays as the strongest predictor (mean |SHAP| = 1.056), followed by three volitional engagement behaviors (VisITedResources, raisedhands, AnnouncementsView); high-achieving students showed roughly four-fold higher participation than low-achieving peers across all engagement variables. In Study 2, the model explained continuous grades (R² = .344, RMSE = 3.13, MAE = 2.34), with prior failures (mean |SHAP| = .880) and absences (.619) dominating the contribution structure, and the behavioral block outweighing the entire demographic block combined. Across samples, countries, educational levels, and outcome types, the disembodiment signature – behavioral withdrawal indexed by absence and passivity – emerged as the most diagnostic marker of poor achievement, while volitional participation was the strongest positive predictor.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings illustrate how explainable AI can discipline theory construction in learning analytics, provide the first large-scale evidence consistent with an embodied mechanism of engagement, and directly inform the design of AI-enabled early-warning systems that treat behavioral presence as the primary signal of academic risk. Implications for digital pedagogy, learning-analytics dashboards, and the methodological use of interpretable machine learning to bridge educational theory and large-scale behavioral data are discussed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Embodied presence predicts academic achievement: a cross-dataset explainable machine learning analysis of student engagement behaviors

items.abstract: <jats:p>Pile foundations constitute a significant fraction of building expenses, rendering the precise evaluation of ultimate bearing capacity (Qu) essential for financial viability and structural integrity. This research examines the amalgamation of Grey Wolf Optimisation (GWO) with six machine learning methodologies: XGBoost, CatBoost, Bayesian Regularisation Neural Network (BRNN), Least Squares Support Vector Machine (LSSVM), Classification and Regression Trees (CART), and a Mamdani-type Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) as auxiliary preliminary estimation instruments in conjunction with traditional static load tests (SLT) and high-strain dynamic testing (HSDT). Employing a curated benchmark dataset comprising 59 driven pile load tests in cohesionless soils (41 for training and 18 for testing), the models integrate five geotechnical and geometric parameters: shaft friction angle (φs), tip friction angle (φt), pile length (L), cross-sectional area (A), and effective vertical stress at the pile tip (σ’v). Model efficacy is assessed using R2, RMSE, MAE, and VAF. GWO-XGBoost attained the superior predictive precision with R2 = 0.9992 (training) and R2 = 0.9418 (testing), closely followed by GWO-CatBoost with R2 = 0.9991 (training) and R2 = 0.9195 (testing). GWO-CART and GWO-Fuzzy demonstrated somewhat elevated prediction inaccuracies, but all six GWO-optimized models effectively represented the nonlinear pile-soil interaction within the database limits. The GWO-optimized gradient boosting models serve as a quick and reliable initial screening tool within the parameter ranges of the assembled 59-case dataset, enhancing traditional geotechnical design evaluations and field load assessments.</jats:p>
title: GWO-Optimized Machine Learning Models for Ultimate Bearing Capacity Prediction of Driven Piles in Cohesionless Soils

<jats:p>
                    Machine learning is widely applied to metabolomic biomarker discovery, yet systematic comparisons of diverse modeling strategies remain rare, particularly in datasets dominated by severe batch effects. We present a comprehensive and reproducible modeling framework comparing six machine learning approaches for metabolomic classification under extreme technical variation. Using a publicly available metabolomic dataset of five grass species (two barley, two wheat, and one Brachypodium) infected with
                    <jats:italic>Fusarium culmorum</jats:italic>
                    (116 samples, 24 911 features), we address a scenario in which batch effects exceed biological signal by 4.9-fold (R²_batch/R²_treatment = 4.9:1). Our framework integrates: (i) ComBat batch correction to reduce technical variation while preserving biological signal, (ii) robust Median Absolute Deviation (MAD)-based feature prescreening resistant to batch-driven variance, (iii) shrinkage-regularized differential correlation networks (Ledoit-Wolf) to derive stable edge features capturing infection-related metabolite rewiring, (iv) systematic epoch optimization for a shallow neural network baseline, and (v) comprehensive evaluation of six model classes: shallow neural network, elastic net, random forest, XGBoost, SVM with linear kernel, and SVM with RBF kernel. XGBoost achieved the highest observed performance (AUROC = 0.869, 95% BCa CI: 0.700–0.956), but the difference versus the elastic net baseline (AUROC = 0.754, DeLong p = 0.065) did not reach statistical significance. Bootstrap confidence intervals (BCa, 2,000 iterations) and pairwise statistical tests (DeLong, McNemar) provided rigorous model comparisons. While all models showed modest discriminative ability (AUROC range: 0.754–0.869), reflecting the inherent difficulty of classification under severe batch effects with small sample sizes, tree-based ensemble approaches (XGBoost, Random Forest) showed the strongest point estimates for extracting non-linear biological signal from correlation-network-derived edge features. These results demonstrate that principled feature engineering, batch correction, and systematic model comparison can identify meaningful differences in challenging metabolomic datasets, but larger independent cohorts are needed to confirm model ranking. The proposed open-source workflow provides transparent guidance for datasets in which batch effects dominate biological signal in high-dimensional metabolomics and related omics settings.
                  </jats:p>
title: Systematic comparison of machine learning approaches for metabolomic biomarker discovery under severe batch effects: From neural networks to support vector machines

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Recent FinTech credit and risk systems demonstrate a marked tendency to utilize machine learning methodologies; still, conventional evaluation benchmarks focus almost exclusively on predictive accuracy. This narrow focus gives rise to a challenging problem. The present study focuses on the fact that the AI Act and the Fair Credit Reporting Act penalize operational carbon footprints, systemic demographic bias and opaque decision logic. In order to address this evident gap in the literature, an evaluation of algorithmic trade-offs is conducted using the four-pillar S.A.F.E. framework (Sustainability, Accuracy, Fairness, Explainability) across three operational domains. The following subjects will be explored the detection of credit fraud; the corporate ESG rating; and geospatial physical climate risk. We benchmark five diverse architectures an Explainable Stacking Ensemble, Enhanced Random Forest, XGBoost, a Feedforward Neural Network, and a simulated Quantum SVM across 160,000 synthetic records calibrated to Lending Club, MSCI ESG, and NOAA distributions. Nonparametric Friedman tests confirm significant performance divergence among the models (chi-square = 18.24, df = 4,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 0.0011). Although Enhanced Random Forest achieves peak raw accuracy in fraud screening (97.90% ± 0.40%), the Explainable Stacking Ensemble secures the highest composite S.A.F.E. score (9.28/10, Grade A+ ), pairing an F1-score of 0.972 with high TreeSHAP explanation fidelity (0.941). Conversely, the simulated QSVM exhibits a substantial classical latency penalty (145.0 ms/pred). Multi-attribute sensitivity tests across four contrasting stakeholder regimes demonstrate that ensemble superiority remains strictly invariant to policy weighting (
                    <jats:italic>W</jats:italic>
                     = 1.00). These findings provide risk managers and regulators with an empirical roadmap for the deployment of high-performing models that satisfy statutory fairness and environmental mandates.
                  </jats:p>
title: Machine learning models in FinTech for sustainable innovation: a comprehensive empirical evaluation with the S.A.F.E. framework

items.abstract: <jats:p>Metaheuristic optimization experiments produce valuable performance evidence, but their reuse and comparison remain challenging when algorithm configurations, problem instances, computational budgets, stopping criteria, provenance, and performance observations are represented inconsistently. This paper presents the Metaheuristic Experiment Ontology (MEXO), a semantic framework for representing, validating, and reusing optimization experiments through a structured knowledge graph. MEXO distinguishes experimental plans, individual executions, and aggregated performance observations while preserving the contextual information required for meaningful comparisons and downstream machine-learning applications. The framework is evaluated using 200 historical aggregate records, 60 completed runs from an external IOHprofiler archive, and 1080 executed reference-optimizer runs across 12 BBOB benchmark functions, two dimensions, and three instances per function. The evaluation produces 492 campaign-level summary observations and verifies the consistency of metadata and execution traces across 1140 runs. SHACL-based and source-aware validation detect 24 deliberately introduced record corruptions without false alarms on three valid controls. An implemented comparison policy identifies 216 eligible configuration comparisons and 30 cases with insufficient contextual information. Five competency questions produce consistent results across MEXO, an OPTION-based representation, and a relational database. Furthermore, an executable feature–target extraction pipeline generates 216 records for a grouped algorithm-selection experiment, demonstrating the integration of semantically represented optimization evidence with machine learning. The findings establish MEXO as an operational semantic framework supporting experimental traceability, contextual validation, controlled comparison, and machine-learning data preparation, while recognizing that these capabilities can also be implemented using alternative data representations.</jats:p>
title: MEXO: A Semantic Framework for Representing and Validating the Context of Metaheuristic Optimization Experiments

                  <jats:p>
                    Magnetorheological fluids (MRFs) have highly nonlinear and heterogeneous rheological behavior due to complicated magnetic field induced particle interaction. Accurate prediction of yield stress is challenging with conventional global machine learning models. To overcome this, in the present work, we proposed a regime-based nested cross-validation (CV) framework where the dataset was divided into different rheological regimes by
                    <jats:italic>K</jats:italic>
                    -means clustering in the logarithmic yield stress domain. Separate machine learning models were subsequently trained within each regime to better capture localized behavior. The proposed framework was organized in a nested CV scheme, combining feature scaling and hyperparameter optimization with GridSearchCV. The results showed that regime-based modeling was effective in handling data heterogeneity and regime-dependent nonlinearities, leading to improved predictive stability and reduced prediction error compared to conventional global models. In summary, the proposed methodology offers an effective and physically interpretable framework for the prediction of the yield stress behavior of MRFs under different magnetic and material conditions.
                  </jats:p>
title: A regime-based nested CV machine learning model to forecast the magneto-induced mechanical characteristics of a magnetorheological fluid

items.abstract: <jats:p>Configuring a diagnostic before the next shot is an instrumentation problem that grows in importance as high-repetition-rate laser-plasma platforms scale from tens of shots to thousands. In the present campaign, a gated intensified optical camera required shot-to-shot retuning as peak image brightness varied with chamber pressure, laser energy, focus conditions, and target state. Static settings produced under-exposed or over-driven images, while manual tuning consumed shots and reduced measurement efficiency. We treat this problem as machine-learning-guided pre-shot diagnostic configuration using a hybrid framework: archived images and machine variables are reduced to a compact descriptor state, a neural-network surrogate is trained to predict that state from operating conditions and detector settings, and Bayesian optimization inverts the surrogate to recommend executable settings before each shot. On a 1 Hz multi-joule platform, the measured peak signal tracked requested targets from 1000 to 4500 counts with a correlation of 0.92 and a mean absolute error of 15%. These results demonstrate that campaign data can train practical empirical models supporting pre-shot diagnostic configuration for enhanced data quality and experimental efficiency in comparable laser-plasma campaigns.</jats:p>
title: Machine-learning-guided pre-shot diagnostic configuration for high-repetition-rate laser-plasma experiments

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Pediatric sepsis is a life-threatening condition with high mortality, underscoring the need for novel diagnostic biomarkers. Dysregulated RNA processing contributes to sepsis pathogenesis, highlighting the need to investigate its association with pediatric sepsis. Methods: Microarray data and machine learning were used to identify diagnostic biomarkers. Microarray data from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed via Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), and four algorithms (Boruta, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), Support Vector Machine - Recursive Feature Elimination (SVM-RFE), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost)) screened feature genes. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using a nomogram, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Immune infiltration was assessed with Cell-type Identification By Estimating Relative Subsets Of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT), molecular subtyping with ConsensusClusterPlus, and pathways through gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). Results: Five diagnostic biomarkers (TDRD9, SRSF8, EXOSC4, DPH3, USB1) were identified. The nomogram showed promising diagnostic performance (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) >0.86), and exploratory consistency patterns were observed in three related pediatric sepsis external datasets. Immune analysis revealed neutrophil/monocyte dominance. Molecular subtyping in the training cohort revealed two potential subtypes with distinct immune profiles, which warrant further validation in independent cohorts. Conclusion: Collectively, we developed and internally evaluated a five-gene signature associated with RNA processing, which showed high discrimination between sepsis samples and healthy controls in the training cohort. Furthermore, exploratory subtype analysis performed in the training cohort revealed two distinct immune-related clusters, providing preliminary insights into the heterogeneity of sepsis.</jats:p>
title: Machine Learning-Based Identification of RNA Processing-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers and Molecular Subtypes in Pediatric Sepsis

                  <jats:p>Mapping microstructural features is vital to developing next-generation materials in renewable energy applications. However, the nanometer-scale dimensions, chemical heterogeneity, and beam sensitivity of these materials make their structural characterization exceptionally challenging. Here, we present a data acquisition and analysis workflow for four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) applied to a beam-sensitive lithium-metal filament sample with a surface passivation layer. By combining data dimensionality reduction with unsupervised machine-learning approaches, we perform real-space clustering to enhance signal-to-noise ratios across large data sets. Automated Bragg reflection analysis was then used to identify distinct crystallographic phases within the surface passivation layer. This approach enables nanoscale phase mapping of dominant species across large fields of view with nanometer-level lateral resolution. We identify lithium oxide and lithium hydroxide as the predominant crystalline phases in the lithium-metal surface passivation layer.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">In electronic devices such as automotive LED lighting and digital screen applications, LDO (Low Drop-Out) or linear regulators are important components used as power supplies. Linear converters regulate the DC voltage by reducing it to a lower DC voltage level with the a dissipation mechanism. Since they constantly dissipate power in the form of heat, their efficiency is low. Linear converters generally need a heatsink, so they are larger and heavier. Conversely, they have simpler design and manufacturing structure with more cost-effective. They have less ripple and noise at the output. In this study, the advantages and disadvantages of linear converters were discussed and their thermal problems were detailed, with recommendations to solve the thermal problems. Thermal problems in these structures were analyzed by aid of Siemens FloEFD software for a linear converter designed with 9.6W output power driven by eight MOSFETs with 28 V input and 12 V output voltage. The thermal measurements taken by a thermal camera were presented for the designed and manufactured linear converter to prove the consistency of measurement and simulation results. The thermal characteristics of the designed circuits were obtained in light of the analysis and the minimum dimensions for long-term stability were studied and four different methods were presented to solve the thermal problems: increasing the surface area, decreasing the power per MOSFET by increasing the number of MOSFETs, adding a heatsink and substituting a switched-mode DC-DC converter instead of a linear converter.</jats:p>
title: Design, Thermal Analysis and Implementation of a Linear Converter

items.abstract: <jats:p>Forecasting with machine learning often goes wrong due to the protocol and not the algorithms for reasons including leakage, model selection on the test sample, no naive benchmark, and no allowance for the number of models tried. 4Cast Lab is a free, open-source, single-file application that makes a benchmark-first protocol the default: time-ordered splits; selection by cross-validation inside the training period; one use of the Test Set; a naive benchmark with Diebold–Mariano and Clark–West tests; and the Holm, Reality Check, SPA and Model Confidence Set procedures. We document the protocol, the leakage controls and the fixed rules of the AutoML verdict, and report three kinds of evidence. A four-stage benchmark against certified values and reference software shows agreement to at least six significant digits and pre-specified equivalence tests for the random learners. A simulation run through the application shows that, for random-walk targets, common reporting rules declare a false success in 21 to 95% of cases and the benchmark-first verdict in 0 to 1%, at a measured cost in power. On 59 M4 monthly series and the US unemployment rate, the application matches MLForecast for like learners and approaches StatsForecast once the target is differenced.</jats:p>
title: 4Cast Lab: Open-Source App for Machine Learning and Statistical Analysis

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper investigates the leakage current in wall bushings of flexible HVDC systems caused by high‐frequency electromagnetic interference from modular multilevel converters. First, an analysis based on on‐site measurements and wideband impedance is carried out, with emphasis on the influence of high‐frequency parameters such as stray capacitance and inductance. A wideband equivalent circuit model of the wall bushing and other main equipment is established. On this basis, the high‐frequency voltage components and their spectral characteristics generated during the switching process of the modular multilevel converter sub‐modules are further analyzed. By constructing a model of the electromagnetic interference conduction path, the frequency‐domain transmission characteristics are analyzed, the resonant circuit is identified, and it is clarified that the high‐frequency oscillation of the modular multilevel converter is the main cause of the leakage current on the wall bushing. The time‐domain waveform and the resulting thermal loss are also analyzed. The results show that reducing the stray capacitance of the bushing to the ground can effectively suppress the leakage current. This study provides theoretical and practical support for leakage current mitigation and insulation design of wall bushings under high‐frequency interference.</jats:p>
title: Analysis of High‐Frequency Leakage Current Characteristics of Wall Bushing in VSC‐HVDC Converter System

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Scientific collaboration is a temporal process: researchers form, strengthen and let lapse collaborations over time, and external shocks perturb the network. Here, we present a reproducible benchmark of dynamic graph neural networks for link forecasting on a large open co-authorship corpus. We use OpenAlex (data snapshot of 22–23 September 2026) across six disciplines—condensed matter physics, genetics, epidemiology, organic chemistry, artificial intelligence, and language and linguistics—spanning 2000–2025. Using strict temporal splits with no future-information leakage, we compare three dynamic architectures (temporal graph convolutional network (T-GCN), dynamic graph convolutional network (DGCN) and EvolveGCN with the output variant (EvolveGCN-O)), a temporal-attention baseline (dynamic self-attention network (DySAT)) and three static baselines, under a rolling-origin evaluation with three temporal cuts and three random seeds. T-GCN achieves the best area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR) (0.777 and 0.978, respectively), outperforming the strongest static baseline by 8.7% and the next-best model excluding the scale-limited DySAT reference—a gated recurrent unit (GRU)-cell EvolveGCN ablation—by 4.7 AUC points. Clustering the best model's embeddings reveals three collaboration archetypes—core contributors, community bridges and peripheral specialists—that are stable across random seeds (multi-seed adjusted Rand index (ARI) 0.998), independent model retrainings (cross-embedding ARI 0.85), and partially across clustering methods (k-means versus agglomerative ARI 0.52; spectral clustering does not recover the partition), and exhibit substantial between-archetype mobility; they are therefore presented as exploratory.A COVID-19 case study using synthetic control and difference-in-differences illustrates how the framework can estimate associations between external shocks and cross-disciplinary collaboration; these estimates are associational, not causal, and the headline result is a placebo-validated null. All data and code are openly available.</jats:p>
title: Dynamic graph neural networks for open-source scientific collaboration networks

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Polish bezpieczeństwo presents a challenge for bilingual dictionary design: its English equivalents, safety and security, are often distinguished by information carried in the complete Polish expression. The study aligns 224 occurrences from 221 Polish-language journal titles with their indexed English-title realisations in Scopus (2015–2026). Annotation covered the complete Polish expression, English realisation, collocational pattern, correspondence status, and contextual evidence. An independent coder recoded 45 units (20.1%), yielding 91.1% agreement and Cohen’s κ = .82. Safety accounted for 56.7% of units, security-based forms for 41.5%, and specialist whole-expression realisations for 1.8%. Among 220 safety- and security-based alignments, 69.5% were conventional, 26.4% context-conditioned, and 4.1% divergent. Phrase-level morphology and recurrent combinations frequently constrained equivalent choice, while broader expressions required contextual discrimination. The findings support source-language guidance for equivalent selection in an encoding-oriented Polish-English entry. The proposed entry combines direct multiword equivalents, Polish-language meaning cues, and cross-references for contrastive expressions; its usefulness for dictionary users remains to be tested.</jats:p>
title: Discriminating English equivalents of Polish bezpieczeństwo : Source-language cues from bilingual academic titles

items.abstract: <jats:p>Multiple neighboring high-current conductors are frequently routed close together in electric-vehicle distribution units and charging installations, where their magnetic fields perturb non-contact current sensors. This paper investigates a reduced-order equivalent-offset representation of simultaneous multi-conductor interference using a six-element semicircular Hall/tunnel-magnetoresistance (TMR) array. The Biot–Savart fields are superimposed vectorially and projected onto the calibrated sensor axes. Normalized six-channel responses identify a two-coordinate equivalent position without supplying the target current to the position fit; a separate absolute-amplitude estimate then reconstructs current. The method is evaluated under explicitly defined in-array, external, mixed, opposing-polarity and four-interferer geometries. In a reproducible 20–200 A numerical sweep, the in-array mean absolute percentage error decreases from 16.57% to 11.89%, and the external-interference error decreases from 2.22% to 0.09%, relative to centered-conductor reconstruction. Across 96 additional vector-model cases, the equivalent-field residual and current error show only moderate correlation (Pearson r = 0.41), identifying the limitations of single-source equivalence. An STM32F103 implementation required approximately 70–80 ms per update. The numerical analysis characterizes the geometry-dependent accuracy of equivalent-offset compensation, while the processor test demonstrates its embedded computational feasibility.</jats:p>
title: Equivalent-Offset Modeling for Multi-Source Magnetic Interference Compensation in Non-Contact Current Sensing with a Semicircular Hall/TMR Array

items.abstract: <jats:p>Separated source–channel coding of unmanned aerial vehicle video fails abruptly below the channel-code threshold. We study frame-wise joint source–channel coding with frozen-detector feature distillation on a compact 5.5 M-parameter codec and, adding DINOv2 and SigLIP terms, a 28.2 M SwinJSCC-scale codec. In six seeded matched pairs at identical capacity and SNR =20 dB, a structural-plus-detector objective raises DINOv2 class-token similarity, a metric outside that objective, by +0.122 (95% CI [+0.108,+0.137]) over plain MSE. The structural MS-SSIM term carries most of it, +0.099; in the larger codec’s final training stage, the detector term buys no robustness. The larger codec degrades continuously under noise and latent-domain jamming, where a JPEG plus rate-1/2 LDPC reference fails, and under symbol erasure; an erasure-augmented variant holds a similarity of 0.963, with no frame below 0.85, at 30% loss. In the latent domain at SNR =20 dB and nominal JNR =10 dB, open-loop jammers cost at most 0.008, and the reactive jammer, with 5.6× an equal-JNR barrage’s power, costs 0.383. A simplified frequency-domain OFDM simulation reverses this ordering, for reasons not established, and latent-domain reactive-jamming augmentation does not transfer. Detector agreement supports the metric as a task surrogate only; for the larger codec, it shares a model family with a loss term. Results support graceful degradation in simulation.</jats:p>
title: Goal-Oriented Joint Source–Channel Coding for UAV Reconnaissance Video Under Contested RF Channels with Detector-Feature Distillation

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The growth of artificial intelligence in marketing has introduced AI-generated word of mouth (AiWOM) alongside influencer eWOM (IeWOM). Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) framework and Source Credibility Theory (SCT), this study compares the effects of AiWOM and IeWOM on purchase intention (PI) and examines the mediating role of source credibility.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional survey was conducted with a verified sample of 562 active digital consumers aged 18 to 45 in Palestine, recruited through a combination of purposive and snowball sampling. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4, and the differences between the two sources were tested with bootstrapped paired-difference tests.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Both human influencers and AI sources positively affected source credibility, but human influencers exerted a statistically significantly stronger effect on source credibility and purchase intention. Source credibility functioned as a complementary partial mediator for both IeWOM and AiWOM, with significant indirect effects coexisting with significant direct effects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Human influencers remain the more persuasive force in digital marketing, although AiWOM represents a viable emerging channel. By providing a formal, same-sample statistical comparison of human and AI eWOM within an integrated SOR-SCT model in an under-researched collectivist market, the study suggests that marketers should anchor credibility-building in human influencers while deploying AiWOM as a complementary, scalable channel.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: AiWOM vs. influencer eWOM: an SOR perspective on source credibility and purchase intention

items.abstract: <jats:p>Interlinking converters of hybrid AC/DC microgrids are increasingly expected to improve power quality (PQ) in addition to transferring power. This paper analyses the performance and limits of current-controlled voltage source converters (CC-VSCs) used for this purpose. A small-signal dq model including the DC-link/current-loop coupling is derived; linear, nonlinear and predictive current controllers are reviewed, and four of them are benchmarked on one identical switched model of a 400 V weak-grid microgrid with nonlinear loads and 10 kW of DC-side injection. Without compensation, the grid-current total demand distortion (TDD) is 17.6 %. Hysteresis and finite-control-set model predictive control reduce it to 2.1 % and 2.3 % at average switching frequencies below 4 kHz, whereas proportional-resonant control reaches 5.7 % and synchronous-frame PI 13.3 %. Four limitations are quantified: instability of an undamped LCL loop beyond 0.6 mH of grid inductance, a trade-off between DC-bus regulation speed and low-order harmonic injection, PLL degradation, and current saturation, where simple limiting either exceeds the rating by 18 % or leaves 29 % of the capacity unused. Design guidelines and research directions are derived.</jats:p>
title: Current-Controlled Voltage Source Converters for Power Quality Improvement in Hybrid Microgrids: Performance and Limitations

items.abstract: <jats:p>Reliably locating airborne chemicals is critical for environmental sensing. Robotic odor source localization (OSL) combines gas and airflow sensing, but implementation on small quadrotors remains difficult due to strict payload constraints. This work presents a 50.8 g Crazyflie‐class quadrotor equipped with a crash‐resistant, multi‐axis airflow sensor and metal‐oxide gas sensor. The system combines a scalar wind residual, computed by fusing airflow‐sensor magnitude and onboard ground‐speed estimates, with bout‐based processing of the gas signal. Importantly, the residual enables ambient wind presence detection at wind speeds below the quadrotor’s flight speed when travel is perpendicular to airflow for OSL in low wind environments. These cues trigger wind servoing, a control strategy that converts apparent airflow direction to in‐plane velocity commands for rapid plume tracking. The system is evaluated using ethanol plumes in fixed indoor flow, shifting indoor flow, and naturally occurring outdoor wind. Indoors, the quadrotor consistently acquires the plume and traces it upwind across a range of initial conditions. Outdoors, the system demonstrates feasibility, with performance limited primarily by rapid ambient wind direction shifts, establishing clear targets for future work.</jats:p>
title: Onboard Airflow Sensing for Odor Source Localization on a 50 g Quadrotor

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Doctor-patient trust is a core issue in building a harmonious doctor-patient relationship. Trust of patients in doctors not only includes personalized special trust but also general trust. The public obtains medical information directly through offline medical experiences, which enhance doctor-patient familiarity and establish interpersonal doctor-patient trust. The process of establishing universal trust is influenced more by indirect medical information obtained through online communication channels. When the public obtains medical information directly through offline medical experience, professional workers often use rational persuasion that is difficult for the public to understand, thus making it difficult to have a substantial impact. With the continuous promotion and application of the Internet, the dissemination of information on the Internet will have an increasing impact on the mentality and even the behavior of the public. This raises the research question in this article. From the perspective of the various channels to acquire medical information, can public acquisition of online medical information and medical experience have an impact on patient trust? Specifically, through what mechanisms do online medical information and medical experience affect patient trust? Is there a difference in the impact of the two medical information acquisition channels on patient trust? Previous research does not provide any answers. In order to answer the above questions, this article is based on data from the Comprehensive Survey of Social Conditions in China (CSS2017). First, it analyzes the patient trust structure and constructs the patient trust variables through doctor trust and hospital trust. Starting from various sources of medical information, it explores the impact of the acquisition of online information and offline medical experience on patient trust, the specific impact mechanisms, and the different impact effects. Research finds that, first, there is a complementarity between the trust of Chinese patients and the mutual influence of internal doctor trust and hospital trust. Second, from the perspective of the Internet channels, public access to medical information through online media can reduce patient trust. Further analysis shows that public perceptions of medical risks play a positive mediating role in this mechanism. Third, from the perspective of offline medical channels, public medical experience has an enhancing effect on patient trust, and mechanism analysis suggests that institutional perceptions play a partial mediating role. Fourth, by comparing the various sources of medical information, it is found that the impact of public access to online medical information on patient trust is stronger than the impact of offline medical experience. Compared to medical workers, the public is more willing to trust medical information from the Internet, indicating that there is an “asymmetry” in patient trust. Therefore, to enhance patient trust, it is necessary for the government to enhance the “contact effects” between healthcare providers and patients, to standardize media promotion and establish correct medical concepts from the perspective of Internet media, and to build a doctor-patient community from the perspective of multi-party collaborative governance in order to enhance patient trust and to achieve effective governance of doctor-patient relationships.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: How Does the Source of Medical Information Affect Patient Trust: A Comparative Analysis Based on Online Media and Medical Experience

items.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid urban expansion and polycentric development create challenges for understanding how flexible transport interacts with changing urban structures. This research develops a two-stage framework that independently identifies urban contexts before introducing taxi GPS as a dynamic sensing layer. Using Bangkok as a case study, approximately 30 years of satellite imagery, POIs and transport-network data were integrated to identify morphological and functional centers. One month of taxi GPS data was subsequently used to examine spatial and temporal patterns of taxi operations. The analysis identified 23 urban centers, revealing that morphological and functional centrality do not necessarily coincide. Taxi presence and movement were more concentrated in integrated urban centers and areas surrounding public-transport facilities, whereas stopping and waiting activities exhibited distinct spatial and temporal patterns. These findings demonstrate the potential of GPS-based mobility analysis to inform context-responsive built-environment planning, strengthen public-transport integration and support adaptive smart mobility planning and governance.</jats:p>
title: A Multi-Source Framework Integrating Urban Centrality and Taxi Mobility Dynamics for Smart Mobility Planning

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Pilocytic astrocytoma is the most common brain tumor in children and is typically classified as a low-grade (WHO grade 1) glioma. Gamma Knife Radiosurgery (GKRS) is a minimally invasive treatment modality designed to maximize local tumor control while preserving surrounding healthy tissue, particularly in lesions located in surgically challenging regions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of GKRS in pediatric pilocytic astrocytoma.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases was conducted for studies published between January 1994 and September 2024, following PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included at least four patients with pilocytic astrocytoma and reported outcomes such as tumor regression, control rates, or safety. Data were pooled using a random-effects model with single-proportion analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Four studies including 101 pediatric patients were analyzed (three retrospective, one prospective). Males predominated (62.4%), with a mean age of 10.5 years. Tumors were most frequently located in the brainstem (n = 29) and cerebellum (n = 28), with mean volumes of 2.1–3.3 cm³. Prior surgery was reported in 51 patients (50.5%), radiotherapy in 12 (11.9%), and chemotherapy in one patient. Overall, GKRS was used mainly as an adjuvant or salvage treatment, serving as first-line therapy in ∼20% of cases. Prescription doses ranged from 9 to 28 Gy, and the mean follow-up was 91 months. Complete regression occurred in 16% (95% CI 0.06–0.34; I² = 65%) and partial regression in 54% (95% CI 0.35–0.71; I² = 63%), yielding overall tumor control in 96% (95% CI 0.77–0.99; I² = 0%). Cyst progression occurred in 17% (95% CI 0.11–0.25; I² = 0%), while solid progression was rare (2%; 95% CI 0.01–0.09; I² = 35%). Favorable neurological outcomes were seen in 98% (95% CI 0.89–1.00), and mortality was 2% (95% CI 0.01–0.09; I² = 0%).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GKRS appears to be a safe and effective treatment option for pediatric pilocytic astrocytoma, providing high tumor control rates with minimal progression of solid components. Although complete regression is relatively uncommon via GKRS, commonly attributed to intrinsic tumor factors – such as cystic components, larger volume, deep or eloquent location, and slow biological growth –, the high rates of disease control and minimally invasive profile support its role as an important adjunct or alternative therapy in selected patients.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: 1014 Gamma Knife Radiosurgery in the Management of Pediatric Pilocytic Astrocytoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on safety and efficacy

items.abstract: <jats:p>A biosensor quantifies an analyte; identifying its biological source requires information about production, removal, transport, and sampling context. This Perspective proposes a mechanistic hierarchy that connects enzymatic sources and oxidant-transforming pathways with reactive species, reversible relays, and persistent molecular modifications. Tissue, compartment, and temporal coordinates qualify the contribution of each observation. NADPH oxidase–nitric oxide synthase interactions illustrate how oxidant generation, nitric oxide consumption, cofactor availability, and nitration provide complementary constraints. The xanthine oxidase/dehydrogenase axis extends the framework to enzyme interconversion, oxygen-dependent product partitioning, and spatial separation between enzyme synthesis and action. A heuristic score organizes source-oriented evidence, accompanied by qualified evidence coverage and reference anchoring. A prospective mechanistically constrained AI model would integrate continuous sensor streams, intermittent assays, physiological perturbations, and covariates to estimate compatible source configurations and their uncertainty. Attribution depends on whether the combined observations distinguish competing explanations; abstention identifies the additional measurement needed to resolve an ambiguous case. An illustrative vascular panel makes these requirements concrete. The immediate contribution is a testable strategy for panel construction and mechanistic interpretation. Translation toward source-informed therapeutic prioritization proceeds through analytical validation, biological attribution, clinical validity, and demonstrated clinical utility.</jats:p>
title: Which redox source, where, and when? AI-guided precision biosensing through mechanistic hierarchy

items.abstract: <jats:p>P. frutescens seeds are increasingly recognized not only for their favorable lipid composition but also as a source of bioactive phenolic acids, particularly rosmarinic acid and caffeic acid. Historically, the biological activities of these compounds have been investigated primarily using in vitro radical-scavenging assays. However, this conventional antioxidant-centered approach does not adequately reflect their potential physiological effects, particularly in light of the limited systemic bioavailability and extensive intestinal and hepatic metabolism of dietary phenolic acids. This critical narrative review re-evaluates the biological activities of perilla seed phenolic acids, proposing a shift from the conventional view of these compounds as direct antioxidants toward their potential roles as xenohormetic modulators of cellular signaling pathways. Specifically, we critically synthesize evidence suggesting that these phenolic acids and their metabolites may influence cellular redox homeostasis and inflammatory responses through the activation of the nuclear factor erythroid 2–related factor 2/antioxidant response element (Nrf2/ARE) pathway and the modulation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways. By integrating evidence on phytochemical composition, bioavailability, metabolism, and molecular mechanisms, this review offers a mechanistically informed framework for understanding the potential relevance of perilla seed phenolic acids to the prevention and dietary management of metabolic disorders characterized by oxidative stress and chronic inflammation.</jats:p>
title: Perilla frutescens Seeds as a Source of Bioactive Phenolic Acids: A Critical Narrative Review of Redox Signaling and Molecular Mechanisms

items.abstract: <jats:p>Indian fast moving consumer goods firms face growing pressure from regulators, investors, and consumers to reduce plastic packaging waste, reinforced by mandatory disclosure under SEBI’s BRSR Core framework and Extended Producer Responsibility rules. This comparative case study evaluates two contrasting strategies: Godrej Consumer Products (GCPL), which redesigns packaging at source, and Hindustan Unilever (HUL), which relies on collection and offset. The analysis combines BRSR Core disclosures, integrated annual reports, and audited financial statements for fiscal 2022/23 to 2024/25 with a consumer survey (n = 134) and one interview with an HUL manager. The two firms are benchmarked on seven dimensions: ESG progress, collection performance, cost efficiency, financial performance, regulatory risk, consumer perception, and disclosure quality. A scenario analysis projects outcomes to 2030. GCPL closed about 80% of the gap to its near term recyclability target at a much lower estimated cost per point of progress, while HUL closed 26.4% of the gap to its recycled content target. GCPL’s progress coincided with a fall in net profit margin from 19.74% to 13.49%, whereas HUL’s margins stayed stable. Estimated penalty exposure is small for both firms today, but HUL’s would rise roughly tenfold if its progress stalled. Neither strategy wins on every dimension: GCPL leads on five of seven and HUL on financial performance and consumer perception. Several HUL figures are estimates and the financial comparison is descriptive rather than causal. The study offers a replicable benchmarking and scenario framework and recommends that firms choose between redesign and collection according to packaging format, regulatory runway, and brand position.</jats:p>
title: The price of green: Comparing source redesign and collection and offset packaging strategies at Godrej consumer products and Hindustan Unilever

                    A thermoelectric generator (TEG) incorporated with solar‐driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE) exploits evaporation‐induced temperature gradients to coproduce water and electricity, representing a promising approach to address the limitations of conventional systems. Despite extensive efforts toward enhancing solar‐thermal conversion, the temperature difference remains limited due to heat conduction, while the high dependence on solar input significantly restricts the application scope. Herein, we report a 3D inverted water‐electricity coproduction (IWEC‐3D) system based on a polyvinyl alcohol aerogel photothermal layer. This highly hydrophilic aerogel and 3D structure enlarge the temperature gradient of the TEG while maintaining rapid water transport. The inverted structure not only enhances the performance but also facilitates the utilization of low‐temperature waste heat as an energy input source for the system. items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Energy-efficient neuromorphic computing at the edge requires simulation tools that can capture the non-ideal behavior of mixed-signal spiking neural network (SNN) hardware while supporting system-level design exploration.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This work presents an open-source hardware-aware simulation framework for mixed-signal SNNs that enables comparative analysis across neuron, synapse and architecture choices. The framework supports multiple neuron models, including Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF), Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) and Axon-Hillock (AH), together with non-volatile analog synapses based on floating-gate transistors and ReRAM devices. By incorporating device-level non-linearities directly into PyTorch-based training and inference, the tool enables optimization of physical synaptic parameters rather than idealized abstract weights.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The framework is evaluated on standard neuromorphic benchmarks, including N-MNIST, DVS Gesture and Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD). For each model dataset configuration, it reports classification accuracy together with hardware-oriented metrics such as silicon area, power consumption and quantization sensitivity. In addition, mismatch analysis has been implemented to capture the impact of real silicon fabrication-based effects, such as device-to-device and transistor-level variability, on network behavior.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These capabilities enable cross-layer design space exploration and help identify neuron-synapse configurations that best satisfy application-specific constraints on accuracy, energy efficiency, area and hardware fidelity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: A hardware-aware open-source framework for design space exploration of mixed-signal spiking neural networks

                    Stochastic computing encodes numbers as probabilistic bit streams and reduces multiplication to a single logic gate, which makes it an appealing arithmetic substrate for always-on biomedical inference under severe energy constraints. Its accuracy is bounded by two effects usually treated as global properties of a design: the inverse square-root convergence of stream-based estimates, and the systematic bias introduced when operand streams are correlated. This article proceeds from a different observation, namely, that the accuracy cost of stochastic approximation is not distributed uniformly across the layers of a network, and that precision should be allocated where measurement shows it is required. We define a layer-wise stochastic sensitivity metric that isolates the accuracy attributable to mapping each individual layer into the stochastic domain, and develop a partitioning procedure that converts the resulting profile into a hybrid binary–stochastic assignment while reporting the retained fraction of stochastic computation as an explicit hardware-cost proxy. The methodology is demonstrated on an 8–12–8–4–1 fully connected classifier trained on the PIMA Indian Diabetes dataset under a leakage-free preprocessing protocol. Profiling reveals a strongly concentrated sensitivity distribution, the second hidden layer alone accounting for an 11.9 percentage-point accuracy loss while the output layer is statistically indistinguishable from exact arithmetic, and excluding that layer alone recovers 5.0 percentage points while retaining

                    of all multiply–accumulate operations in stochastic form. A controlled comparison of independent and shared stochastic number generators demonstrates a correlation-induced error floor that does not diminish with stream length, the implemented bank holding a stochastic cross-correlation of approximately 0.038 independently of length; classifier AUC accordingly remains flat with the generators as implemented but rises toward the exact reference with idealised generators. All four arithmetic partitions were placed and routed for a Xilinx Zynq-7000 device with power annotated from simulated switching activity. items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Objective: This study aimed to assess the vaccination status of children whose parents refused vaccination in the Rize Central District and to explore the underlying reasons for parental refusal.Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in June- December 2023, using vaccination records of 80 children obtained from the Public Health Management System and phone interviews with their parents in the Rize Central District who had refused childhood vaccination during 2021 and 2022. Descriptive statistics, univariate analyses and logistic regression analyses were used to examine vaccination status and related factors.Results: Among the children, 28.8% had never been vaccinated, while 71.2% were partially vaccinated. The most common reasons for vaccine refusal included distrust in vaccines, concerns about side effects, beliefs that vaccines are unnecessary or harmful, and personal research. In the univariate analyses, reporting religious groups and television/radio broadcasts as sources of information was significantly associated with complete non-vaccination. In addition, identifying religious groups as an information source was associated with a significantly higher likelihood of the child being completely unvaccinated (odds raito: 6.7, p=0.036). No significant associations were found with parental education level, income level, number of children in the family, or birth order.Conclusion: These findings suggest that communication strategies involving healthcare professionals and community actors may be important when addressing vaccine refusal.</jats:p>
title: Characteristics of families refusing vaccination and factors associated with vaccine refusal: A cross-sectional study in Rize

items.abstract: <jats:p>Urban environments face increasing biodiversity loss, highlighting the need for accessible and scalable tools to monitor insect communities. This study presents a low-cost, do-it-yourself (DIY), AI-assisted camera system designed to automate insect observations and explore the feasibility of estimating morphospecies-based biodiversity indices in urban environments. The system integrates a camera, low-power computing components, and artificial intelligence algorithms for image acquisition and processing. Field observations were conducted to evaluate its performance by comparing automated image-based detections with independent visual assessments performed by trained entomologists. The system enabled continuous image acquisition and the detection of insect morphospecies visiting an artificial sampling platform, providing preliminary data for estimating biodiversity metrics, including morphospecies richness and diversity indices. Overall, the findings suggest that this affordable, AI-assisted approach may complement conventional entomological surveys by facilitating repeated observations and preliminary assessments of insect diversity. Future studies are envisioned across different habitats, seasons, and insect assemblages to establish its reliability and broader applicability.</jats:p>
title: BioTrap OpenVision: An Open-Source Edge AI System for Non-Invasive Insect Biodiversity Monitoring

                    The red bed reservoirs in the first member of Kongdian Formation (E
                    <jats:sub>k1</jats:sub>
                    ) in the Wangjiagang area, Dongying Depression, exhibit significant exploration potential. However, poorly understood charging mechanisms pose challenges to predictive exploration and trap assessment. The study integrates biomarker analysis, fluid inclusion microthermometry, burial-thermal history reconstruction, and structural analysis to elucidate these mechanisms. Quantitative end-member mixing analysis reveals that E
                    <jats:sub>k1</jats:sub>
                    crude oil is mainly derived from the lower fourth member of Shahejie (45%) and second member of Kongdian Formation (40%) source rocks (C
                    <jats:sub>35</jats:sub>

                    <jats:sub>30</jats:sub>
                    hopane <0.7, Pr/Ph=0.5-0.7) with minor contribution from the upper fourth member of Shahejie Formation source rock (15%). Bimodal hydrocarbon charging events occurred during the deposition of the Dongying (Ed, 65-75°C) and Minghuazhen (Nm, 85-110 °C) Formations. Petroleum ascended vertically via source-connected faults and subsequently propagated laterally into red-bed traps through the carrier-bed networks. The red bed oil accumulation is controlled by: (1) trap formation timing (NE-trending faults ceasing activity by the end of E
                    <jats:sub>s1</jats:sub>
                    times period (74% reservoir probability)), (2) distance to structural ridges (<0.5 km for high oil shows), and fault lateral integrity, which is quantitatively thresholded by a Shale Gouge Ratio (SGR) exceeding 0.7 and a vertical throw surpassing 60 m. A two-stage charging-structural ridge-fault sealing accumulation model is proposed, which explains the mixed oil source of E
                    <jats:sub>k1</jats:sub>
                    red beds and quantifies the key controlling factors for high-precision exploration. The refined accumulation model and quantified thresholds established herein offer a predictive template for exploring deep-seated red-bed systems in analogous rift basins globally.

items.abstract: <jats:p>Effective environmental policymaking requires accurate quantification of how changes in emissions impact air quality. Chemical transport models, such as GEOS-Chem, are widely used for such analysis. Traditional methods to compute the relative influence of a change in emissions, or the sensitivity of pollutant concentrations to a change in emissions, with these models often suffer from numerical inaccuracies, especially when evaluating nonlinear atmospheric processes. To overcome these limitations, we integrated a novel sensitivity analysis approach leveraging hyperdual numbers into GEOS-Chem, making GEOS-Chem-hyd. The hyperdual step method accurately calculates first- and second-order sensitivities simultaneously and avoids common numerical errors associated with traditional finite difference methods. The real concentrations as well as first- and second-order sensitivities with respect to emissions calculated with GEOS-Chem-hyd align with the values calculated with GEOS-Chem version 14.0.0-rc.3 within expected error. GEOS-Chem-hyd is applied to assess how changes in emissions of nitrogen oxides can alter ozone, particulate matter, ammonium, and biogenic organic aerosol concentrations, demonstrating regional differences and nonlinear influences. As an example of regional variations, the relative influence of increasing nitrogen oxide emissions was to decrease biogenic organic aerosol concentrations in most areas, except in portions of the boreal forests in Siberia. The nonlinear influence of emissions of nitrogen oxides on ozone, ammonium, and biogenic organic aerosol was evidenced by second-order sensitivities on the same order of magnitude as the first-order sensitivities. GEOS-Chem-hyd incurs approximately four times greater computational costs than GEOS-Chem, which is competitive with the three GEOS-Chem model executions required for less accurate second-order sensitivities using the central finite difference method. GEOS-Chem-hyd provides a framework for efficient assessment of the influence of new scientific modules, which are easily incorporated into the sensitivity analysis framework, and supports informed emission control policy development through accurate, source-oriented sensitivity analysis.</jats:p>
title: GEOS-Chem-hyd: enabling source-oriented sensitivity  analysis with GEOS-Chem

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Potassium (K) is essential for maintaining cellular and physiological functions, and disturbances in K homeostasis can lead to conditions such as cardiac diseases in clinical practice. In this study, we examined the δ41K values in serum, urine, and various organs from five groups of Sprague-Dawley rats subjected to different conditions of K homeostasis, including varying dietary K intake and diuretic treatments (furosemide and spironolactone). Our results show K isotopic variability throughout different rat organs, with δ41K spanning up to 1.7‰. Compared with the skeletal muscle, which is the major intracellular K+ pool in the rat body, the heart is enriched in 41 K (Δ41Kheart-muscle = 0.57 ± 0.29‰), whereas the spinal cord fluid is enriched in 39 K (Δ41Kspinal cord fluid-muscle = −1.25 ± 0.81‰). We interpreted tissue K isotope fractionation within an electrochemical pump-leak model, which links membrane electrochemical conditions to the relative K⁺ efflux and influx. Notably, changes in serum δ⁴¹K were observed before K⁺ concentrations deviated from the clinical reference range in the hypokalemia group, which need to be verified by more rigorous experiments in the future. This work suggests that stable K isotopes may provide a potential indicator of dynamic K⁺ regulation across intracellular and extracellular compartments.</jats:p>
title: Potassium Isotope Fractionation as a Dynamic Signature of Transcellular K⁺ Transport: Mechanisms and Implications for Systemic K Homeostasis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Shallow polyhalite potash ore hosted in the Lower–Middle Triassic evaporites of the Quxian area, northeastern Sichuan Basin, has been known since the 1980s. The uncertainty regarding its genesis has hindered the exploration of marine potash deposits in the study area and elsewhere worldwide. Sedimentological and sulfur isotope analyses of the newly drilled well LJ1 core were carried out. Four microfabric types of polyhalite (PM1–PM4) are recognized within four types of polyhalite rock. Their δ34S values average 29.7 ‰, consistent with globally high Early Triassic values and indicating a 34S-enriched seawater source. The microfabric types record multi-stage sedimentation and a genetic model of the study area polyhalite is established. Fine-grained polyhalite (PM1) represents primary or penecontemporaneous origin, formed by the K+- and Mg2+-rich brine supplied from the adjacent areas mixed with the Ca2+ and SO42−-rich brine formed by in situ evaporation. Fibrous (PM2) and metasomatic relict-textured (PM4) polyhalite formed later at polyhalite–anhydrite contacts through metasomatism. Prismatic polyhalite (PM3) formed in both settings. The comparison of sulfur isotopes among different minerals and among evaporites from different regions provides important evidence for the sources of the ore-forming material and further verifies the above-mentioned genetic model.</jats:p>
title: Genesis of the Triassic Polyhalite in the Quxian Area, Northeastern Sichuan Basin, China: Evidence from Sedimentary Characteristics and Evaporite Sulfur Isotope Geochemistry

items.abstract: <jats:p>In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly reshaped language services, particularly translation practices. By integrating AI technologies into source text (ST) analysis and target text (TT) production, contemporary systems have improved both the speed and consistency of translation workflows, thereby increasing the accessibility of information across linguistic boundaries. As demand for rapid and accurate digital communication continues to grow, AI-enabled machine translation tools have become central to how organizations and individuals manage multilingual content. Nevertheless, despite their efficiency, these systems often struggle to fully capture cultural nuances, pragmatic context, and meaning that depends on subtle linguistic or situational cues. This study examines the multifaceted impact of AI on translation, focusing on the benefits of technological advancement alongside its limitations in producing contextually and culturally resonant target texts. Ultimately, the paper emphasizes the importance of understanding how AI and human expertise can complement each other to support high-quality translations that effectively engage diverse audiences</jats:p>
title: The Impact of AI on Target Text Production

                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The co-production of public goods and services by public organizations and individuals is a common phenomenon in public management, and co-production studies have recently been a hot issue in public management research. However, previous research has not paid sufficient attention to the information asymmetry between public organizations and individuals, and how information affects the decision to deliver public goods and services to individuals of different races. This paper presents four articles published in 2021 that use experimental research methods to demonstrate the progress of collocation research in examining how information feedback and ethnic background influence willingness to co-produce and consequently co-production performance. This introduction should hopefully draw greater scholarly attention to co-production and advance research on the co-production motivation, information communication, and use of information technology in co-production, co-production performance, and the impact of ethnic diversity on co-production.</jats:p>

title: Information, Race and Co-production: Introducing Recent Representative Studies

items.abstract: <jats:p>Kebutuhan pakan dalam budidaya ikan sangat bergantung pada produk pakan komersial yang harganya terus meningkat, sementara potensi pemanfaatan limbah organik lokal seperti jeroan dan tulang ikan lele (Clarias sp.) belum dimaksimalkan. Limbah tersebut kerap dibuang begitu saja dan berkontribusi terhadap pencemaran lingkungan. Kegiatan pengabdian masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk memberikan edukasi dan pelatihan kepada kelompok wanita usia lanjut Melati 2 di Desa Mejono, Kabupaten Kediri, mengenai pemanfaatan limbah jeroan dan tulang ikan lele sebagai bahan tambahan nutrisi dalam pembuatan pelet ikan alternatif. Sebelum sosialisasi, tim mahasiswa melakukan percobaan mandiri untuk memastikan komposisi dan metode produksi yang efisien dan layak. Kegiatan inti berupa sosialisasi diikuti oleh 50 peserta dan mencakup materi tentang kandungan nutrisi, manfaat limbah, formulasi pakan, dan proses pembuatan pelet. Evaluasi dilakukan melalui pretest dan posttest, serta dianalisis menggunakan uji Wilcoxon Signed Rank yang menunjukkan peningkatan pemahaman peserta secara signifikan (p < 0,05). Kegiatan ini menunjukkan bahwa masyarakat mampu memahami konsep dan praktik pengolahan limbah menjadi produk bernilai ekonomi.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Oval brooches are among the most widely distributed artefacts of Viking Age Scandinavia (AD 750–1050) and their standardised forms have been cited as evidence for mass production. Yet, their distribution has not been studied beyond considerations of typology. Here, the author uses high-resolution digital scanning to compare 244 casting-mould fragments from Ribe (Denmark) and 105 extant Berdal-type oval brooches. Matches between five brooches from Denmark and Norway and 58 mould fragments are identified, supporting suggestions of a west-Scandinavian north–south sailing route but also calling established narratives of mass production at emporia such as Ribe into question.</jats:p>
title: Casting connections: rethinking Viking Age oval brooch production through high-resolution 3D modelling
