                    The abundances of stable isotopes in methane (CH
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    ) are used to distinguish fossil and biological emissions and to constrain the global methane budget. While these analyses require correction for isotopic fractionation occurring in methane’s atmospheric reactions, the temperature dependence of the kinetic isotope effects (KIEs) are poorly described and typically ignored. Here we combine density functional theory, Møller–Plesset perturbation theory, coupled-cluster calculations, and tunneling-corrected transition state theory to develop a first-principles description of the temperature-dependent KIEs for CH
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    and its isotopologues reacting with OH and Cl over the range 100 to 500 K which exhibit substantial and previously neglected temperature dependence. Incorporation of these KIEs into the EMAC chemistry–climate model yields systematically different effective atmospheric sink fractionation factors than those obtained using temperature-invariant values. The largest differences occur for chlorine oxidation in the cold upper troposphere and stratosphere, where methane isotope budgets are particularly sensitive to reactive halogens. We find a weak
                    <jats:sup>13</jats:sup>
                    C–D clumping anomaly and a strong D–D clumping anomaly, confirming earlier work and demonstrating that atmospheric oxidation produces substantial enrichment in Δ
                    <jats:sup>12</jats:sup>
                    CH
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    D
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    , and helping to reconcile source signatures with atmospheric observations. These results show that temperature-dependent KIEs are required for robust interpretation of methane isotopes in both contemporary and past atmospheres.
                  </jats:p>
title: Temperature-dependent kinetic isotope effects in methane reactions with OH and Cl reshape atmospheric sink fractionation

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The sociological analysis of gourmet and high-quality foods is primarily based on three research programs. From the perspective of economic sociology, the value of gourmet goods is inferred from the conventions and practices of the worlds of consumption and production. In contrast, cultural sociology examines gourmet foods as objects of status-related consumption, which indicate the social position and thus the symbolic value of the consumer. Finally, from an ethnomethodological perspective, the application and elaboration of vocabularies of valuation, connoisseurship, and taste are highlighted. We bring these three approaches together around a blind spot they share—taste work and the sensory socialization of customers. Empirically, we draw on field observations of coffee tastings and coffee packaging. Tastings as a form of taste work are based on the explicit linking of sensory experience (tasting the coffee) and discursive communication of evaluation categories. This not only cultivates bodies that are able to taste and evaluate, but also produces the customers on which roasteries depend. Coffee packages work as intermediary objects: they stabilize customers’ expectations and carry the evaluative categories and taste notes of professional tastings into everyday consumption.</jats:p>
title: Taste Work and Evaluative Knowledge

items.abstract: <jats:p>This review examines the integration of electrospun nanofiber architectures into PEM and AEM water electrolyzers. It focuses on representative studies in which nanofibers are used in reinforced membranes, catalyst-layer architectures, or transport interlayers. Across these applications, nanofiber networks have mainly been explored to improve mechanical stability, swelling control, gas crossover, catalyst utilization, and water or gas transport. The reviewed studies show that nanofiber integration can support thin membrane design and porous electrode engineering, but the reported benefits are still difficult to compare directly because testing conditions and performance metrics vary widely. Key remaining challenges include defect-free scale-up, long-term durability under realistic operating conditions, and more consistent benchmarking across studies.</jats:p>
title: Integrated nanofiber membranes for green hydrogen production via water electrolysis

<jats:p>
                    The effect of geological constraints on future hydrocarbon production is often underestimated in energy policies due to unreliable or incomplete reserve data. An alternative is to rely on production data, on the premise that production trajectories of non-renewable resources reflect underlying geological factors. Curve-fitting techniques, such as Hubbert linearization, have long been used to estimate ultimate recovery and forecast future production, but their typical application provides only a snapshot of the current situation, making it difficult to capture the influence of fluctuating human factors on oil extraction. They have therefore often proved unsatisfactory, resulting in repeated revisions. Here, we introduce a new dynamic Hubbert linearization framework that transforms the conventional single linear regression into a comprehensive diagnostic tool. Our contribution rests on four key elements: (1) systematic backward regressions over multiple time windows (e.g., 10–40 years), thus generating up to several dozens of estimates of ultimate recovery (U
                    <jats:sub>est</jats:sub>
                    ) and logistic growth rate (r
                    <jats:sub>est</jats:sub>
                    ) per year; (2) a visualization mapping all U
                    <jats:sub>est</jats:sub>
                    and r
                    <jats:sub>est</jats:sub>
                    over time, generating a diagnostic “fingerprint” that reveals characteristic temporal patterns of the production profile; (3) the interpretation of the fingerprint, allowing the detection of production above or below trends, and the distinction between transient deviations and sustained changes in logistic trends and its parameters; and (4) the introduction of the apparent depletion level (cumulative production/U
                    <jats:sub>est</jats:sub>
                    ) as a practical peak-warning indicator. Applied to three contrasting production profiles, conterminous US conventional oil, Norwegian offshore oil, and Barnett shale gas, this dynamic approach resolves long-standing limitations of static curve-fitting by extracting persistent production trends from time-dependent noise and market fluctuations.
                  </jats:p>
title: Revisiting Hubbert linearization: a dynamic regression approach for analyzing hydrocarbon production trajectories

<jats:p>
                    This study examines long-term assessments of energy generation, usage, and banked rates in a multi-purpose religious development in the eastern United States. Solar photovoltaic panels were installed to improve the development’s energy efficiency. The overarching goal of the research is to understand on-site energy generation, consumption, and banked rates over multiple years in historic religious buildings that have not been retrofitted with updated building envelopes. The research explored environmental monitoring from Nov. 2021 to Jul. 2022 and collected actual on-site energy generation, consumption, and banked data from 2016 to 2021. The average energy banked rate was reported at 5747 kilowatt-hours per year (kWh/year). Average solar radiation, in kilowatt-hours per square meter per day (kWh/m
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    /day), ranged from 2.80 in November to 5.65 in June. The development used approximately 7% (i.e. 0.07) less solar energy than the energy consumed annually. The actual/predicted energy rate varied from 0.67 to 1.21 over the years, averaging 0.93. The research indicates that energy-saving measures are critical in the first and fourth quarters because energy generation is lower than in the rest of the year. The study offers insights into integrating cleaner energy sources to support solar energy production in large developments during the colder months. Other measures, such as user activities, occupancy hours, preferences, smart metering, and retrofitting, can further improve energy savings in buildings. The study suggests future research should develop best practices for implementing solar technologies that respect the historical significance of these structures.
                  </jats:p>
title: Solar energy production, utilization, and savings rates in a historic religious building

items.abstract: <jats:p>The paper describes the features of the public-society partnership model emerging between the state, represented by authorities at various levels, and local communities that self-organize into territorial public self-government (TPSG). The specifics of using the TPSG institution in this process are analyzed. It is shown that the state acts as an initiator and regulator of these evolving relations, defining the boundaries and conditions under which communities are granted access to the production of public goods. The primary mechanism involves financing territorial public self-governments through a grant system. The formal status of the established TPSG institutions is a characteristic feature of the current stage of local community development, serving as a new collective adaptation strategy that enables access to resources (grants and administrative support). Changes in the relationship between these new formal institutions and the previously established system of informal interactions are analyzed. The complementary nature of these elements is demonstrated. Limitations that reduce the effectiveness of using the TPSG institution as a mechanism for solving problems within local communities have been identified.</jats:p>
title: Territorial Public Self-Government as a Mechanism for Community Participation in the Production of Public Goods

items.abstract: <jats:p>As mobile artificial intelligence (AI) systems become embedded in everyday technologies such as smartphones and social media platforms, it becomes critical to examine how they reshape the production of space, visibility, and belonging. This paper defines mobile AI as algorithmic systems that use real-time location and behavioral data to curate content, producing spatially situated experiences that encode racial and cultural assumptions about place. Rather than treating platforms as neutral intermediaries, I argue that mobile AI functions as a layered infrastructure—digital, sociotechnical, and spatial—that actively constructs racialized digital geographies while mediating access to representation and spatial meaning. Focusing on TikTok’s For You Page as a primary case, I demonstrate how platform algorithms leverage location metadata and engagement signals to generate “place profiles,” privileging content that is broadly legible and often aligned with outsider perspectives. In doing so, mobile AI amplifies narratives that flatten Black spatial knowledge while rendering culturally embedded, insider representations less visible. Extending Black geographic and critical race frameworks, I situate these dynamics within longer histories of spatial control, arguing that algorithmic systems reproduce racial inequality by determining whose presence is visible, whose movement is monitored, and whose culture is circulated in real time. At the same time, Black users engage these platforms as sites of active negotiation and resistance. Through strategic content creation, aesthetic choices, and narrative practices, they work within and against algorithmic constraints to assert spatial presence, archive community memory, and reimagine belonging. These practices constitute a form of digital placemaking in which cultural production becomes a means of reclaiming space across both physical and algorithmic terrains.</jats:p>
title: Mobile AI and the Making of Place: Black Spatial Production and Algorithmic Curation

items.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now a routine presence in foreign language classrooms, yet the gap between what the technology can do and what it actually teaches remains poorly theorised. This paper argues that the gap is structural, and that it is best analysed at the level of the pedagogic move. Taking the Production-Oriented Approach (POA) as its anchor, the paper identifies three chronic constraints in POA practice: the cost of evaluating student output, the difficulty of matching input to diagnosed gaps, and the delay between production and feedback. It then proposes the construct of an AI-enabled Production-Oriented Approach (AI-POA), which frames AI as a change in the resourcing and pacing of an existing cycle. Three affordances of generative AI (generative, dialogic, evaluative) are specified, together with four conditions under which they couple with instruction: goal alignment, temporal placement, cognitive appropriateness and teacher control. A nine-move cycle is derived, and implications for objectives, materials, assessment, teacher judgement and institutional arrangements are discussed. The framework is offered as a falsifiable middle-range theory rather than a design recipe.</jats:p>
title: From Affordance to Coupling: Reconstructing Foreign Language Pedagogy through an AI-Enabled Production-Oriented Approach

items.abstract: <jats:p>Electrochemical hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production is progressing from catalyst-centred proof-of-concept studies toward reactor and process development. This review evaluates the engineering and economic requirements for scalable H2O2 electrosynthesis, with emphasis on cathodic two-electron oxygen reduction, anodic two-electron water oxidation, and dual-pathway systems that generate peroxide at both electrodes. Gas-diffusion-electrode flow cells currently provide the most mature benchmark because they alleviate dissolved-oxygen transport limits and can sustain higher current densities than submerged electrodes. Their practical performance nevertheless depends on pressure balance, wetting stability, oxygen utilization, product residence time, crossover, thermal management, and component durability. Anodic peroxide generation expands the design space but remains constrained by competition with oxygen evolution, limited catalyst lifetime, and sparse reactor-scale validation. Reported technoeconomic advantages are highly sensitive to cell voltage, electricity price, electrode lifetime, product concentration, system boundaries, and coproduct credits, so Faradaic efficiency (FE) alone is not a sufficient measure of commercial readiness. The strongest near-term opportunities are decentralized applications in which on-site generation avoids transport and storage of concentrated peroxide or supplies oxidant directly to a downstream process. Progress toward industrial deployment requires standardized reporting of delivered H2O2 productivity, energy consumption, oxygen utilization, product quality, and durability under realistic feed and operating conditions, followed by scale-out demonstrations in repeatable cell and stack architectures.</jats:p>
title: Toward Scalable Electrochemical Hydrogen Peroxide Production: Engineering, Economics, and Emerging Industrial Systems

<jats:p>Subject. This article looks at a mix of theoretical, methodological, and practical questions about organizing internal audits of the use of drones in crop farming in the context of the digitalization of the agro-industrial complex. 
Objectives. The article aims to develop theoretical principles and practical recommendations for organizing internal audits of agro-drones usage in crop production, an audit methodology that includes checking the validity of routes and application rates, monitoring the completeness and quality of work, evaluating resource use efficiency, as well as creating an algorithm for integrating telemetry data into the accounting system for automated material write-offs. 
Methods. For the study, we used analysis and synthesis, a systems approach, classification, comparison, generalization, as well as risk management methods and modeling of control procedures. 
Results. The article presents an author-developed three-level methodology for internal auditing of agro-drone usage and proposes an algorithm for integrating telemetry data into the accounting system, consisting of seven consecutive steps – from creating a digital flight mission to monitoring deviations by the internal audit service. The article also presents an author-developed form of an electronic primary document, the Log of Agro-Drone Performed Operations, which ensures the transformation of technical information into an accounting document. 
Conclusions and Relevance. The proposed method and algorithm create
a closed-loop system for managing the use of agro-drones – from planning flight missions to material write-offs and evaluating effectiveness. The approach ensures accurate accounting by automatically generating primary documents based on verified telemetry data, preventing unwarranted resource write-offs. This turns internal auditing into a tool for managing the risks of digitalizing crop production. The results obtained can be used by internal audit services and management of agricultural organizations of various sizes to improve control and risk management systems when implementing drone technologies, and they can also be applied in the educational process when training specialists in economic security, auditing, and accounting in the agricultural sector.</jats:p>
title: The development of internal audit in the context of crop production digitalization

items.abstract: <jats:p>Data-driven monitoring and optimization require execution-time records that many labor-intensive offsite plants lack, because their records mark completions without timestamps. This study designs, implements and verifies a data-integration layer for a three-line bathroom-module factory. Operators declare task starts and finishes on tablets, and each declaration is reconciled into explicit time magnitudes and labeled by origin and evidence tier before reaching line balancing, discrete-event simulation and backward scheduling. The architecture operates as an operator-mediated digital shadow: the physical-to-digital flow is automated once an operator declares an event, and every proposal returned to the plant requires authorization by the production manager. As raw production records could not be released, the system was exercised on 1880 prototype task durations transformed from plant measurements and on 50,630 generated observations. Reconciliation exposed overstatements of 7 to 18 min that adding concurrent task durations would cause at three stations. The simulation engine matched an analytical bound exactly in eight typologies and within 0.4% in seven project mixes. The balancing module recovered a deliberately built opportunity, lowering the modeled bottleneck from 80 to 65 min in three typologies under the adopted station-load convention, a reduction that falls to 1 min in the typology examined if no task overlap is assumed. In a stress scenario, the scheduler flagged 804 of 1815 units as infeasible. These results verify functional behavior on selected scenarios, not operational performance in the plant. The layer makes data sufficiency explicit and prepares statistical monitoring once measured samples accumulate.</jats:p>
title: Data Integration for Production Monitoring in Labor-Intensive Offsite Manufacturing: A Human-in-the-Loop Digital Shadow

<jats:p>Subject. Factors determining the dynamics of nickel production in Russia.
Objectives. To identify the factors influencing the volume of nickel production in Russia, as well as to assess the nature of the interrelationships between nickel production, world nickel prices, the exchange rate of the US dollar against the ruble and investments in fixed assets.
Methods. The information base of the study was the annual data for 2006–2024. Methods of descriptive statistics, correlation and regression analysis, logarithmic modeling, time series stationarity tests, information criteria for choosing the lag length, Granger causality tests, cointegration analysis, ARDL approach and error correction model are used. Additionally, the sensitivity of the results to the structural periods of 2008–2009, 2020 and 2022–2024 and the exclusion of observations for 2021 was checked.
Results. A moderate negative relationship has been revealed between the volume of nickel production and the exchange rate of the US dollar against the ruble. Linear and logarithmic regression models showed a statistically significant negative correlation of nickel production only with the exchange rate, whereas no statistically significant coefficients were obtained for world nickel prices and fixed asset investments. Granger's causality tests did not reveal stable short-term predictive relationships. The Johansen test and the ARDL bounds test did not provide convincing evidence of a long-term cointegration relationship. A negative and statistically significant error correction factor in the reduced ECM showed the presence of a dynamic correction mechanism. The main result for the exchange rate remains after excluding the observation for 2021.
Conclusions. The development of the Russian nickel industry is explained not only by the macroeconomic factors considered, but also depends on a wider range of long-term industry and institutional conditions.</jats:p>
title: Statistical assessment of the relationship between macroeconomic factors and nickel production in Russia

items.abstract: <jats:p>LLM agents have evolved from demonstrations to enterprise applications in customer support, software engineering, document processing, and more. But more than benchmark accuracy is required to determine their production value. An agent could choose to use tools, access evidence, alter records, and/or repeat actions, and failures could be due to stale sources, weak authorization, non-convergent planning, duplicated writes, incomplete audit trails, or misleading measurement of outcomes. The paper suggests a five-layered architecture consisting of the following: Workflow plane, Bounded agent runtime, Grounding and knowledge layer, Observability and governance plane, Outcome-measurement control loop. It also creates a seven-level taxonomy of telemetry: sessions, planning steps, tool calls, retrieval, outputs, human interventions and population drift. Grounding is considered as an admission control: material assertions are required to be backed up by legitimate and up-to-date evidence or abstention and escalation. The business value is measured using controlled comparison, task stratification, quality review, intervention accounting and joint reporting of performance/cost. Field experiments show that the use of generative AI has the potential to boost speed, quality, and throughput, however, depending on the experience of the workers and the location of the task within the system's capability range. These principles are then broken down into operational controls and measurement definitions in two tables and integrated with the architecture and feedback loop in one figure. Production AI agents need to be deployed as bounded, observable, evidence-linked systems with permissions, sources, and versions that can be tested continually, and with claims of outcomes.</jats:p>
title: Deploying Production AI Agents in Enterprise Workflows: Observability, Grounding, and Measured Business Outcomes

                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Public explanations of flooding in Greater Accra frequently foreground indiscriminate waste disposal. This study aims to argue that such behaviour matters but becomes analytically misleading when separated from the institutions that organise land development, drainage, wetlands and the waste chain. Its main objective is to explain how landfill governance and land-use institutions mediate the relationship between waste and flood-risk production in Greater Accra.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>It combines a critical interpretive synthesis, qualitative document analysis and secondary satellite change detection around Kpone, Adekopa–Sonitra and the western corridor. Urban political ecology explains how flood exposure is produced through uneven urbanisation, while the Institutional Analysis and Development framework identifies how authority mismatch, information gaps, monitoring failures and weak sanctioning sustain that exposure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Six classified maps achieved 86.4%–99.5% internal hold-out accuracy (kappa = 0.80–0.99). Only the western corridor produced change exceeding the combined classification-error allowance where built-up land increased by 3.59 km⁲ between 2006 and 2026.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The article’s theoretical contribution is the governance-mediated urban-risk cascade, which links landfill lifecycle pressures, infrastructure disruption and spatial redistribution of exposure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings support transparent facility information, ring-fenced closure finance, emergency waste-routeing plans, interoperable spatial records and long-term environmental monitoring.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study is product of original thought and analysis of structured synthesis of scholarship published between 2006 and 2026, qualitative analysis of policy, audit, project and media documents, and secondary satellite change detection around Kpone, Adekopa–Sonitra and the McCarthy Hill–Oblogo–Mallam corridor.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Nanjangud Rasabale (NR), a banana variety from Karnataka with Geographical Indication (GI) status, is a traditional fruit crop of Mysuru district; however, its growers face production and marketing problems that limit profitability. The present study, conducted during 2025–26 in Nanjangud taluk, analysed production costs and returns, marketing channels, marketing costs and margins, marketing efficiency, and production and marketing constraints. Primary data were collected through a structured interview schedule from 38 respondents comprising 30 farmers, two village-level traders, two wholesalers-cum-commission agents and four retailers. Cost concepts, price spread, the producer's share in the consumer's rupee, Acharya's marketing efficiency index and Garrett's ranking technique were used. The total cost of cultivation was ₹2,81,580.74 per acre, with net returns of ₹2,12,181.76 and a benefit–cost ratio of 1.75. Two marketing channels were identified, of which Channel II (farmer–wholesaler-cum-commission agent–retailer–consumer) handled 84.50 per cent of the marketed produce. Marketing efficiency was higher in Channel I (1.77) than in Channel II (1.73), while the producer's share in the consumer's rupee was 63.91 per cent in Channel I and 63.38 per cent in Channel II. Garrett's ranking identified pest and disease incidence, low price realisation and labour scarcity as the foremost constraints. Strengthening plant protection services, collective marketing, market linkages and post-harvest infrastructure is recommended to improve profitability and supply chain efficiency.</jats:p>
title: Nanjangud Rasabale: Production Economics and Supply Chain Performance

<jats:p>Subject. Production and technological supply chains as a set of enterprises (links) united by the flows of products and resources, where the focus firm is the last one. In single-industry cities, a city-forming enterprise linking related manufacturers into a system can be considered as a focus company. 
Objectives. Substantiation of the possibility of applying the methodology of intersectoral balance as the most adequate tool for quantifying production and technological supply chains.
Methods. The methodological basis consists of methods of abstraction, generalization, and matrix modeling based on the methodology of intersectoral balance.
Results. It is proved that the methodology of the intersectoral balance is the most adequate tool for describing vertically integrated supply chains, which makes it possible to assess the effectiveness of their activities in terms of resources expended and achieving a given output.
Conclusions. The methodology of intersectoral balance makes it possible to analyze the system of internal production links of the chain, where the focus company is the city-forming one, in order to develop practical recommendations in the field of industrial and regional policy. The considered tools can be used by firms in the supply chain, allowing them to determine the optimal options for the transition from a raw material model to a closed-cycle bioeconomy on a strict mathematical basis using digital technologies, and to design new systems with horizontal and vertical connections between firms.</jats:p>
title: Modeling of production and technological chains in single-industry towns based on the methodology of intersectoral balance

<jats:p>Subject. The system of economic interrelations of three functions of corporate management – production control, marketing and economic analysis, considered as a single contour of creation and realization of consumer value in conditions of competition and high consumer awareness.
Objectives. To substantiate the economic necessity of integrating production control, marketing and economic analysis into a single quality management system and to show the mechanism of such integration, including a formal optimization model.
Methods. The research is based on a set of strategic analysis (SWOT analysis and PEST analysis) adapted to the cross-functional formulation of the problem, as well as on the apparatus of economic and mathematical modeling. A model of the total cost of quality is constructed, including the cost of preventive control, internal losses from defects and external (market) losses from inconsistencies, the model is generalized to the case of maximizing profits, taking into account the price premium for quality. 
Results. It is revealed that the three functions correspond to the three economic dimensions of quality – production, market and analytical, together forming
a complete cost management circuit. It is shown that the central connecting category is the total cost of nonconformity, the external component of which transfers the consequences of marriage into the sphere of market relations. An analytical condition for the optimal quality level has been obtained.
Conclusions. It has been established that the optimal level of quality is determined by the balance of marginal control costs, losses from nonconformities and the marginal price premium for quality. A corporation focused solely on minimizing costs systematically underproduces quality and misses profits. The practical significance of the work lies in the possibility of quantifying the allocation of resources between the functions of control, marketing and analysis, which forms an objective basis for management decisions aimed at increasing the value of the corporation.</jats:p>
title: Production control, marketing and economic analysis as a single system of corporate value formation

items.abstract: <jats:p>Sewage sludge contains valuable organic matter and nutrients, but its valorization through composting can be constrained by odour and gaseous emissions. This study compared two industrial-scale composting technologies for high-nitrogen municipal sewage sludge with carbon-rich biodegradable waste: a conventional technology and an inoculated technology combining a microbial inoculant containing an anaerobic facultative microbial consortium with reduced windrow turning. Conventional and inoculated windrows were compared in terms of process performance, odour, NH3, H2S and VOC concentrations, odour dispersion, and final compost quality. On Day 5, odour, NH3 and H2S concentrations were 80.6%, 78.0% and >99.5% lower, respectively, in the inoculated windrow. By Day 40, odour, NH3 and NMVOC concentrations remained 27.8%, 90.5% and 43.0% lower, respectively. Dispersion modelling showed that the maximum odour concentration at the facility boundary decreased from 9.25 OUE m−3 in the conventional scenario to 4.18 OUE m−3 in the inoculated scenario. The matured inoculated compost contained 20.9% more total nitrogen, maintained a higher organic matter content, and had substantially lower E. coli counts than the conventional compost (51 vs. 630 CFU g−1). These findings provide full-scale evidence that the inoculated composting technology can combine sewage sludge valorization with lower odour and gaseous pollutant concentrations and the production of nutrient- and organic-matter-rich compost.</jats:p>
title: Microbial Consortium-Based Inoculation Technology for Industrial-Scale Sewage Sludge Valorization: Odour Mitigation and Production of Value-Added Compost

items.abstract: <jats:p>Waste cooking oil (WCO) is an abundant waste resource that is often poorly managed. Phase change materials (PCMs) derived from WCO are typically prepared from crude or lightly refined oil, resulting in broad and poorly defined melting ranges that fall below the indoor thermal-comfort range. In conventional biodiesel production, winterization improves cold-flow properties, while the crystallized saturated fraction is discarded as a yield loss. In this study, winterization is instead employed as a co-production step to obtain both biodiesel and a bio-based PCM (Bio-PCM) from a single batch of WCO. WCO was processed through a sequence of bleaching-earth pretreatment, acid-catalyzed esterification, base-catalyzed transesterification, and controlled low-temperature winterization. Bleaching with 3% (w/w) activated bleaching earth removed pigments but reduced the free fatty acid (FFA) content only from 7.22% to 5.60%. Subsequent esterification using 4.0 g of H₂SO₄ reduced the FFA content to 0.55 ± 0.09% (one-way ANOVA, F = 2735.69, p-value < 0.0001). Transesterification subsequently achieved a fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) yield of 94.60 ± 0.92% and an ester content of 97.53 ± 0.55%, both of which met the requirements of EN 14214 and SNI 7182. A single controlled cooling stage at 10–12 °C isolated a solid fraction equivalent to 33.22 ± 2.41% of the FAME mass. This fraction was enriched in saturated esters, whose proportion increased from 72.8% to 76.8%, and was dominated by methyl palmitate (29.23%) and methyl laurate (21.22%), as determined by GC–MS. Differential scanning calorimetry of five eutectic formulations containing the solid FAME fraction (Fs) and stearic acid (5–25 wt% stearic acid) showed that both the transition temperature and latent heat increased with stearic acid content. Under a nitrogen atmosphere, the blend containing 25 wt% stearic acid (P5) exhibited a melting range of 31.0–39.0 °C, making it potentially suitable for exterior building-envelope applications, such as roofs and sun-exposed walls. However, its latent heat was only 8.08 J/g under nitrogen and 28.08 J/g under air, substantially lower than that of commercial fatty-acid-based and paraffin-based PCMs. The possible causes of this low and variable latent heat, along with practical strategies for improvement, are discussed. This study establishes a statistically validated mass balance for converting a waste feedstock into a compositionally and thermally characterized Bio-PCM candidate and identifies the remaining performance gaps that must be addressed before the material can be used for passive thermal management of tropical building envelopes.</jats:p>
title: Valorization of Waste Cooking Oil via Co-Production of Fuel-Grade Biodiesel and Solid Bio-PCM Thermal Storage

items.abstract: <jats:p>In the context of rural revitalization, public art is increasingly introduced into rural public spaces, yet its relationship with everyday village life across different spaces remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on spatial production theory, this study examines Songzhuang Village, Songyang County, China, using non-participant observation at 12 public-space nodes, public participation geographic information system (PPGIS)-assisted mapping, semi-structured interviews, and documentary evidence, with qualitative materials interpreted through reflexive thematic analysis. The findings identify three interrelated mechanisms of spatial reconfiguration, cultural translation, and relational restructuring, through which public art introduces cultural uses, reinterprets local knowledge and everyday experiences, and reshapes collaborative roles and responsibilities. However, perceived artistic change did not necessarily correspond with villagers’ routine use. Place meanings varied across participant groups, while villagers’ participation in specific projects did not necessarily extend to the planning and organization of subsequent activities. The use of art venues also varied with artistic programming and operating arrangements. Comparisons across spaces and participant groups provide a context-specific understanding of how public art relates to established spatial practices, place meanings, and continued involvement in rural public-space production.</jats:p>
title: Between Representation and Everyday Life: Public Art Interventions in the Production of Rural Public Space in Songzhuang, China

items.abstract: <jats:p>Dairy goat production plays a crucial role in food security and rural livelihoods worldwide, yet has received far less scientific attention than dairy cattle farming. Moreover, most sustainability assessments currently assess farm sustainability using a single metric. This narrative review synthesizes more than 100 studies, published between 2015 and 2025, to show the need for multi-metric assessment. It finds that farm management affects nearly everything that matters: greenhouse gas emissions, profit, milk quality, and resilience to shocks. Research is deep within each dimension but poorly integrated across them. For instance, environmentally efficient farms may not necessarily be the most profitable; farm size and system type predict sustainability outcomes less reliably than farm-level management; and subclinical disease pressure may lead to hidden farm inefficiencies. Economic models rarely account for uncertainty from disease, reproduction, and feed or milk prices, and environmental and economic impacts have not been evaluated within a single framework. Research is concentrated in Europe and the Mediterranean, and U.S. systems are largely absent. This review maps these gaps as a baseline for integrated frameworks that support dairy goat systems that are both environmentally responsible and economically viable.</jats:p>
title: Multidimensional Sustainability of Dairy Goat Production: A Review

items.abstract: <jats:p>Blood mineral concentrations are commonly used to assess mineral status in dairy herds, but their interpretation may be influenced by physiological stage and diet. This prospective longitudinal study aimed to characterize serum macromineral and trace element profiles throughout the production cycle in 48 multiparous Holstein-Friesian cows sampled five times from the dry period to late lactation. Mineral concentrations in diets and drinking water were assessed, and serum macrominerals and trace elements were analyzed by inductively coupled plasma–optical emission spectrometry and inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry, respectively. Significant temporal variation was observed for Co, Cu, Fe, I, Mg, Mn, Mo, total P, S, and Zn. Among the sampling periods evaluated, Fe, I, Mg, Mn, total P, and Zn showed their lowest concentrations during early lactation, whereas Cu increased after calving and Co and Mo followed distinct temporal patterns. Calcium, Cr, K, Na, and Se remained comparatively stable, with all elements within physiological ranges. Total P was affected by lactation group, and time-by-lactation interactions occurred for Co, Se, and Zn. Milk yield was modestly positively associated with several minerals. Overall, serum mineral profiles varied across the sampling periods evaluated and should be interpreted considering production stage, dietary transition, and lactation group.</jats:p>
title: Serum Macromineral and Trace Element Dynamics Throughout the Dairy Cow Production Cycle

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Aromatic nitriles are an essential part of today’s chemical industry and are widely applied in many industrial sectors. However, limitations of current large-scale synthetic processes like ammoxidation, a widely applied gas-phase reaction, include a high energy demand and a limited substrate scope, especially for high-boiling substrates. Accordingly, a representative challenge remains the development of efficient production processes for 4-phenylbenzonitrile, which represents an industrially needed specialty chemical with a large substituent on the benzene ring. This industrial specialty chemical is used as a key intermediate for pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and high-performance pigments, but also serves as a precursor for liquid crystals used in LCD screens. In this contribution, we present the development of a cyanide-free enzymatic synthesis of this biphenyl-based nitrile in water at a low temperature of 10 °C (and thus energy-saving conditions) by means of a regioselective recombinant OxdRE mutant from Rhodococcus erythropolis. We provide a method for optimized production of this biocatalyst and demonstrate that the resulting biotransformation runs under mild reaction conditions and enables excellent conversion to the target molecule with perfect chemoselectivity and at high substrate loadings of up to 158 g/L (corresponding to a substrate concentration of 800 mM), thus providing prospects for technical feasibility and production. Furthermore, we report the expansion of the substrate scope to the synthesis of the related 3-phenylbenzonitrile at the same high substrate loading and with quantitative conversion by means of another, meta-selective OxdRE mutant as biocatalyst.</jats:p>
title:

                    To evaluate weak-echo angle retrieval for space-target active laser sensing under strong background, we develop a photon-counting model integrating a vortex-phase-encoded wide-angle metalens (WAM) with a multi-pixel photon counter (MPPC). The WAM maps the incidence angle onto an annular focal spot, while an adaptive pipeline performs full-area response acquisition, coarse centroid estimation, pre-aperture-assisted annular photon selection, multi-response centroid refinement, and angle retrieval. The system model couples laser propagation, Lambertian target reflection, telescope collection, WAM focusing, MPPC parasitic effects, and four-electrode readout. For an idealized 100 km link at zenith and azimuth angles of 30° and 180°, respectively, simulations predict zenith and azimuth errors of 0.0305° and 0.0201°, a detection probability of 99.981%, and a false-alarm probability of 0.0131%. The estimated annular center meets the 0.5
                    <jats:italic>μ</jats:italic>
                    m convergence criterion after four iterations. Without prior knowledge of the true spot center, the adaptive method approaches ideal fixed-annulus selection and markedly outperforms full-surface MPPC integration. This model provides a framework for evaluating and optimizing wide-field photon-counting angle retrieval under weak-echo and strong-background conditions.

                  <jats:p>77Se nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a key method to probe selenium functional centers in biology and materials science, yet its practical application is severely hindered by its intrinsically low sensitivity due to the low gyromagnetic ratio (19% of 1H) and natural abundance (7.6%). Overhauser effect dynamic nuclear polarization (OE-DNP) has recently emerged as a promising method for generating steady-state signal enhancement in high-field liquid NMR at room temperature. However, its application to 77Se has remained unexplored to date. Here, we present liquid-state OE-DNP as a route for 77Se NMR. At 9.4 T, we report 102 to 103 fold signal enhancements for organoselenium compounds, including the drug candidate ebselen, with polarization buildup within seconds. The large enhancements are the result of efficient electron-to-nuclear polarization transfer with OE-DNP coupling factors of ≳|0.4|, the highest reported so far at high magnetic fields (≥3 T) for NMR-active nuclei. The replenishable signal enhancements allow reaction monitoring by NMR on timescales longer than nuclear T1. As a proof of concept, we monitor a diselenide metathesis reaction over 48 h, capturing species evolution for kinetic studies. This effect can be further expanded to the heavier chalcogen, tellurium, as demonstrated by 123Te OE-DNP with similar efficiency.</jats:p>

by Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization at 9.4 T for Real-Time

                  <jats:p>To achieve stable single-longitudinal-mode (SLM) operation in an erbium-doped fiber (EDF) configuration, a compound-fiber-ring design can be proposed and systematically investigated. items.abstract: <jats:p>In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly reshaped language services, particularly translation practices. By integrating AI technologies into source text (ST) analysis and target text (TT) production, contemporary systems have improved both the speed and consistency of translation workflows, thereby increasing the accessibility of information across linguistic boundaries. As demand for rapid and accurate digital communication continues to grow, AI-enabled machine translation tools have become central to how organizations and individuals manage multilingual content. Nevertheless, despite their efficiency, these systems often struggle to fully capture cultural nuances, pragmatic context, and meaning that depends on subtle linguistic or situational cues. This study examines the multifaceted impact of AI on translation, focusing on the benefits of technological advancement alongside its limitations in producing contextually and culturally resonant target texts. Ultimately, the paper emphasizes the importance of understanding how AI and human expertise can complement each other to support high-quality translations that effectively engage diverse audiences</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Quantum nonlocality, encompassing entanglement, EPR steering, and Bell nonlocality, is a core resource in quantum information science. However, in the literature, these important quantum properties are identified with the non-existence of discrete convex decomposition (D-model) or continuous probabilistic integral representation (C-model), where C- model refers to an integral representation over an arbitrary probability space, which may include atomic measures. This work establishes the equivalences between the C-model and D-model for bipartite separability, EPR unsteerability, and Bell locality in finite-dimensional systems. All proofs are based on an integral mean-value lemma for bounded measurable vector-valued functions on a probability space, which is built upon the Hahn–Banach separation theorem and Carathéodory’s convex hull theorem. This single technical lemma serves as a common tool to convert Bochner integral representations of continuous models into finite convex combinations. Consequently, in a finite dimensional bipartite system, C-separability, C-unsteerability, and C-Bell-locality are equivalent to D-separability, D-unsteerability, and D-Bell-locality, respectively.</jats:p>
title: Equivalence between continuous and discrete models in quantum nonlocality theory

items.abstract: <jats:p>The mechanisms of energy transfer between rare-earth ions and their influence on luminescence efficiency are analysed. On the basis of the Förster–Dexter theory, the dependence of the probability and efficiency of dipole–dipole energy transfer on the donor–acceptor distance is calculated. Using the Inokuti–Hirayama model, the donor luminescence decay curves in a YAG host are simulated for acceptor concentrations of 0.5–5 at.%, and it is shown that for a critical distance R0 = 1.5 nm the energy transfer efficiency increases from 71.7% to 99.3%. The practical significance of sensitisation, cross-relaxation and concentration quenching is discussed using the examples of Yb3+→Er3+ and Nd3+.</jats:p>
title: Energy transfer and luminescence efficiency in rare-earth-ion-based materials

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    A morphologically modified PANI/ZnO NCs was synthesized using
                    <jats:italic>Solanecio gigas</jats:italic>
                    (
                    <jats:italic>S. gigas</jats:italic>
                    ) leaf extract as a reducing and capping agent for the photocatalytic degradation of crystal violet (CV) under sunlight irradiation. Additionally, PANI and ZnO NPs were synthesized for comparison. All synthesized nanomaterials were characterized using UV–Vis, FT-IR, SEM, and XRD. The blue shift in the absorption peak of PANI/ZnO NCs suggests modifications in their optical and electronic properties, potentially associated with interfacial interactions and heterojunction formation between PANI and ZnO. FT-IR analysis revealed red-shifted absorption bands, suggesting possible hydrogen-bonding interactions between PANI and ZnO. Morphological analysis indicated that the composite exhibited surface features combining the rough texture of ZnO NPs with the relatively smooth morphology of PANI. Furthermore, XRD patterns exhibited overlapping diffraction peaks corresponding to the constituent phases, while the estimated crystallite size of the PANI/ZnO NCs (5.577 nm) was smaller than that of pristine ZnO NPs (9.455 nm), suggesting a reduction in crystallite growth upon composite formation. The effects of key photocatalytic parameters were investigated, and a solution pH of 11, photocatalyst dosage of 0.12 g, and an initial CV concentration of 20 ppm were determined to be optimum. The PANI/ZnO NCs exhibited higher photocatalytic activity, achieving 98.25% degradation compared to ZnO NPs with 92.76% under optimal conditions after 60 min of sunlight exposure. Kinetics studies indicated that the degradation rate fit well with the PFO kinetics (
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.968) for PANI/ZnO NCs. The composite demonstrated good catalytic activity with four cycles of reusability time compared to non-coated ZnO NPs. These findings highlight the potential of
                    <jats:italic>S. gigas</jats:italic>
                    leaf extract-assisted PANI/ZnO NCs as effective and sustainable nanocatalysts with promising applications in photocatalytic decomposition of organic contaminants for environmental remediation.
                  </jats:p>
title: Photocatalytic activity of green-synthesized PANI/ZnO nanocomposite under solar irradiation: water remediation application

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Neptunian desert is a prominent feature in the exoplanet population, thought to arise from both XUV-driven photoevaporation and tidal circularisation following high-eccentricity migration. However, the extent to which each mechanism contributes, and where, remains uncertain. We examine the desert as a function of stellar type as a test of these mechanisms. We determine the desert boundaries for subsamples of F, G, K, and M-hosted planets for radius against period, semi-major axis, bolometric instellation, and lifetime XUV irradiation. Going from F to M, we observe shifts in the boundary between 2.2–7.5 R⊕ towards shorter orbital periods, smaller orbital distances, and much smaller instellations. These shifts match changes in lifetime XUV irradiation as a function of stellar mass at fixed period, semi-major axis, and bolometric instellation, evidence towards a photoevaporative origin for the desert at these radii. This is especially the case for orbital period, where the boundary should be invariant across stellar types under the high-eccentricity mechanism. In lifetime XUV space, we see significant overlap in the boundary across stellar types up to 7.5 R⊕. While this could be further evidence towards the XUV-driven mechanism in this regime, our uncertainties cannot rule out a shift in the boundary of the magnitude expected under the high-eccentricity mechanism. Overall, our results suggest a photoevaporative origin of the Neptunian desert up to sub-Saturn radii, but increased sample sizes, especially for M-hosted, Neptune-sized planets, will help distinguish further between the mechanisms.</jats:p>
title: Carving the Neptunian desert as a function of stellar mass and lifetime XUV irradiation

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Local ion mobility and the connectivity of ion-conducting regions determine the measured conductivity of a solid electrolyte. In nanocrystal (NC)-derived solids, that connectivity is potentially tailorable through facet selection, ligand chemistry, attachment, ion exchange, and consolidation. This Perspective examines how the order of those operations sets particle contacts, boundary chemistry, and porosity. Case studies pair structural measurements with impedance spectroscopy under controlled pressure, temperature, and electrode conditions. Comparing matched processing routes helps identify whether the dominant resistance lies within crystalline domains, between particles, or at the electrode. The objective is to identify phases with high intrinsic ionic conductivity and preserve connected ion-transport pathways when those phases are incorporated into pellets, films, and composite electrodes.</jats:p>
title: Writing Ion-Transport Networks through Colloidal Pathways for Solid Electrolytes

<jats:p>
                    In this study, 304, 316L, and 316LN austenitic stainless steels were subjected to neutron irradiation at a relatively low fluence of 1 × 10
                    <jats:sup>18</jats:sup>
                     n/cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    , and their tensile properties were evaluated before and after irradiation. Notably, the ductility of 316L and 316LN steels increased by more than 25% without a significant reduction in ultimate tensile strength, whereas both ductility and strength of 304 stainless steel remained essentially unchanged. Neutron irradiation introduces point defects that subsequently evolve into a complex defect network consisting of dislocations, stacking faults, and deformation. The resulting strain fields exhibit pronounced spatial heterogeneity, forming chain‐like and banded distributions along dislocation lines, stacking‐fault arrays, and twin interfaces, indicative of strong local strain gradients and stress concentration effects. The incorporation of twin boundaries, stacking faults, and multioriented domains provides additional deformation accommodation pathways, including twinning‐induced plasticity (TWIP) and interface‐mediated slip, while simultaneously promoting sustained dislocation nucleation and glide. These mechanisms facilitate progressive strain delocalization across heterogeneous microstructural units, effectively suppress strain localization, and thereby enhance overall ductility. These findings provide a design strategy for irradiation‐tolerant alloys that retain high strength while achieving enhanced ductility under neutron exposure in next‐generation nuclear systems.
                  </jats:p>
title: Low‐Fluence Neutron Irradiation Slightly Enhances the Ductility of 316L and 316LN Austenitic Stainless Steels

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Reconfigurable metasurfaces provide a versatile platform for dynamically manipulating optical wavefronts, enabling emerging applications in holography, information processing, and optical encryption. However, existing phase‐change metasurface holograms predominantly exploit binary transitions between amorphous and crystalline phases, which severely restrict the attainable information capacity. Here we present a multilevel phase‐change metasurface architecture that leverages multiple intermediate crystallization states to encode substantially more holographic channels. We further introduce a cascaded metasurface configuration, where propagation‐assisted cooperative modulation creates an additional encoding dimension while mitigating inter‐channel crosstalk. By integrating the device physics into an end‐to‐end differentiable optimization framework, the cascaded structure is jointly optimized for dynamic multichannel holographic reconstruction. Numerical demonstrations validate that distinct combinations of crystallization states across the cascaded metasurfaces can selectively reconstruct multiple holographic images with high fidelity. This scalable strategy expands the information capacity of programmable metasurface holography and opens new opportunities for high‐density optical encryption, multidimensional information storage, and programmable wavefront engineering.</jats:p>
title: Reconfigurable Multi‐Channel Holography Based on Multi‐Level Phase‐Change Metasurfaces

items.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid identification of likely transport directions and particle deposition zones is needed after a nuclear accident, particularly before a defensible radionuclide source term and field network are available. We conducted a retrospective Fukushima case study to test the information content of a daily GOCI constrained PM2.5 series used to weight particle releases from the known plant location. The archived calculation released 7,163,349 computational particles from March 11 through March 30, 2011 and transported them with hourly winds, terrain dependent stochastic spreading, empirical dry removal, and precipitation dependent wet scavenging on a 0.05° grid. The plant PM2.5 series showed weak and nonsignificant daily correspondence with the monitoring constrained reverse estimates of iodine 131 and cesium 137 release from Katata et al. Pearson correlations were 0.275 and 0.255. These source terms were reconstructed after the accident from environmental observations and dispersion calculations. They were not direct measurements of emissions. No independent accident period radionuclide monitoring station was available within the modeled study area. The spatial analysis therefore compares March relative deposition with a later June and July air dose field and uses the Meteorological Research Institute site, about 172 km southwest of the plant, only as external temporal context. After georegistration to 1,050 common cells, modeled relative deposition and the later air dose field had Pearson’s r of 0.511 with a spatial block bootstrap 95 percent interval from 0.334 to 0.729. Spearman’s rho was 0.462 and bivariate Moran’s I was 0.494 with a fixed seed permutation p value of 0.0001. The model recovered 65.2 percent of the highest 20 percent of air dose cells. Particle number experiments were stable, but uniform hourly source weighting produced an almost identical map with a correlation of 0.9986 to the PM2.5 weighted baseline. Nearly all particles occupied the smallest numerical size class. The broad spatial agreement is therefore attributable mainly to the known source location, wind sequence, and empirical removal rather than evidence that the PM2.5 series reproduced radionuclide release timing. The transported population may include newly condensed accident particles and ambient particles that acquired radionuclides, but its radioactive fraction is unknown. The method may support rapid directional screening for particle associated contamination, but it does not estimate radionuclide activity, gas transport, dose, or exposure.</jats:p>
title: Rapid screening of particle associated deposition after a nuclear accident using satellite constrained aerosol weighting

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Using multimode fiber (MMF) as an architype complex optical medium, we introduce Dispersion‐Steered Modes (DSMs) for dynamic spatio‐spectral wave control. Unlike previous approaches that suppress modal dispersion to maintain static phase‐locking, DSMs actively transform the intrinsic dispersion into a synthetic transverse momentum. By utilizing spatio‐spectral operators to construct a generalized eigenvalue equation, we establish a deterministic mapping between spectral detuning and spatial translation. Specifically, we analyze the complex spatial velocity (the eigenvalue of the equation) and elucidate the physical meaning of its real and imaginary parts: the former governs spatial translation, and the latter degrades mode field stability. To obtain optimal modes, we establish a dual‐criterion selection mechanism based on the mean‐delay approximation and tailored inter‐mode coupling to synthesize robust DSMs that achieve dynamic steering with minimal spatial distortion. With experimental verification showing continuous translation of the focusing spot across a 1 THz bandwidth and spatial fidelity maintained above 0.8, this operator‐driven approach provides a framework for dynamic light manipulation in complex scattering environments.</jats:p>
title: Translational Steering With Multimodal Dispersion

items.abstract: <jats:p>Mass-selectable focused-ion beams (FIBs) expand nanoscale implantation beyond conventional Ga sources, but sodium remains challenging to implement in liquid-metal ion sources due to its chemical reactivity, low surface tension, sensitivity to residual gases, and poor wetting on refractory emitters. Here, we report a sodium-containing liquid-metal alloy ion source that delivers a mass-selected 23Na+ beam through a Wien-filtered focused-ion-beam column. The source combines a Ta emitter, an Au wetting layer, a porous Au-rich scaffold, and a Na-Bi reservoir. Emission began near 8.8 kV and entered a saturationlike regime near 9.1 kV. At an extraction voltage of 9.5 kV, the source maintained a mean emission current of 10.8 ± 0.2 μA over 3600 s. Mass analysis resolved a distinct signal at m/z = 23, and the selected Na+ beam was transported through the ion-optical column. Edge-response measurements yielded spot sizes of 44.4 ± 5.1 nm along the x direction and 49.1 ± 4.7 nm along the y direction at 20 kV. An energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy line scan across patterned Na-exposed regions showed a spatially correlated Na K signal. These results demonstrate the feasibility of sodium-compatible, mass-selected FIB operation for site-selective Na delivery.</jats:p>
title: Sodium-compatible liquid metal alloy ion source for mass-selected focused-ion beam operation

items.abstract: <jats:p>Erbium-modified mesoporous TUD-1 silica was investigated for light-assisted methylene blue (MB) decolorization in water. Four materials with nominal Si/Er molar ratios of 100, 50, 20, and 10 were prepared by a surfactant-free sol–gel route and characterized using X-ray diffraction, nitrogen physisorption, electron microscopy, elemental analysis, and photoluminescence spectroscopy. The materials retained the amorphous silica diffraction envelope without an XRD-detectable bulk crystalline Er2O3 phase. Increasing erbium loading decreased the BET surface area from 832.17 to 398.13 m2 g−1 and pore volume from 0.779 to 0.468 cm3 g−1, while increasing emission intensity under 245 and 397 nm excitation. At an initial MB concentration of 100 mg L−1, a catalyst dosage of 1 g L−1, and 25 °C, UV-driven decolorization after 55 min increased from 86.6% for Er-1 to approximately 99.9% for Er-10, compared with 5.8% for pristine TUD-1. Er-10 also achieved approximately 73% decolorization under visible light. The increase in decolorization despite decreasing surface area shows that the nitrogen-accessible area alone does not account for the observed response. The loading-dependent PL response is reported as an optical correlation and is not interpreted as direct evidence of charge-separation efficiency. A proposed light-driven response is discussed as a mechanistic interpretation; direct verification of reactive species and mineralization requires further experiments. These findings identify erbium loading as an influential variable in developing TUD-1-based materials for light-assisted dye decolorization.</jats:p>
title: Enhancing Methylene Blue Decolorization over Erbium-Modified Mesoporous TUD-1 Silica Under UV and Visible-Light Irradiation

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a prevalent microvascular complication, remains a leading cause of irreversible vision loss globally. Traditional DR managements, including anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) intravitreal injections, are limited by high treatment burden, suboptimal patient adherence, and transient efficacy. In recent years, gene therapy has represented a promising alternative, enabling long-term, adjustable, and endogenous production of therapeutic agents through a single administration. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current understanding of DR from epidemiology, multimodal diagnosis, and molecular pathogenesis to the historical evolution and limitations of conventional therapies. Building upon these mechanistic insights, we further discuss recent advances in gene therapy for DR, extending beyond conventional anti-angiogenic strategies toward neurovascular unit protection, inflammation modulation, and metabolic regulation. Emerging gene-editing technologies, including Cas13-based RNA editing and prime editing (PE) for DNA correction, are also highlighted as promising next-generation therapeutic platforms. In addition, we summarized pioneering candidates in clinical trials, such as RGX-314, ADVM-022, and 4D-150, which have demonstrated promising efficacy in reducing the frequency of injections. Despite promising advances, we also discussed remaining challenges involving vector optimization, immune safety, transgene regulation, disease modeling, and patient stratification. Overall, gene therapy holds substantial potential to transform DR management from repetitive symptomatic intervention toward durable and personalized molecular treatment.</jats:p>
title: Diabetic retinopathy: epidemiology, risk factors, mechanisms, clinical features, diagnosis and management

items.abstract: <jats:p>Ketidakseimbangan lintasan produksi (line balancing) pada industri manufaktur komponen otomotif sering kali memicu bottleneck dan waiting waste yang menghambat pencapaian target produksi. Penelitian ini dilakukan di CV. SYP Motor Parts, yang mengalami kegagalan pencapaian target produksi stang sepeda sebesar 820 unit/hari akibat bottleneck ekstrem pada Stasiun O-4 (Assembly & Welding). Tujuan penelitian ini adalah mengidentifikasi pemborosan, menganalisis beban kerja, dan merancang keseimbangan lintasan tanpa penambahan headcount. Metode yang digunakan meliputi Stopwatch Time Study, Westinghouse Performance Rating, Allowance ILO, Analisis Beban Kerja, dan Line Balancing yang diintegrasikan dengan pendekatan Skill Matrix. Hasil kondisi eksisting menunjukkan Line Efficiency (LE) hanya 57,31% dengan Balance Delay (BD) 42,69%, di mana O-4 mengalami overload 166% dan O-6 underload 66,2%. Perbaikan dilakukan melalui redistribusi operator berbasis kompetensi (Skill Matrix) dari O-6 ke O-2, dan O-2 ke O-4. Implementasi perbaikan berhasil menurunkan Cycle Time maksimum dari 51,04 detik menjadi 32,49 detik, meningkatkan LE menjadi 84,84%, menurunkan BD menjadi 15,16%, dan mereduksi kebutuhan waktu lembur dari >120 menit menjadi hanya 24 menit per hari untuk mencapai target produksi secara presisi.</jats:p>
title: Optimasi Lini Produksi untuk Meminimalkan Waktu Tunggu dan Meningkatkan Target Produksi Stang Pada CV. SYP Motor Parts

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Photon blockade is of critical importance for realizing single‐photon emitters and for the quantum simulation of interacting systems with light. Through destructive quantum interference, strong photon blockade in a cavity system can be observed even in the common weak‐coupling (weak‐nonlinearity) regime. However, previous protocols to realize such unconventional photon blockade require fine‐tuning of system parameters and can only operate within particular time windows. Leveraging dark‐state physics, we report in this work a mechanism for robust photon blockade operating continuously without fine‐tuning. Specifically, we consider a system consisting of a two‐level atom weakly coupled to an optical cavity supporting two coupled modes. Under a weak on‐resonance probe field, quantum interference creates single‐ and double‐excitation dark states, and the coupling strength between these two types of dark states is drastically reduced by quantum destructive interference. The dominating single‐excitation dark state, resonantly coupled with the probe field, then leads to a photon blockade mechanism that is robust against cavity parameter variations and allows continuous‐time operations of photon blockade. We discuss possible applications of such dark‐state‐mediated photon blockade in the realization of a narrow‐bandwidth single‐photon source.</jats:p>
title: Robust Interference‐Induced Photon Blockade Mediated by Dark States

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose of Review</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Three prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography (PET) tracers hold FDA approval, and the theranostic agent, 177Lu-PSMA-617, given with an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) is now indicated for PSMA-positive metastatic hormone-sensitive disease, in addition to its use in metastatic castration-resistant disease. Our aim is to summarize the PSMA PET tracers in clinical use and their cross validity for 177Lu-PSMA-617 target efficacy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Recent Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Ga-68 PSMA-11, F-18 piflufolastat, and F-18 flotufolastat differ marginally in half-life, production, and urinary excretion, but none have shown diagnostic superiority. Pivotal trials, including
                      <jats:italic>VISION</jats:italic>
                      ,
                      <jats:italic>PSMAfore</jats:italic>
                      , and
                      <jats:italic>PSMAddition</jats:italic>
                      determined eligibility with centrally read Ga-68 PSMA-11. American Society of Clinical Oncology guidance nevertheless accepts any of the three PSMA PET tracers for candidacy, and the 177Lu-PSMA-617 product label concurs. The rationale is physiologic and consensus-based:
                      <jats:italic>VISION</jats:italic>
                      defined positivity relative to liver uptake, and joint European American nuclear medicine guidance applies this rule to all tracers. Additionally, tumor/liver and tumor/salivary gland ratios are scanner-independent surrogates, supporting this cross validity. Quantitative predictors of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response and overall survival were derived using Ga-68 PSMA-11, but emerging fluorine-18 data are supportive, though there’s a lack of standardization.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Summary</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The approved tracers appear cross-valid for liver-referenced eligibility and quantitative metrics predicting treatment response, but the strongest evidence remains tied to Ga-68 PSMA-11. Tracer interchangeability rests on consensus, rather than companion-diagnostic trials. Future randomized intra-patient comparison could potentially establish whether tracer choice alters eligibility or predicts benefit, and whether thresholds are tracer specific.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Interchangeability of PSMA PET Tracers and Theranostic Target Efficacy in Prostate Cancer

items.abstract: <jats:p>Indigenous lactic acid bacteria (LAB) drive the fermentation and maturation of artisanal raw-milk cheeses, yet tracking individual species over several months of ripening remains difficult when relying solely on conventional agar media. Extending our earlier work on molecular LAB detection, we developed intercalating dye-based quantitative PCR (qPCR) assays directed at single-copy chromosomal loci (yjaE for Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis and ACRRRJ_03990 for Streptococcus thermophilus) to follow target DNA levels across 180 days of raw cow’s milk cheese maturation (sampled at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, and 180 days) in parallel with routine enumeration on M17 agar. Selecting single-copy targets eliminated the copy-number variation typical of 16S or 23S rRNA operons. According to qPCR measurements, S. thermophilus gene copies increased up to day 90 (reaching 6.32–6.89 log10 gene copies/g) and subsequently dropped to 2.74–3.51 log10 gene copies/g by day 180, reflecting progressive loss and degradation of amplifiable chromosomal DNA. By contrast, L. lactis subsp. lactis target DNA accumulated throughout the entire ripening period, reaching 7.26–7.90 log10 gene copies/g at day 180. Routine plate counts diverged substantially from qPCR data during mid- and late ripening: colonies of presumptive thermophilic streptococci were no longer recovered by day 90 (<1.0 log10 CFU/g), whereas presumptive mesophilic lactococci decreased to roughly 1.95 log10 CFU/g at day 90 and fell below the detection limit from day 120 onwards. Because standard DNA-qPCR amplifies total intact template regardless of physiological state, these data alone cannot separate viable-but-non-culturable (VBNC) cells from intact dead cells or residual matrix-bound DNA. Nevertheless, the high abundance of target gene copies detected long after colony formation ceased shows that culture-based monitoring alone markedly under-represents the persistence of autochthonous LAB target DNA during extended cheese ripening.</jats:p>
title: Longitudinal Quantification of Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis and Streptococcus thermophilus Target DNA in Ripening Raw-Milk Cheese Using Single-Copy Gene qPCR and Agar Plating

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Keratoconus (KC) is primarily characterized by progressive corneal structural changes; however, whether it is associated with alterations in posterior segment morphology remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate posterior pole retinal thickness distribution using Posterior Pole Asymmetry Analysis (PPAA) in patients with KC and to investigate whether PPAA-derived retinal thickness parameters are associated with KC severity. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 90 eyes of 90 patients with KC and 30 eyes of 30 healthy controls. Posterior pole retinal thickness distribution was assessed using PPAA with Spectralis spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), while corneal parameters were obtained using Scheimpflug tomography (Pentacam). KC severity was classified according to the Belin ABCD staging system. Mean posterior pole retinal thickness and regional superior–inferior (S–I) thickness differences were compared between groups and across KC severity stages. Associations with keratoconus-related parameters were also examined. Results: Age, sex, and axial length were comparable between the KC and control groups (all p > 0.05). Of the 90 patients with KC, 26.7% (n = 24) had mild, 31.1% (n = 28) moderate, and 42.2% (n = 38) severe KC. Mean posterior pole retinal thickness in Zone 1 and Zone 2 did not differ significantly between KC and control eyes or across KC severity stages (all p > 0.05). The peripheral S–I thickness difference was greater in all KC severity groups than in controls (p < 0.001), whereas the central S–I thickness difference varied across groups (overall p = 0.0025), with a significant post hoc difference between moderate and severe KC. No significant correlations were observed between keratoconus-related parameters and mean Zone 1 or Zone 2 retinal thickness. Conclusions: Regional S–I analysis may reveal differences in posterior pole retinal thickness distribution in KC that are not captured by conventional mean thickness measurements. The clinical significance of these findings warrants further investigation.</jats:p>
title: Analysis of Posterior Pole Retinal Thickness Distribution in Keratoconus
