items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Brucellar sacroiliitis can remain abnormal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) after clinical and biochemical improvement, creating uncertainty about the interpretation of follow-up tests. We characterized the timing of MRI improvement relative to inflammatory markers. Methods: In this single-center retrospective case series, 39 patients with brucellosis, scintigraphic sacroiliac involvement, and baseline plus follow-up sacroiliac MRI were evaluated between 2010 and 2015. Patients whose therapy was stopped without follow-up MRI were not included, and the number of patients screened could not be determined. Serial MRI reports, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), antimicrobial regimens, and treatment durations were reviewed. Results: All patients were male (mean age, 21.05 ± 1.63 years). Mean treatment duration was 265.82 ± 114.94 days. ESR decreased from 17.28 ± 15.46 mm/h at baseline to 5.82 ± 7.07 mm/h at first follow-up (p < 0.001), and CRP > 6 mg/L declined from 22/39 (56.4%) to 7/37 (18.9%; p = 0.009). Nevertheless, 34/39 patients (87.2%) had persistent active MRI findings at the first follow-up. MRI abnormalities resolved at different subsequent assessments; seven patients first showed resolution at the sixth follow-up and had a mean treatment duration of 428.00 ± 93.84 days. Conclusions: Biochemical improvement and resolution of active MRI findings were not synchronous in this selected cohort. The 87.2% MRI persistence rate applies only to this selected, MRI-followed cohort of young men and cannot estimate the prevalence of persistent abnormalities in unselected brucellar sacroiliitis. Because treatment was continued until active MRI findings resolved, longer treatment in late-resolving patients reflects this stopping rule; the study provides no evidence that prolonging antibiotics until MRI resolution improves clinical outcomes. Persistent MRI signal should not be interpreted as microbiological failure or an automatic indication to extend treatment. Because patient-relevant outcomes were not available, the clinical significance of this discordance remains unknown. Standardized prospective studies are needed before an MRI-guided treatment algorithm can be recommended.</jats:p>
title: Discordance Between Biochemical Improvement and Serial MRI Findings During Treatment of Brucellar Sacroiliitis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Elevated serum vitamin B12 accompanies liver injury, but its relationship with outcomes in acute hepatitis remains uncertain. We evaluated admission vitamin B12 and an exploratory B12–ferritin index (BFI). Methods: This retrospective study included 186 adults hospitalized with acute hepatitis or acute liver injury (2018–2025). Outcomes included ward length of stay, transplantation, and in-hospital mortality; exploratory endpoints were ICU admission, encephalopathy, and an ICU-inclusive composite. Discrimination was assessed using ROC AUC, including comparison with MELD 3.0. Eight B12 values exceeded the assay limit of 4000 pg/mL and were top-coded in numerical analyses. Results: Nine (4.8%) patients died, one (0.5%) underwent transplantation, and 20 (10.8%) met the ICU-inclusive composite; all 20 were admitted to the ICU. Encephalopathy occurred in 11 (5.9%). Vitamin B12 AUCs were 0.935 (95% CI 0.891–0.979) for mortality, 0.944 (0.904–0.984) for death or transplantation, and 0.938 (0.897–0.980) for the composite. B12 was unrelated to ward length of stay (Spearman ρ = 0.017; p = 0.818). BFI did not improve discrimination over B12. In an exploratory model adjusted for age and MELD 3.0, the B12 association persisted (adjusted OR per 1000 pg/mL, 7.67; 95% CI 3.38–17.44). Conclusions: Admission B12 was associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes, but limited event counts, uncertain sampling–event timing, and assay censoring prevent clinical prediction claims. Prospective validation is needed.</jats:p>
title: Admission Vitamin B12 and in Hospital Outcomes in Adults with Acute Hepatitis and Acute Liver Injury

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Postmortem computed tomography (PMCT) has been proposed as an adjunct or alternative to autopsy, but its agreement with autopsy in fatal trauma has not been comprehensively reviewed since 2009. Methods: Four databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science) were searched from inception to 22 October 2026. Of 51 eligible studies, 14 were excluded during data extraction and one was added from citation-chasing, leaving 38 studies (1994–2026; 18 countries). Findings were synthesized narratively by injury category without pooling because outcome definitions were heterogeneous; risk of bias was assessed with Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 (QUADAS-2). Results: PMCT detected skeletal fractures and air-containing lesions as often as or more often than autopsy (e.g., skull fractures, 100% vs. 76.9% in one cohort), whereas autopsy detected more soft-tissue injuries and, in most cohorts, more solid-organ injuries. Agreement on cause of death varied widely (cohort-level estimates from 33.9% to 99%). The most common risk-of-bias concern was an autopsy that was not blinded to PMCT. One study of pedestrian fatalities (n = 21) showed the same pattern. Conclusions: PMCT is supported as an adjunct to, not a replacement for, autopsy in fatal trauma. Its contribution depends on injury type, imaging protocol, and the forensic question, and injury detection should be distinguished from cause-of-death determination. Evidence for pedestrians is preliminary.</jats:p>
title: Postmortem Computed Tomography Versus Conventional Autopsy in Fatal Trauma: A Systematic Review

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objective: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been investigated for the radiographic recognition of existing complications and prediction of subsequent adverse outcomes after total hip arthroplasty (THA). We synthesized the reported diagnostic and prognostic performance and examined testing strategies, calibration, and methodological limitations. Methods: We conducted a systematic review reported in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020. Eligible English-language full-text studies published between 1 January 2010 and 31 August 2026, evaluated Artificial intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) models using radiographic information, alone or with clinical data, to detect an existing post-THA complication or predict a subsequent complication or implant failure. Mixed-population studies required separately extractable THA-specific results. The final search was executed on 21 October 2026. Eligible models incorporated radiographic images or image-derived features; clinical-only models were not eligible. A structured narrative synthesis was used because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Results: Twelve studies met the eligibility criteria for qualitative synthesis after the exclusion of studies focused on pre-arthroplasty osteoarthritis progression or short-term need for THA, which were outside the pre-defined review scope. Across the included post-THA studies, AI models were applied to tasks including aseptic loosening detection, multiclass failure classification, dislocation risk prediction, periprosthetic fracture as a label within the broader THA complication recognition, and longitudinal prediction of prosthesis failure. Several studies reported high apparent discrimination, particularly in internally validated single-center datasets, while some studies evaluated performance in additional institutional cohorts. Registry linkage was not treated as evidence of external evaluation. However, the evidence base was limited by substantial heterogeneity in populations, outcome definitions, model designs, and validation strategies, and most studies were judged to be at high overall risk of bias. Conclusions: Current evidence suggests that AI-based radiographic assessment of selected post-THA complications is promising, but the principal limitations are incomplete independent external evaluation, sparse calibration and clinical-utility evidence, and methodological concerns. The reported retrospective performance does not establish improved implant survivorship or patient outcomes. A prospective multicenter evaluation, transparent reporting, human–AI workflow assessment, and clinical-impact studies are needed before routine adoption.</jats:p>
title: Artificial Intelligence for Radiographic Identification, Detection, and Prediction of Complications Post-Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: The anatomical distribution of the muscular branches of the median and ulnar nerves in the forearm may provide anatomically relevant information for clinical examination, lesion localization, and therapeutic planning. To describe the anatomical organization and muscle-target-derived functional associations of the muscular branches of the median and ulnar nerves in the anterior compartment of the forearm and to quantify the muscle-target-derived association gradient along their proximal-to-distal branching sequence. Methods: Descriptive, observational, cross-sectional anatomical study using cadaveric dissection. Sixteen fresh right upper limbs from 16 adult donors were studied. Muscular branches were grouped by individual, nerve, and order of origin. For descriptive analysis, branches were classified according to their order of origin as proximal, middle, or distal; for inferential analysis, a continuous relative position ranging from 0 to 1 was calculated. Paired differences between nerve territories were assessed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and the functional gradient was evaluated using conditional logistic regression stratified by individual, with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment for functional comparisons. Results: A total of 68 primary branches were identified in the median nerve territory and 44 in the ulnar nerve territory. The median nerve had more branches and more muscular targets per branch. In the median nerve territory, the odds of the combined pronation outcome decreased toward the distal end, predominantly reflecting the proximal distribution of pronator teres rather than pronator quadratus (OR 0.04; 95% CI 0.01–0.24; q = 0.003), whereas the association with proximal interphalangeal flexion increased (OR 8.37; 95% CI 1.67–41.89; q = 0.034). In the ulnar nerve territory, wrist flexion/ulnar deviation decreased distally (OR 0.04; 95% CI 0.003–0.59; q = 0.039), whereas the association with distal interphalangeal flexion increased (OR 14.99; 95% CI 1.47–152.85; q = 0.039; imprecise estimate). Conclusions: The observed proximal-to-distal branch-origin sequences showed directional associations with functional domains inferred from muscular targets, not directly measured motor function. The proximal pronation association was predominantly attributable to pronator teres, while pronator quadratus had a different distribution. These anatomical findings are hypothesis-generating; their clinical diagnostic value requires prospective validation.</jats:p>
title: Proximal–Distal Functional Organization of the Muscular Branches of the Median and Ulnar Nerves in the Forearm

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Whole-genome doubling (WGD) is reported in clinical sequencing, but its prognostic value in sarcoma has not been assessed after accounting for histologic subtype. We evaluated whether fraction of genome altered (FGA) is associated with overall survival (OS) and whether WGD adds prognostic information beyond FGA. Methods: We analyzed 1494 MSK-IMPACT patients (593 deaths) across 17 subtypes using subtype-stratified Cox models adjusted for age and sample type; OS was measured from sequencing. Incremental value was assessed with likelihood-ratio tests and optimism-corrected C-indices. TCGA sarcomas (n = 241; 233 with ABSOLUTE-based WGD) were used for external replication. Results: FGA was associated with worse OS (hazard ratio [HR] per 0.10 increase, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.06 to 1.16; per unit increase, 2.84; 95% CI, 1.81 to 4.46), with a graded relationship across quartiles (HR per step, 1.21). WGD was associated with OS unadjusted (n = 1774: HR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.02 to 1.43; n = 1494: HR, 1.25; 95% CI, 1.05 to 1.50) but not after subtype stratification (n = 1494: HR, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.36). Adding FGA to WGD improved model fit (p < 0.001); adding WGD to FGA did not (p = 0.81). Optimism-corrected C-indices were 0.618 (clinical model), 0.618 (plus WGD), and 0.633 (plus FGA). In TCGA, FGA was associated with OS (HR per unit, 5.15; 95% CI, 2.05 to 12.93) and added information beyond WGD (p = 0.004), whereas WGD added none beyond FGA (p = 0.44), although WGD alone remained associated with OS in TCGA (HR, 1.69). FGA effect size varied across subtypes (I2 = 57%) but persisted without gastrointestinal stromal tumors (HR, 2.06; 95% CI, 1.26 to 3.36). Conclusions: Higher FGA was associated with shorter OS in two sarcoma cohorts, and WGD added no detectable incremental information beyond FGA in either. Discrimination gains were modest; grade, stage, and treatment were not modeled in the main analyses; and OS was measured from sequencing. Prospective evaluation is needed before clinical use.</jats:p>
title: Association of Fraction of Genome Altered with Overall Survival in Sarcoma: Histologic Subtype-Stratified Discovery and External Replication Study

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: The relationship between pericardial tethering and constrictive physiology remains incompletely understood. We investigated whether either the tethering burden and ventricular distribution are associated with constrictive haemodynamics. Methods: In this prospective cohort study, 45 patients with tuberculous (TB) pericarditis underwent baseline and 6-month cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging with tissue tagging. Pericardial tethering was assessed at 6-month follow-ups using a validated 20-segment pericardial segmentation model. Constrictive haemodynamics at 6 months were assessed by transthoracic echocardiography. Results: Six of forty-five participants (13.3%) had constrictive haemodynamics at 6 months. Participants with constriction had greater left ventricular (LV) (36.4% [29.6–39.8] vs. 18.2% [13.7–25.0], p = 0.002), right ventricular (RV) (25.0% [22.2–32.0] vs. 0.0% [0.0–11.1], p < 0.001), and total tethering burdens (63.7% [51.8–73.7] vs. 22.8% [13.7–34.9], p < 0.001). LV tethering showed a substantial overlap between groups, whereas RV tethering demonstrated complete separation: all participants with constriction had ≥4 tethered RV segments (22.2% of total pericardial surface area), while none without constriction reached this threshold. The discrimination for constrictive haemodynamics was greatest for RV tethering (AUC 1.000), followed by total (AUC 0.987) and LV tethering (AUC 0.893). The RV threshold was identified post hoc, and its apparent discriminatory performance requires validation given the small number of constrictive events. Conclusions: Constrictive haemodynamics in TB pericarditis were associated not only with the overall tethering burden but also showed a distinct pattern of ventricular involvement. LV tethering was common in the absence of constriction, whereas all participants with constrictive haemodynamics demonstrated substantial biventricular tethering, including the involvement of at least four RV segments. These findings support the hypothesis that the haemodynamic expression of pericardial tethering may depend on its ventricular distribution in addition to its overall extent, although the independent contribution of RV involvement remains to be established.</jats:p>
title: Regional Ventricular Pericardial Tethering and Constrictive Haemodynamics in Tuberculous Pericarditis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: This secondary analysis of a previously published cohort addressed four measurement questions:: variability from repeated caliper placement on the same image, change-score reliability across active straight leg raise (ASLR) trials, sensitivity to trial selection, and reproducibility of delayed rereading of stored images Methods: Thirty-three healthy adults completed three paired rest–ASLR trials under relaxed, maximal dorsiflexion, and maximal plantarflexion conditions. The dataset contained 594 stored images, each measured three times for each of the transversus abdominis (TrA), internal oblique (IO), and external oblique (EO). Fifty images from 11 participants were reread by the same examiner 15 days after the original assessment, as reported in the parent publication. Results: Mean within-image SDs were 0.143, 0.231, and 0.185 mm for TrA, IO, and EO. The pooled single-trial TrA change-score intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC(A,1)] was 0.629 (95% CI, 0.431–0.760); model-projected ICCs for averages of two and three complete trials were 0.772 (95% CI, 0.603–0.864) and 0.836 (95% CI, 0.695–0.905), respectively. The complete-trial dorsiflexion-minus-relaxed TrA contrast was 0.162 mm (95% CI, 0.059–0.265); plantarflexion-minus-relaxed was 0.085 mm (95% CI, −0.022–0.193). Estimates based on different trial subsets varied, particularly for the plantarflexion contrast. Delayed rereading ICC(A,1) values were 0.819 (TrA), 0.893 (IO) and 0.848 (EO).Absolute differences were larger than would be expected from immediate caliper dispersion alone. Conclusions: Caliper-placement variability, reliability across ASLR trials, sensitivity to trial selection, and delayed rereading of stored images represent distinct measurement properties and should not be conflated. Trial-averaging values were conditional model projections rather than validated clinical recommendations, and this study did not assess diagnostic validity or repeat-scan reliability.</jats:p>
title: Measurement Reliability and Trial-Sampling Effects in Ultrasound Assessment of Abdominal Muscle Thickness During the Active Straight Leg Raise

items.abstract: <jats:p>Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) microstates have been proposed as an accessible complement to established biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). This critical narrative review asks whether findings from studies deriving microstate parameters differently can be compared. PubMed, PubMed Central, Google Scholar, Web of Science and Scopus were searched to 20 August 2026, and fifteen studies of healthy control, mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD groups were synthesised by parameter family, with each study’s pipeline extracted and its reporting and bias appraised. No finding was directly replicated. Increased class B duration (four cohorts differing in population and pipeline), reduced sequence complexity (two studies) and a label-level association between class C topography and cerebrospinal fluid amyloid (two cohorts) recurred in the same direction and are hypothesis-generating; increased class A temporal parameters were inconsistent. Findings conflicted on changes in occurrence in AD, microstate syntax and topographic sensitivity to group. Each conflict coincided with a methodological difference; two such effects were demonstrated within single cohorts, and the others remain untested. No cohort has been measured twice, and similar alterations occur in psychiatric disorders. Microstates are therefore candidate research markers, not established or disease-specific clinical biomarkers; progress requires standardised reporting, verified topographic correspondence and prospective participant-level validation.</jats:p>
title: Disentangling Stage-Related Findings from Methodological Heterogeneity in Resting-State EEG Microstate Studies of Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer’s Disease

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Pericardiectomy is the definitive treatment for constrictive pericarditis (CP), but data on postoperative cardiac remodeling remain limited. Methods: In this single-center retrospective study, 117 of 126 patients undergoing pericardiectomy (mean age 49.9 ± 14.8 years; 71.8% male) had paired pre- and postoperative echocardiograms. Ten parameters were primary; inferior vena cava (IVC) diameter was exploratory. False discovery rate and Bonferroni corrections were applied. Results: At a median interval of 39 days, left atrial (LA) diameter decreased by 3.68 mm (−8.0%) and right atrial (RA) diameter by 4.44 mm (−10.6%), whereas left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD) increased by 2.75 mm (+6.5%) and right ventricular (RV) transverse diameter by 2.62 mm (+8.6%) (all q < 0.001). RV s′ decreased (p < 0.001), whereas TAPSE and LVEF were unchanged; TR velocity increased (+13.2 cm/s; n = 53; p = 0.017; q = 0.024). Among 60 patients with at least two postoperative TAPSE measurements, TAPSE increased from the first to the last study (+1.55 mm; 95% CI +0.41 to +2.70; p = 0.009). Valve surgery was associated with greater RA reduction (β = −4.89; p = 0.005). Preoperative severity correlated with remodeling magnitude, but Oldham analysis supported an independent relationship only for LA, RV, and LVEF. In-hospital mortality was 2/126 (1.6%; paired 1/117, 0.9%). Conclusions: Pericardiectomy is associated with prompt biatrial decompression and progressive ventricular enlargement. Early TAPSE reductions were not sustained in patients with repeated studies, cautioning against interpreting isolated early changes as RV dysfunction; these parameters provide reference values for postoperative surveillance.</jats:p>
title: Paired Echocardiographic Characterization of Reverse Cardiac Remodeling After Pericardiectomy for Constrictive Pericarditis: A 117-Patient Cohort Study

items.abstract: <jats:p>Computed tomography (CT) frequently shows the tip of a cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) lead, or the fixation tine of a leadless pacemaker, beyond the myocardial contour in patients without symptoms or hemodynamic compromise. What such an image means is a separate question the literature has not settled. This narrative review sets out the definitions in use, the three CT cohorts behind the argument, the observed natural history and the management choices that follow, keeping anatomical observations apart from clinical events. Reported penetration was 15/100 conventional-device recipients, 26/463 conventional leads (25/271 patients) and 15/88 leadless recipients; a conference abstract reported 12 of 31 leadless recipients (38.7%). Sampling, observation unit, device structure and imaging interval differ across these sources, so none supports an incidence figure or a device comparison. No clinical perforation developed over 2.7 years among 25 patients with conventional-lead findings, and no related adverse event occurred over a mean of 12.4 months among 15 leadless recipients; both figures concern findings already silent at CT, neither cohort sized the residual risk, and imaging accuracy measured in recognized perforation does not carry over to screening. Implantation guidance sets no screening or intervention criteria. What the evidence supports is individual assessment, not routine CT screening, universal intervention or fixed warning thresholds. Assessment criteria, a reporting checklist, and emerging imaging and automation tools are summarized.</jats:p>
title: The Lead Tip Beyond the Myocardial Contour: A Narrative Review of Cardiac Implantable Electronic-Device Perforation Detected by Computed Tomography

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) is associated with mortality in Fournier gangrene, but its value beyond albumin remains uncertain. We examined preoperative RAR in patients requiring postoperative intensive care and compared its performance with its components. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 105 adults admitted to intensive care after their first debridement (January 2024–January 2026). RAR was calculated from operative-day preoperative measurements. Logistic regression adjusted for American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status. Firth regression, covariate sensitivity analyses, paired discrimination comparisons and bootstrap internal validation were performed. Results: Twenty-five patients (23.8%) died during hospitalization. Median RAR was 8.30 (interquartile range 6.74–10.21) in nonsurvivors and 5.04 (4.17–6.19) in survivors. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.888 for RAR, 0.839 for albumin and 0.799 for red cell distribution width. The adjusted odds ratio per one-unit RAR increase was 1.77 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.32–2.39); for ASA IV–V versus II–III, it was 10.98 (2.63–45.74). The ASA–RAR model had an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.914 (approximate 95% CI 0.836–0.971) and calibration slope of 0.962. Its corrected AUC difference from ASA plus albumin was 0.015 (−0.019 to 0.045). Conclusions: Higher preoperative RAR was associated with in-hospital mortality independently of ASA physical status. A predictive advantage over ASA plus albumin was not demonstrated. External validation against albumin and established severity scores is required before clinical use.</jats:p>
title: Preoperative Red Cell Distribution Width-to-Albumin Ratio and In-Hospital Mortality in Patients with Fournier Gangrene Requiring Postoperative Intensive Care: A Retrospective Cohort Study

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise for acute cervical spine fracture (CSFx) detection, but its performance across diverse computed tomography (CT) protocols in unselected emergency workflows requires validation. This study evaluated an AI application on dedicated non-contrast cervical spine CTs and conducted a ‘stress test’ on contrast-enhanced whole-body trauma CTs. Methods: This retrospective study included 724 consecutive adults undergoing cervical spine or whole-body CT at a Level I trauma center (November 2023–February 2025). Disagreements with retrospective review defaulted to the original senior-validated clinical report, reflecting agreement with routine practice rather than an independent expert consensus. Results: Overall, 79/724 patients had acute CSFx (10.9% prevalence), including 54/627 (8.6%) imaged for acute initial trauma. On non-contrast CTs (n = 298), the AI achieved 88.0% sensitivity (95% CI: 76.2–94.4), 88.3% specificity, 60.3% positive predictive value (PPV), and 97.3% negative predictive value (NPV); in the acute-initial-trauma non-contrast subgroup (n = 204), sensitivity was 80.0% (20/25; 95% CI: 60.9–91.1). On contrast-enhanced CTs (n = 426), sensitivity was 86.2%, whereas specificity was lower (75.1%), associated with arterial opacification artifacts and protocol-group differences. Exact vertebral level localization was achieved in 60/69 (87.0%) detected positive examinations and 60/79 (75.9%) fracture-positive examinations. Conclusions: Evaluated for agreement with routine senior-validated clinical reports, the AI showed high sensitivity and NPV in an unselected cohort, suggesting potential triage utility, though acute-initial-trauma non-contrast sensitivity was lower (80.0%) and workflow impact remains unmeasured. Arterial-phase acquisitions were associated with higher false-positive rates, warranting protocol-aware interpretation.</jats:p>
title: Real-World Clinical Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Application for Acute Cervical Spine Fracture Detection on CT

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (HT) is associated with autoimmune inflammation. We investigated serum IL-1β and IL-8 concentrations in relation to routine systemic inflammatory markers and explored their discriminatory performance. Methods: This single-center, cross-sectional case–control study included 212 participants (109 patients with HT and 103 healthy controls), all recruited during the same study period. The primary analytical cohort comprised 205 participants (102 patients with HT and 103 controls) with available hematological measurements. Additional analyses were conducted using analysis-specific sample sizes according to data availability. Serum cytokines were measured using sandwich ELISA. Spearman correlations, covariate-adjusted regression and exploratory ROC analyses were performed. Results: In the primary analytical cohort (n = 205), serum IL-1β (86.26 ± 27.63 vs. 40.04 ± 19.34 pg/mL) and IL-8 (112.18 ± 30.30 vs. 50.19 ± 29.49 pg/mL) concentrations were significantly higher in patients with HT than in healthy controls (both p < 0.001). The absolute cytokine concentrations were higher than those typically reported and may partly reflect assay-specific characteristics. CRP, WBC count, platelet count, and MPV showed no significant between-group differences. Neither cytokine showed consistent correlations with these conventional inflammatory parameters within the HT group. Age-, BMI-, and sex-adjusted geometric mean ratios were 2.267 (95% CI, 2.032–2.530) for IL-1β and 2.445 (95% CI, 2.209–2.706) for IL-8 (n = 208). The combined cytokine model yielded an exploratory five-fold internally cross-validated AUC of 0.934 for distinguishing patients with HT from healthy controls; however, this case–control estimate does not establish clinically validated diagnostic performance. Conclusions: Serum IL-1β and IL-8 concentrations were elevated in patients with HT despite largely unchanged conventional systemic inflammatory parameters. The clinical utility of these cytokines remains unestablished, and further investigations in clinically relevant populations with independent external validation is warranted.</jats:p>
title: Circulating IL-1β and IL-8 in Hashimoto’s Thyroiditis: Systemic Inflammatory Profiles and Exploratory Case–Control Discrimination

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Depressive disorders contribute substantially to global nonfatal health loss, and electroencephalography (EEG) combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been investigated for depression detection. This scoping review mapped EEG-based AI approaches and evidence gaps. Methods: The included evidence was identified through searches of nine selected electronic information sources conducted in April 2026 for publications from 2000–2025; eligibility was restricted to English-language original journal articles and full conference papers. The review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Publications were charted and synthesized descriptively. Results: Of 48,706 records identified through these sources, 273 publications were included. The number of included publications increased from 2020 onward. Resting-state EEG, particularly eyes-closed recordings, predominated; spectral, connectivity, nonlinear, signal-level, and time–frequency representations were common. Among the mutually exclusive dominant-model categories, classical machine learning was the most frequently identified category (99/273, 36.26%), while the four deep-learning-centered categories accounted for 131 publications (47.99%). Most publications involved 100 or fewer participants (189/273, 69.23%) and binary case–control tasks (256/273, 93.77%). Participant-isolated evaluation was explicitly reported in 124 publications (45.42%); external, cross-center, or cross-dataset evaluation in seven (2.56%); identifiable study-specific code resources in 17 (6.23%); and explicit model explanation or attribution in 31 (11.36%). Conclusions: Heterogeneous protocols, limited independent validation, recurring dataset reuse, and incomplete computational transparency constrain reproducibility and clinical generalizability. The included evidence does not support standalone clinical diagnostic use; a potential adjunctive role requires prospective validation and demonstrated clinical utility.</jats:p>
title: Artificial Intelligence Approaches to EEG-Based Depression Detection: A Scoping Review

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: We assessed treatment associations, exploratory biomarker pathways, and interpretable prediction of recorded 28-day COVID-19 mortality after auditing outcome and treatment chronology. Methods: The source cohort yielded 2277 eligible adults. Complete post-discharge vital-status ascertainment was unverified. Treatment comparisons used an end-of-day-2 landmark, initiation on admission days 0–1, ten clinical covariates, and a calendar spline. Selected-cohort mediator models used laboratory measurements on days 2–3. Twenty predictive mean matching imputations addressed missing retained variables. Five model families underwent internal validation; regularized linear discriminant analysis (RLDA) additionally underwent repeated five-fold validation. Post hoc sex, age, and intersectional subgroup analyses applied ISO/IEC TR 24027:2021 definitions. Results: There were 390 recorded deaths (17.1%). In 2125 treatment-landmark patients, spline-adjusted risk differences were −0.002 (95% CI −0.057 to 0.053) for remdesivir, −0.009 (−0.069 to 0.051) for tocilizumab, and 0.036 (−0.005 to 0.076) for corticosteroids. The strict mediator cohort contained 235 patients; sparse early-treatment groups and window sensitivity limited interpretation. Repeated-validation non-SMOTE RLDA achieved AUC 0.841 (95% CI 0.821–0.859) and Brier score 0.112. At the illustrative 0.20 threshold, subgroup assessment detected sex differences in equalized odds for RLDA (adjusted p < 0.001) and TabNet (p = 0.024), with age disparities in all four criteria (both models, adjusted p < 0.001). Conclusions: Treatment associations did not establish benefit or harm, and selected-cohort decompositions did not identify biological mediation. ISO-informed assessment revealed threshold-dependent disparities. Complete outcome ascertainment, external evaluation, and clinically justified operating thresholds are needed before application.</jats:p>
title: A Causal AI Framework for Treatment Associations, Exploratory Mediation, and Interpretable Prediction of Recorded 28-Day Mortality in COVID-19

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Sorption‐based water capture and release in atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) materials are governed by the binding state of confined water. However, salt‐containing sorbents, such as LiCl, usually suffer from strong ion‐water interactions, leading to energetically demanding water release. Herein, a hierarchical wood/metal‐organic framework (MOF) /chitosan hygroscopic material is proposed to regulate confined ion‐water interactions through dual‐confined electron‐density shielding. The MOF provides coordination sites for near‐field polarization around Li
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    , while the chitosan network supplies outer‐shell electron‐density compensation and restricts ion mobility. The results show that this hierarchical electronic microenvironment redistributes electron density around Li
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    , weakens localized ion‐water interactions, and alters the hydrogen‐bonding dynamics of confined water. The material achieves a moisture sorption of 1.78 g g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    and releases 97.2% of captured water at 50°C, with a desorption enthalpy of 1270.5 J g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    . This work establishes electron‐density shielding as a materials design principle for regulating confined hydration, enabling fast and low‐energy water release for sustainable AWH.

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background and Aims: As intestinal ultrasound (IUS) is increasingly used to monitor ulcerative colitis (UC), standardized activity scores are recommended. The Milan Ultrasound Criteria (MUC) and the International Bowel Ultrasound Segmental Activity Score (IBUS-SAS) are promising tools, but their comparative performance remains unclear. This study aimed to compare their diagnostic accuracy and define optimal cut-off values for detecting active disease. Methods: In this prospective study, adults with left-sided or extensive ulcerative colitis (UC) undergoing intestinal ultrasound (IUS) were evaluated. Disease activity was assessed clinically (Patient-Reported Outcome 2, PRO-2), biochemically (C-reactive protein, CRP; fecal calprotectin FC), and endoscopically (Mayo endoscopic subscore, MES). Correlations were analyzed with Spearman’s coefficient, and diagnostic accuracy with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis to define optimal cut-offs. Results: A total of 87 patients underwent 297 IUS examinations. IBUS-SAS and MUC were strongly correlated (ρ = 0.82; p < 0.01) and significantly associated with clinical, endoscopic, and biochemical disease activity. Correlations with PRO-2 and MES were moderate, while weaker associations were observed with inflammatory biomarkers. ROC curves showed comparable accuracy for detecting clinical and endoscopic activity (AUC 0.758–0.790). Optimal cut-offs for active disease (MES ≥ 2) were MUC ≥ 7.88 and IBUS-SAS ≥ 25.0. Cut-offs for severe disease (MES = 3) were also identified (MUC ≥ 8.40 and IBUS-SAS ≥ 49.2). MUC had a higher AUC for detecting biochemical activity based on FC (AUC 0.730 vs. 0.652; p = 0.015). Conclusions: MUC and IBUS-SAS were strongly correlated and showed similar diagnostic performance in UC, with MUC possibly reflecting biochemical activity better, suggesting a possible role of the two scores in IUS monitoring.</jats:p>
title: Ultrasound Activity Scores in Ulcerative Colitis: Comparison Between the International Bowel Ultrasound Segmental Activity Score (IBUS-SAS) and Milan Ultrasound Criteria (MUC)

items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Secondary neutron fields generated by high-energy proton–target interactions constitute one of the major radiation components that must be considered in the design of shielding systems for accelerator facilities. In this study, the multidirectional transport of secondary neutrons produced by the interaction of 1000 MeV protons with a copper target, together with the associated spatial attenuation characteristics of ambient dose equivalent H*(10), was investigated within a tunnel-type accelerator geometry. The shielding geometry comprised concrete side walls modeled as successive layers, a monolithic concrete base block, and a surrounding soil region, enabling neutron transport to be evaluated in both the horizontal and vertical directions. A dataset consisting of 1158 spatial data points was generated from high-fidelity ambient dose equivalent H*(10) distributions calculated using FLUKA Monte Carlo (MC) simulations and was subsequently employed to develop regression-based machine learning (ML) surrogate models. For the ML analysis, spatial distance along the investigated horizontal and vertical directions was used as the predictor variable, while the corresponding FLUKA-calculated H*(10) value was used as the target variable. The ETR, RF, GBR, HGBR, and KNN algorithms were trained and evaluated using a 10-fold cross-validation procedure. All models reproduced the FLUKA-derived H*(10) distributions with high predictive accuracy (R² &gt; 0.98), with the most stable predictive performance achieved by the tree-based ensemble models.The FLUKA results demonstrated a distance-dependent reduction in ambient dose equivalent H*(10) across the modeled concrete shielding regions and revealed pronounced directional variations in neutron transport within the investigated concrete-soil geometry. Since the adjacent concrete layers were defined with identical elemental composition and density, the calculated attenuation behavior was not interpreted as arising from an additional physical scattering mechanism associated with the boundaries between these layers. Furthermore, because a controlled comparison with a monolithic concrete reference configuration having identical total thickness and material properties was not performed, no inference was made regarding superior shielding performance of the layered geometry relative to monolithic concrete. Accordingly, the present results characterize the multidirectional neutron transport and H*(10) distributions of the investigated concrete-soil shielding geometry under 1000 MeV proton irradiation conditions. The findings demonstrate that integrating MC simulations with ML-based surrogate modeling provides a practical and computationally efficient approach for rapid H*(10) prediction and shielding assessment within the investigated fixed irradiation and shielding configuration.</jats:p>
title: Monte Carlo and Machine Learning Analysis of Multidirectional Neutron Shielding in Layered Concrete Accelerator Tunnels over a Soil-Embedded Concrete Base

<jats:p>Subject. Early diagnostics of structural changes in financial, economic, and managerial systems based on weak signal analysis.
Objectives. To develop a phase-based approach to assessing the sustainability of organizations, enabling the identification of pre-crisis states before they manifest in financial and market indicators.
Methods. A synthesis of methods of systems and morphological analysis, the provisions of nonlinear dynamics, and the concept of weak signals is used.
Results. It is shown that financial sustainability is determined by the configuration of internal and external ties, whereas traditional indicators reflect delayed effects of structural changes. It is substantiated that weak signals capture early shifts in the architecture of interactions and precede the deterioration of financial metrics. A phase model is proposed that interprets the development of
a system as a sequence of stable configurations, and the Fibonacci sequence as an analytical scale of structural thresholds and saturation levels. It is shown that structural dynamics can develop while the statistical stability of indicators is preserved. 
Conclusions and Relevance. The phase-based approach enables a shift from the ex post detection of deviations to the identification of structural preconditions for crisis, reduces the lag of managerial responses, and lays the foundation for anticipatory management. The results are applicable to tasks of financial sustainability diagnostics, risk management, analysis of corporate dynamics, and the development of decision support systems.</jats:p>
title: Development of weak signal methodology: Phase diagnostics of changes in management systems

<jats:p>
                    Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging arthropod-borne virus causing Oropouche fever. OROV is transmitted predominantly by the biting midge
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">Culicoides paraensis</jats:italic>
                    . Although historically confined to South America, imported cases have been reported, highlighting its expanding geographic range and global public health relevance. Currently, there are no commercially available diagnostic assays for laboratory confirmation of OROV infection. In addition, no specific antiviral therapy or licensed vaccine is available. The recent emergence of cases outside traditional endemic areas further emphasizes the urgent need to address critical knowledge gaps. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on OROV virology, transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum and diagnostic challenges. We further contextualize OROV within the Indian setting, where competent Culicoides vectors are present, and discuss the importance of incorporating OROV into targeted surveillance and travel-related screening frameworks to facilitate early detection, reduce diagnostic misclassification and strengthen one-health preparedness in regions currently considered non-endemic
                  </jats:p>
title: Oropouche fever in a changing tropical world: emergence, diagnostics and surveillance preparedness for India

<jats:p>Subject. This article discusses the organizational and methodological approaches for diagnosing the economic safety state of nuclear industry construction organizations. 
Objectives. The study aims to develop methodological approaches for diagnosing the state of economic security, taking into account industry specifics in the field of nuclear power plant construction.
Methods. For the study, I used the methods of systems approach, theoretical analysis and classification, as well as structural analysis.
Results. The article reveals the limitations of traditional approaches for diagnosing the economic safety of the nuclear industry, and outlines five key features that determine the specifics of the nuclear power plants construction.
It also develops an author's system of indicators to offset the existing limitations in traditional approaches, proposes calculation formulas and thresholds.
Conclusions. The proposed author's indicators make it possible to take into account industry-specific features and improve the efficiency of diagnosing the state of economic security. The research results can be helpful for the economic safety departments of construction organizations in the nuclear industry.</jats:p>
title: Features of the economic safety diagnostics state of nuclear industry construction organizations

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Cholesteatoma is a benign but locally destructive lesion of the middle ear that can cause hearing loss and serious complications. Patients with middle ear effusion requiring ventilation tube insertion (VTI) may have more persistent or severe middle ear disease than those managed without surgery. Chronic otitis media with effusion and repeated ventilation tube insertion have both been linked to cholesteatoma, yet large-scale evidence on cholesteatoma risk stratification among patients with middle ear effusion—including those who subsequently undergo VTI—remains limited. Nationwide longitudinal claims data from Taiwan provide an opportunity to examine the association between subsequent VTI and recorded cholesteatoma among adults with middle ear effusion. Methods: Taiwan’s Longitudinal Health Insurance Research Database (2000–2021), comprising two million beneficiaries sampled from National Health Insurance enrollees, was used in this retrospective cohort study. Adults with newly diagnosed middle ear effusion in 2001–2014 who subsequently underwent VTI were matched 1:1 by age, sex, index year, and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) score with adults who did not undergo VTI during follow-up. Follow-up continued through December 2021. A multivariable Cox model treated VTI as a time-dependent exposure. Cholesteatoma was identified using a repeated outpatient diagnostic claim definition. Baseline-variable rankings were explored with four machine learning algorithms (logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost) using a SHAP-based averaged-importance score, and their stability was compared between 1:1 and 1:10 matching. Results: Among 1812 matched adults (mean follow-up, 13.24 ± 5.16 years), 55 met the claims-based cholesteatoma definition: 38 in the VTI group and 17 in the non-VTI group. Time-updated VTI was associated with a higher hazard of subsequently recorded cholesteatoma (adjusted hazard ratio, 4.54; 95% confidence interval, 2.47–8.34). In the exploratory SHAP-based ranking, benzodiazepine use, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug use, allergic rhinitis, and antihistamine use ranked within the top five at both matching ratios, and rankings showed moderate-to-high concordance between 1:1 and 1:10 matching (Kendall’s τ-b, 0.72–0.74 for N = 10). Conclusions: In this matched cohort of adults with middle ear effusion, VTI was observationally associated with a higher hazard of subsequently recorded cholesteatoma. Residual confounding by indication, selection based on future VTI status, and closer otologic surveillance limit interpretation. The data cannot distinguish VTI as a marker of disease severity from VTI as a possible contributor to cholesteatoma.</jats:p>
title: Association Between Ventilation Tube Insertion and Subsequent Cholesteatoma in Adults with Middle Ear Effusion: A Nationwide Observational Cohort Study

<jats:p>Subject. Diagnostics of the sustainable development of industrial enterprises as the primary level of monitoring of the regional economy.
Objectives. To propose and test a two-block methodology for diagnosing the sustainable development of industrial enterprises, to substantiate its calculated parameters – the weights of indicators, threshold criteria for scoring and the scale of interpretation of the integral index, to determine the possibilities of applying aggregated results in regional industrial monitoring.
Methods. The research is based on system, process, resource, and risk-based approaches. The assessment was based on fixed documentary criteria, normalization, calculation of partial and integral indices, and sensitivity analysis. Equal weights of indicators and blocks are accepted in accordance with the principle of insufficient foundation.
Results. A methodology is proposed that combines eight organizational and eight economic indicators, partial, integral and aggregated indexes, and eight analytical contours. The zone of permissible deviation ±5% when converting indicators into points and a five-level equal-interval scale of interpretation of the integral index are substantiated. The methodology is applicable to assess the sustainable development of enterprises, their cross–industry comparison and identification of risk areas, and the diagnostic results are used to justify management decisions and targeted measures of regional industrial policy.
Conclusions. A joint review of organizational and economic indicators makes it possible to determine which factors contribute to the sustainability of each enterprise. Even with similar values of the integral index, enterprises differ in the composition and severity of the identified limitations. The aggregated index characterizes only the surveyed population and is not an assessment of the entire industrial complex of the region.</jats:p>
title: Diagnostics of the sustainable development of industrial enterprises in the monitoring system of the regional economy

items.abstract: <jats:p>Off-vehicle traction battery storage and diagnostics motivate the assessment of supervisory gas reporting. This retrospective study uses three non-rail system experiments and eight synthetic-effluent tests; its 9324 method-specific records are deterministic phase configurations, not independent trials. Exact-timestamp archive snapshots and interval maxima were compared in 5, 10, 30, and 60 s intervals. In the system series, snapshot-window-level reporting decreases from 91.67% to 42.71% over the specified near-smoke window. At 60 s, 399/1440 first opportunities lack an exact finite observation, reflecting timestamp gaps and channel blanks rather than packet loss. Interval maxima retained all supported exceedances by construction, yet only 18.33% of system configurations met a hypothetical 10 s added-wait target. Supplementary checks show sensitivity to threshold, window length, and register-hold assumptions: a 1 s hold increases the 60 s system snapshot result to 49.17%, while full-record evaluation increases window-level reporting to 100%. An ideal threshold-event baseline removes scheduled wait, without modeling transport delay. The engineering contribution is an auditable separation of archived exceedance visibility, source age, and supervisory latency, supporting conditional interface design rules. Numerical proportions and setpoints require railway-site validation before operational use, including in China.</jats:p>
title: Gas Monitoring Reporting Latency for Railway Traction Battery Storage and Diagnostics

<jats:p>The radiative flux behaviour associated with spectral absorption in RR Lyrae atmospheres remains poorly characterised.
We investigate phase-dependent flux integrals for the Hα and Fe ii ,łambda4923.921 lines in the RRc star MT,Tel and explore their potential as diagnostics of depth-dependent atmospheric dynamics and radiative-kinematic coupling.
Using HARPS spectra, we derived three heliocentric radial-velocity estimates and constructed Planck-based and velocity-based flux integrals. We examined their phase variations and Van Hoof-like relations, estimated the uncertainties through Monte Carlo propagation, and tested the sensitivity of the results to the adopted temperature curve and Fourier representation. An approximate photon-number correction was applied to the velocity-based estimates.
The radial-velocity and uncorrected flux-integral diagrams show asynchronous, depth-dependent behaviour between Hα and Fe ii , including distorted and self-intersecting loops. The phase-coloured points show similar crossing tendencies near the Fourier-fitted self-intersections, providing qualitative support for these features. The photon-number correction brings the velocity-based and Planck-based estimates to comparable scales, while the three corrected estimates nearly overlap. Their residual phase-dependent discrepancy, quantified by r_ dy = / , shows line-dependent structure broadly associated with the corresponding atmospheric acceleration features. F_ th F_ dy,co
The uncorrected loop topology reveals asynchronous behaviour consistent with nonlinear depth-dependent atmospheric motion, while the corrected r_ dy diagnostic highlights line-dependent radiative-kinematic coupling. Considered alongside independent indicators of shock-related dynamics, these diagnostics offer a complementary approach to probing the stratified dynamics of RR Lyrae atmospheres. Detailed non-local thermodynamic equilibrium radiative-transfer modelling and larger RR Lyrae samples will further establish its broader applicability.</jats:p>
title: Phase-dependent radiative flux integrals and Van Hoof-like diagnostics in the RRc star MT Tel

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: We examined the association between tumor abnormal protein (TAP) and gastrointestinal pathological status in a symptomatic surgical population. Methods: This retrospective single-center study assessed 485 patients tested in 2024 without requiring matched general laboratory measurements. The principal analysis included 259 patients: 63 with malignant and 196 with nonmalignant pathology. Pathology ascertainment extended into 2025 using a 90-day post-TAP window adopted during revision. Analyses used the fixed institutional threshold of 121 µm2 and included age-and-sex adjustment, bootstrap optimism correction, exploratory chronological assessment, and selection weighting. Results: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.775 (95% CI 0.713–0.834). Sensitivity was 82.5% and specificity 64.3%, with 11 false negatives and 70 false positives. Against 70 benign neoplasms, polyps, or adenomas, AUC was 0.716. Adding TAP increased apparent model AUC from 0.715 to 0.790; the paired fixed-score difference was 0.075 (95% CI 0.024–0.125), and optimism-corrected AUC was 0.780. Later-period model AUCs ranged from 0.677 to 0.728; selection-weighted AUC was 0.775. Conclusions: TAP showed modest discrimination with substantial overlap between malignant and nonmalignant disease. Incremental discrimination did not establish clinical utility. Incomplete diagnostic and treatment histories and selective reference availability restrict interpretation to association with pathological status, rather than accuracy in an untreated, previously undiagnosed population. Independent prospective evaluation is required.</jats:p>
title: Association Between Peripheral-Blood Tumor Abnormal Protein and Gastrointestinal Pathological Status: A Retrospective Single-Center Study

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Electronic textiles capable of delivering metallic‐level conductivity while preserving mechanical durability and breathable comfort remain a longstanding challenge, as conductive coatings block textile pores and suffer from poor interfacial stability under deformation. Here we present a hierarchical liquid metal–MXene interfacial architecture that resolves this conductivity–durability–breathability trade‐off in conductive fabrics. The strategy constructs a conformal fiber‐level conductive network by electrostatically anchoring MXene nanosheets onto cationic‐modified cotton fibers followed by the deposition and mechanical activation of liquid metal nanoparticles. Strong interfacial coordination (Ti–O→Ga3+) between MXene and liquid metal enables efficient charge transport and robust interlayer coupling, while a hydrophobic encapsulation preserves stability without compromising the porosity of the textile. As a result, the fabric exhibits a high conductivity of 2.9 × 104 S m–1, outstanding electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness of 81 dB in the X‐band and equally impressive shielding performance over broadband frequency range, together with high air and moisture permeability. The textile demonstrates excellent durability under repeated deformation, washing, and environmental exposure, along with multifunctional capabilities including infrared camouflage and low‐voltage Joule heating. This work establishes a general interfacial design principle for constructing high‐performance electronic textiles and provides a potentially scalable pathway for continuous production of multifunctional wearable electronic systems.</jats:p>
title: A Hierarchical Interfacial Engineering Strategy Achieves High Electrical Conductivity, Durable Shielding, and Wearable Comfort in a Multifunctional Fabric

                  <jats:p>
                    One of the main sources of the electromagnetic pollution is electromagnetic interference (EMI) that lowers the behavior of the electronic equipment and communication systems. Therefore, the present study investigates the influence of nickel-phosphorous (NiP) graphene-coated fiber layer architecture and composite thickness on the dielectric properties and EMI shielding effectiveness (SE) of ramie fiber–reinforced polymer composites. Chemically treated and NiP–graphene-coated ramie fiber was used for fabricating composites having one, two, and three coated fiber layers. Compression molding technique was adopted to fabricate the composites with varying numbers of coated fiber layers (1–3 layers). The dielectric constant and losses were evaluated between the frequency range 50 Hz and 1 MHz. Results showed that the composites with a single coated fiber layer had the maximum dielectric constant (3.9 at 50 Hz and 35 °C), which decreases with increase in frequency because of the Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars polarization. The EMI SE of the fabricated composites was measured through a vector network analyzer (8–12 GHz). Electrical conductivity of the coated fiber layer was found to be 15.5 (Ω cm)
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    whereas SE of the developed composites increased from 25 dB for CNFC-1 to 27.5 dB for CNFC-2 and 31.5 dB for CNFC-3. Thus, the findings of the present study suggested that incorporation of NiP/graphene-coated ramie fiber layer significantly improved EMI SE of the composite, whereas dielectric behavior depends upon coated fiber layer architecture and composite thickness, making them suitable for EMI shielding and dielectric applications.
                  </jats:p>
title: Influence of NiP graphene-coated fiber layers and composite thickness on the dielectric and electromagnetic shielding characteristics of ramie fiber–reinforced polymer composites

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Regulatory processes for medicines and diagnostics can be lengthy and time-consuming, causing delays for effective access at the patient level. In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), this is particularly pressing due to constrained regulatory capacities which result in decision-making timelines varying widely. Additionally, cancer medicines and diagnostics often require specialized assessment, including bioequivalence, comparability and risk evaluation, which can further delay access. Reliance mechanisms can help address these challenges by allowing national regulatory authorities to leverage decisions or assessments by trusted authorities and by enabling work-sharing across agencies, enabling faster access for patients. This review outlines reliance procedures that can be used to improve access to cancer medicines and diagnostics within LMICs targeted by the Access to Oncology Medicines Coalition. We reviewed regulatory authorities’ websites to assess the relevance and utility of reliance mechanisms in the context of cancer technologies and LMIC settings and complemented our findings with a consultation exercise for completeness. We also present a guiding framework to help companies and regulators identify appropriate reliance pathways. We highlight that reliance practices offer practical opportunities to accelerate access to cancer medicines and diagnostics in LMICs.</jats:p>
title: Breaking Barriers: A Call to Leverage Regulatory Reliance for Cancer Medicines and Diagnostics

items.abstract: <jats:p>Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is caused by excessive parathyroid hormone (PTH) secretion, typically due to a solitary adenoma, while multiglandular adenomas, supernumerary glands, and ectopic locations are rare and pose significant diagnostic and surgical challenges. We report a 36-year-old female presenting with recurrent bilateral nephrolithiasis, pathological fractures, gastrointestinal symptoms, hypercalcaemia, raised PTH, hypophosphatemia, elevated serum prolactin, and a pancreatic lesion. Although ultrasonography suggested bilateral inferior adenomas and Tc-99m sestamibi single photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) revealed multiple tracer-avid lesions in the neck and mediastinum, intraoperative findings during bilateral neck exploration and transcervical thymectomy confirmed multiglandular disease involving five adenomas, including an ectopic thymic parathyroid gland. This rare presentation highlights that while hybrid SPECT/CT improves localisation, multiglandular and ectopic disease significantly reduces conventional imaging sensitivity, making comprehensive surgical exploration essential for achieving successful outcomes in complex PHPT cases.</jats:p>
title: Ectopic Supernumerary Parathyroid Adenomas: Diagnostic Dilemma and Surgical Management Challenge

items.abstract: <jats:p>Configuring a diagnostic before the next shot is an instrumentation problem that grows in importance as high-repetition-rate laser-plasma platforms scale from tens of shots to thousands. In the present campaign, a gated intensified optical camera required shot-to-shot retuning as peak image brightness varied with chamber pressure, laser energy, focus conditions, and target state. Static settings produced under-exposed or over-driven images, while manual tuning consumed shots and reduced measurement efficiency. We treat this problem as machine-learning-guided pre-shot diagnostic configuration using a hybrid framework: archived images and machine variables are reduced to a compact descriptor state, a neural-network surrogate is trained to predict that state from operating conditions and detector settings, and Bayesian optimization inverts the surrogate to recommend executable settings before each shot. On a 1 Hz multi-joule platform, the measured peak signal tracked requested targets from 1000 to 4500 counts with a correlation of 0.92 and a mean absolute error of 15%. These results demonstrate that campaign data can train practical empirical models supporting pre-shot diagnostic configuration for enhanced data quality and experimental efficiency in comparable laser-plasma campaigns.</jats:p>
title: Machine-learning-guided pre-shot diagnostic configuration for high-repetition-rate laser-plasma experiments

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed, back-spliced transcripts with high stability that have been proposed as minimally invasive cancer biomarkers, yet their diagnostic performance across gynaecological malignancies has not been synthesized in an up-to-date review that draws on both English- and Chinese-language databases.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We searched seven databases from inception to 26 September 2026 without language restriction. Human studies that evaluated one or more circRNAs for the detection of cervical, ovarian, or endometrial malignancy against healthy, benign, adjacent-normal, or intraepithelial-disease comparators were eligible, with histopathology as the reference standard. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled jointly with a bivariate binomial-normal random-effects model; studies comparing individuals with and without malignancy (patient-level detection) were analysed separately from studies contrasting tumour with adjacent-normal or benign tissue (tissue-level discrimination), and an overall estimate was retained only as an exploratory summary; risk of bias and certainty were appraised with Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (QUADAS-2) and Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) for diagnostic tests.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Of 1,544 records (914 unique), 29 studies entered qualitative synthesis and 16 independent contrasts (1,141 case and 1,157 control observations, from approximately 1,943 unique individuals) entered meta-analysis; these observations include paired tumour and adjacent-normal specimens and do not represent 2,298 independent participants. Overall pooled sensitivity was 0.84 (95% CI 0.78-0.88) and specificity 0.86 (95% CI 0.82-0.90), with a positive likelihood ratio of 6.20 (4.50-8.53), a negative likelihood ratio of 0.19 (0.14-0.25), and a diagnostic odds ratio of 33.1 (19.8-55.4); a summary receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was derived from the fitted bivariate model. Patient-level detection (10 contrasts) gave sensitivity 0.87 (0.80-0.91) and specificity 0.89 (0.81-0.93), and tissue-level discrimination (6 contrasts) gave sensitivity 0.85 (0.80-0.89) and specificity 0.85 (0.77-0.90). Between-study heterogeneity was substantial and prediction intervals were wide (sensitivity 0.58-0.95; specificity 0.68-0.95). Central estimates were directionally stable across sensitivity analyses. A Deeks asymmetry test was not statistically significant (P = 0.74) but was underpowered. Every study carried high risk of bias for patient selection and index-test interpretation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CircRNAs show promising but very-low-certainty exploratory discrimination for cervical and ovarian cancer. Only a minority of studies used benign or pre-malignant comparators. Prospective, preregistered, multicentre studies that use intended-use populations, prespecified thresholds, and external validation are required before any clinical application.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Diagnostic performance of circular RNAs for detecting gynaecological malignancies: a systematic review and bivariate meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec id="j_dx-2026-0166_abs_001">
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To trace how a suspected but unexamined surgical complication propagated through non-disclosure, anchoring, and fragmented care into months of diagnostic delay, unresolved illness, and lasting harm.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_dx-2026-0166_abs_002">
                    <jats:title>Case presentation</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A 23-year-old woman developed persistent clear nasal drainage after elective functional endoscopic sinus surgery and asked her surgeon whether it was a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak. Beta-2 transferrin was never ordered. The complication was never confirmed or excluded. In March of her first year of medical school, at 24, she became acutely ill. An early lumbar puncture was reported to her as viral meningitis and not investigated further. That record is lost, and the only surviving lumbar puncture was essentially normal. Over many months she cycled through various emergency departments, dismissed as drug-seeking and a frequent flier, then was committed to a psychiatric unit. She had seizures before receiving intravenous treatment for presumed Lyme meningitis and for toxoplasmosis supported by elevated Toxoplasma IgM and IgG. Medical school ended. Cognitive impairment and fatigue persist 20 years later.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_dx-2026-0166_abs_003">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The failure was not one missed clue but a cascade in which each error made the next more likely: a suspected leak became an incomplete history, then a confident but incorrect psychiatric closure. Two mechanisms stand out: a private workup withheld from the treating team, and an illness that corrupted the patient’s symptom reporting and generated false histories clinicians anchored upon, even as her core account, that her illness was organic, stayed correct. Disclosure, ownership of the whole picture, and repeated reassessment can interrupt such a cascade.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Conservative management: diagnostic error after suspected CSF leak

items.abstract: <jats:p>Recently, multi-view clustering methods based on deep matrix factorization have exhibited significant promise in learning hierarchical semantic representations. However, three critical limitations remain in existing approaches. First, due to the independent intra-view hierarchical decomposition, these methods rely on pairwise view correlations, thereby failing to capture high-order consistency. Second, the complementary information embedded in intermediate layers remains under-utilized. Third, they are susceptible to sensor noise and feature redundancy, which degrades the quality of learned representations. To address these limitations, this paper presents a novel approach named Noise-Aware Hierarchical Tensor Fusion (NAHTF). The proposed NAHTF integrates tensor dictionary learning with deep semi-nonnegative tensor decomposition, leveraging the tensor t-product to facilitate cross-view and cross-layer information fusion of multi-view data. Specifically, a noise-aware tensor dictionary learning module is designed to construct a robust tensor representation by combining Schatten p-norm-based low-rank tensor recovery for capturing high-order correlations and l2,1-norm-based sparse noise modeling for suppressing adverse components. A deep semi-nonnegative tensor factorization module is then employed to hierarchically decompose the refined tensor representation using the tensor t-product, which facilitates the propagation of complementary information across all decomposition layers and thereby fully exploits both inter-view consistency and intra-view diversity. Moreover, a joint optimization framework is developed to simultaneously learn the tensor representation and perform deep tensor factorization, avoiding suboptimal representations caused by decoupled processes. Extensive experiments on six benchmark datasets, including text, face, and image data, demonstrate that NAHTF outperforms fourteen state-of-the-art multi-view clustering methods.</jats:p>
title: Noise-Aware Hierarchical Tensor Fusion for Multi-View Clustering

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Materials discovery is cumulative: once a crystal is made, nearby chemistry can inherit clues about precursors, conditions, and competing phases. We quantify structural memory by embedding 167,392 ICSD entries with CrystalWeave and replaying their neighborhoods through publication time. New-community births fall from 33.8% in the 1930s to 1.9% in the 2010s; the decline survives four alternative representations. Growth pulses reveal renaissances in cuprates, manganites, permanent magnets, iron pnictides and borocarbides. Historical CrystalWeave maps place later ICSD structures inside established basins more often than all five computed cohorts. GNoME combines extensive compositional novelty with familiar local Graphlet distributions: only 0.010% of its release matches an ICSD formula, yet 79.6% shares an anonymous stoichiometry. Its basin placement depends on descriptor construction and calibration. In A-Lab, 87.5% of in-basin targets and 42.1% of frontier targets were made. These measures distinguish forms of computational novelty; CrystalWeave basin membership supports a synthesis-relevant prior for triage.</jats:p>
title: Structural memory links experimental discovery and computational novelty

items.abstract: <jats:p>Advancing Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF), particularly Fast Ignition and Shock Ignition, requires a deeper understanding of laser–plasma interactions in extreme regimes that remain difficult to access at large-scale ICF facilities. Long-wave infrared (LWIR) lasers provide a powerful approach, leveraging favorable wavelength scaling to access relativistic plasma physics, enable efficient laser beam channeling, and enhance the generation of hot electrons and energetic ions at significantly reduced laser intensity and plasma density. This capability allows laboratory-scale experiments to reproduce ICF-relevant conditions with improved diagnostic access and greater physical transparency. The Brookhaven National Laboratory Accelerator Test Facility offers a unique platform for such studies, combining a multi-terawatt LWIR laser with synchronized optical diagnostics and accelerator-based probes. This capability enables systematic investigation and optimization of key plasma processes governing ICF performance, thereby supporting the development of practical fusion energy systems.</jats:p>
title: Long wave infrared laser platform for plasma studies relevant to inertial fusion

items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Secondary neutron fields generated by high-energy proton–target interactions constitute one of the major radiation components that must be considered in the design of shielding systems for accelerator facilities. In this study, the multidirectional transport of secondary neutrons produced by the interaction of 1000 MeV protons with a copper target, together with the associated spatial attenuation characteristics of ambient dose equivalent H*(10), was investigated within a tunnel-type accelerator geometry. The shielding geometry comprised concrete side walls modeled as successive layers, a monolithic concrete base block, and a surrounding soil region, enabling neutron transport to be evaluated in both the horizontal and vertical directions. A dataset consisting of 1158 spatial data points was generated from high-fidelity ambient dose equivalent H*(10) distributions calculated using FLUKA Monte Carlo (MC) simulations and was subsequently employed to develop regression-based machine learning (ML) surrogate models. For the ML analysis, spatial distance along the investigated horizontal and vertical directions was used as the predictor variable, while the corresponding FLUKA-calculated H*(10) value was used as the target variable. The ETR, RF, GBR, HGBR, and KNN algorithms were trained and evaluated using a 10-fold cross-validation procedure. All models reproduced the FLUKA-derived H*(10) distributions with high predictive accuracy (R² &gt; 0.98), with the most stable predictive performance achieved by the tree-based ensemble models.The FLUKA results demonstrated a distance-dependent reduction in ambient dose equivalent H*(10) across the modeled concrete shielding regions and revealed pronounced directional variations in neutron transport within the investigated concrete-soil geometry. Since the adjacent concrete layers were defined with identical elemental composition and density, the calculated attenuation behavior was not interpreted as arising from an additional physical scattering mechanism associated with the boundaries between these layers. Furthermore, because a controlled comparison with a monolithic concrete reference configuration having identical total thickness and material properties was not performed, no inference was made regarding superior shielding performance of the layered geometry relative to monolithic concrete. Accordingly, the present results characterize the multidirectional neutron transport and H*(10) distributions of the investigated concrete-soil shielding geometry under 1000 MeV proton irradiation conditions. The findings demonstrate that integrating MC simulations with ML-based surrogate modeling provides a practical and computationally efficient approach for rapid H*(10) prediction and shielding assessment within the investigated fixed irradiation and shielding configuration.</jats:p>
title: Monte Carlo and Machine Learning Analysis of Multidirectional Neutron Shielding in Layered Concrete Accelerator Tunnels over a Soil-Embedded Concrete Base

<jats:title>Abstract:</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Pseudolymphomatous cutaneous angiosarcoma (cAS) is a rare variant of cAS characterized by a dense lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate that can obscure the underlying malignant endothelial proliferation, mimicking inflammatory dermatoses or cutaneous lymphoid neoplasms, creating a major diagnostic pitfall. We describe a new case and review the existing literature on this rare entity.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A 71-year-old man presented with a scaly pruritic eruption that progressed to extensive adherent necrotic plaques with secondary infection. Histological examination revealed a diffuse dermal neoplasm with irregular anastomosing vascular channels accompanied by a dense lymphocytic infiltrate. The diffuse strong expression of endothelial markers (including erythroblast transformation-specific-related gene (ERG)) by the atypical endothelial cells, along with the morphology, confirmed the diagnosis of pseudolymphomatous cAS. The tumor later metastasized to the breast, and the patient died 11 months after the initial diagnosis.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This case underscores the significant clinical and histological diagnostic challenges posed by pseudolymphomatous cAS. It also emphasized that despite its clinically deceptive appearance, this variant may follow an aggressive clinical course with metastatic spread and disease-related death. Recognition of this rare variant requires a high index of suspicion, careful clinicopathologic correlation, and awareness of immunohistochemical pitfalls and limitations.</jats:p>
title: Pseudolymphomatous Cutaneous Angiosarcoma of the Scalp: A Clinicopathological Diagnostic Challenge
